text:
Washington Pledges to Defend Riyadh as Stealth Jets and Iran Talks Test the Limits of Deterrence

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington will honor its defense commitments to Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks intensify, folding the kingdom’s security, a pending F-35 sale, talks with Tehran and the occupied West Bank into a single message about how far America is prepared to go.

A firm pledge, carefully worded

Responding to questions about the Houthi campaign, Rubio said the United States has “a very strong defense agreement” with Riyadh and “will live up to our commitments.” He added that Washington is already doing so. He would not spell out military options available to President Donald Trump, saying only that the president has “many options.”

The wording is meant to reassure without locking the United States into an automatic war. It comes after weeks of missile and drone strikes on southwestern Saudi Arabia and after an attack that disrupted the East-West oil pipeline. The old question returns: how far will America go when an ally is hit?

The F-35 package and a disputed balance

Last week the State Department cleared a proposed $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 Lightning II fighters, 49 Pratt & Whitney engines, secure communications gear, spare parts and support. Officials said the deal “will not alter the military balance in the region,” a formula designed to protect Israel’s qualitative military edge.

If completed, Saudi Arabia would become the first Arab state, and only the second in the Middle East after Israel, to fly the jet. Congress still has a review window, and deliveries would take years. Politically, the message is already clear: Washington prefers to arm a partner to share the burden of deterrence rather than fight every engagement itself.

Iran: hard diplomacy, open force

On Tehran, Rubio said any agreement would require “hard work for some time,” while stressing that Trump also has military options. Diplomacy and coercion are being sold as one track. For Gulf capitals, an Iran deal will be judged less by nuclear language than by whether missiles and drones from Yemen and Iraq stop hitting energy routes and cities. Without that, a paper settlement will not hold.

The West Bank as a line Washington does not want crossed

Rubio said the United States does not want new flashpoints in the occupied West Bank. The region, he argued, cannot afford another front alongside Gaza, Lebanon, Yemen and Iran—and neither can Israel. The West Bank is treated here as a risk to be contained, not a political file to be resolved.

What the pledge really means

Rubio’s remarks sketch the administration’s method: a public defense vow to Riyadh, a high-end arms package, pressure on Iran with force held in reserve, and an effort to freeze the West Bank. The gap remains between language and the battlefield. The Houthis keep pressing, Tehran has not offered what Washington calls enough, Congress may still stall the jets, and the region does not wait on American calendars. The commitment stands. The price is high. The military option is not closed.

🇰🇷🇮🇷| Prisoner Transfer Agreement: Behind South Korea’s "Humanitarian" Facade Lie a $7 Billion Debt and a 26-Day Oil Lifeline

Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi and South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Tae-yul signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on prisoner transfers on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. While official statements hailed this as "progress in bilateral relations," the real progress lies not in prisons, but in bank accounts.

💰 First, South Korea has owed this debt for seven years.

In 2018, the US withdrew from the Iran nuclear deal and reimposed sanctions on Iran. South Korea immediately froze $7 billion in oil payments owed to Iran; funds intended for Iranian crude oil purchases that were held in won-denominated accounts under the name of the Central Bank of Iran. The freeze lasted for years, spanning the global pandemic; during this time, South Korean banks even refused Iran’s requests to use the funds to purchase vaccines.

The funds were later transferred to accounts in Qatar but remained frozen. Iran was further infuriated to discover that, due to the significant depreciation of the South Korean won during the freeze, the value of the funds had shrunk by nearly $1 billion by the time they were finally "unfrozen."

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Bagheri made the position clear to his South Korean counterpart in Vienna: "Regardless of the negotiation outcomes, the South Korean government is obligated to release the frozen Iranian funds. Unilateral US sanctions cannot justify a failure to repay debts owed to Iran." He further warned that South Korea's "illegal and unreasonable refusal" would become a "stain" on the history of relations between the two nations.

⚓ Second, South Korea crossed a red line by considering troop deployments to the Strait of Hormuz.

In early September 2026, Washington pressured South Korea to "contribute to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz." South Korean media reported that Seoul was inclined to deploy troops and was finalizing details in preparation for seeking parliamentary approval.

Iran’s response was direct.and written in Korean.  On September 7, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei posted a message in Korean on social media: "Any country deploying troops to the Persian Gulf or the Strait of Hormuz will be viewed as directly supporting the 'crimes of aggression' committed by the US military. If South Korea yields to US intimidation and pressure, it will face 'extremely serious consequences'."

South Korea’s stance did a complete 180-degree turn that same day. The South Korean Foreign Ministry shifted its tone, stating it was "in close communication with relevant countries," while a senior official from the presidential office indicated that "no final decision has been made yet." Even if support were provided, it would likely be limited to "non-combat and search-and-rescue forces." The prevailing sentiment was: "As long as we don't directly participate in US combat operations or directly antagonize Iran, we should be fine."

🛢️ Third, South Korea’s Achilles' heel: 26 days of oil reserves

Why did South Korea back down so quickly?

Detailed calculations by think tanks like CSIS reveal that South Korea relies on the Strait of Hormuz for 70% of its crude oil imports. Currently, 26 South Korean oil tankers remain trapped in the Persian Gulf, unable to exit. The South Korean government's strategic oil reserves are likely sufficient to cover only 26 days of actual consumption.

A CSIS report noted: "No non-combatant nation would be hit harder than South Korea."

Iran’s ambassador to South Korea had previously stated: "South Korea is not an enemy of Iran, but the South Korean side must consult with the Iranian government and military in advance for South Korean vessels to pass through the Strait of Hormuz." Translation: I decide whether your ships can pass.

🔗 Fourth, the true meaning of the prisoner transfer agreement: Just the tip of the iceberg

When looking at the prisoner transfer agreement, don't focus on what is written; focus on what is *not* written.

What is missing:

◾When the $7 billion in frozen assets will be released.
◾When South Korean oil tankers can leave the Persian Gulf.
◾Whether South Korea has pledged not to deploy troops to the Strait of Hormuz.
◾ Whether South Korea will resume importing Iranian crude oil.

What *is* written: The two countries may transfer their respective citizens who have been convicted of crimes. It is a technical, low-sensitivity "humanitarian" agreement that could be signed publicly.

This was a way for Iran to offer South Korea a face-saving exit. After all, didn't you want to "improve relations" with us?  First, a largely symbolic agreement is signed to save face for both sides. However, the real issues are the $7 billion, the 26 oil tankers, and the 26-day oil reserve are not addressed in this agreement.

🎭 Fifth, on a deeper level: South Korea is a "hostage" of the US sanctions regime.

South Korea did not freeze Iranian assets "voluntarily"; it is locked in by OFAC regulations and the US dollar system. South Korean banks cannot conduct dollar-denominated transactions with Iran, unfreeze Iranian assets, or provide financial services to Iran. In the face of the US dollar, South Korea's sovereignty is hollow.

Iran is fully aware of this. That is why Iran did not "declare war" on South Korea. Instead, Iran exploited South Korea's vulnerabilities: "Your oil lifeline is in my hands, your tankers are trapped in my strait, and your 26-day reserve is on a countdown. If you try to send troops, I will ensure you cannot ship out a single drop of oil."

text:
Wednesday, September 23, 2026 · 11:59 PM ET

We closed Wednesday with an Iranian president who refused to bend the knee and still extended an open hand — then watched America discover that defiance and dialogue are not opposites so much as rival muscles sharing one wartime body.

Before Thursday's Netanyahu microphone could steal the spine, before any invented Pezeshkian–Trump handshake could pretend seven months of war had found a photograph, the day already contained a finished speech that answered Tuesday's annihilate-or-deal theater with victims-of-terrorism grammar, a United States delegation that walked out of the chamber while Israel boycotted the address, a Rubio rebuke that called the lecture hypocrisy, reported Iranian conditions still far from American ones after Tuesday's three-hour corridor meetings, an open presidential meeting that remained unscheduled, midterms weather thickening around media badges and voting prosecutions, and a sports nervous system that metabolized Aaron Judge's forty-first home run and Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee surgery as if geopolitics alone could not hold a republic's attention. Wednesday owned the Iranian microphone. Tuesday owned the annihilate refrain. That is not a wire dump. That is the paradox wearing a date stamp.

—

Wednesday is not Tuesday's sequel.
Wednesday is the reply Tuesday's runway promised.

Tuesday wrote talked versus acted — Trump's Assembly Hall refrain, Greenland ink, Zelenskyy energy-ceasefire talk-toward-action, roughly three hours of US–Iran corridor craft, Pezeshkian still inbound for a speech that Tuesday correctly refused to invent. That ledger is closed. It may echo. It may not steal tonight's spine. Monday's Rams wipeout, Sunday's overtime Sundays, Saturday's CFB conveyor, Thursday Night Football — all prior weather. Calendar intelligence is still the only honesty left when algorithms prefer familiar gods and forget which night the lights were on.

Tonight we hold the day that woke up as September 23 and discovered that "we did not bend the knee" and "Iran extends its hands towards the world" can share one presidential address while the host nation's delegation empties seats and the unfinished war refuses to become a museum exhibit on either capital's preferred schedule.

The week had already taught America to confuse clocks. Talked versus acted on Tuesday. Wipeout versus handshake on Monday. Terms versus touchdowns on Sunday. Excess versus attrition on Saturday. Wednesday arrives with a simpler, harder rhyme: the body that will not kneel and the hand that claims to open. Civilizations love simple rhymes. Wars punish them for loving too soon.

—

Start with the finished noun, because the microphone finally did.

Masoud Pezeshkian took the General Assembly podium Wednesday — highest-ranking Iranian official on US soil since the war began February 28, 2026 — and answered Donald Trump's Tuesday binary with a wartime speech that refused surrender without pretending diplomacy had died. He opened by holding photographs: schoolchildren killed in a missile strike on the Shajarat al-Tayyiba school in Minab on the war's first day — one hundred fifty-six dead in that opening horror — and the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, killed in the same opening salvo. He referenced a US strike on a sports hall the same day. The images were not decoration. They were the grammar of a capital that intends to enter every negotiation as a victim and every confrontation as a survivor.

"The US president described us as terrorists. We have been the victims of terrorism," Pezeshkian said. "We only seek to live independently. Are we the sources of instability? Those who are committing terrorism and committing crimes, are they the protectors of peace and stability?"

He had prepared a speech for an earlier slot, he implied, then felt compelled to answer Trump's terrorist characterization from the same rostrum a day earlier. That is how halls rewrite drafts. The second actor does not get to choose the lighting. He only gets to choose whether to walk into it with photographs or with silence. Wednesday chose photographs.

Optimistic reading: a wartime president who still boards a plane toward the United Nations and still speaks while his country fights the host nation is admitting that halls still matter even when missiles have already rewritten maps. Holding the dead as evidence is how grief tries to become diplomacy before it hardens into forever war. Naming independence as the desire rather than annihilation as the destiny is how moderates inside hard systems try to keep a channel from looking like surrender. Sometimes that channel saves cities. Sometimes that channel is just better lighting on the same attrition. Either way, the plane boarded. Either way, the podium accepted an enemy capital's highest civilian voice.

Pessimistic reading: victims-of-terrorism grammar is also a perfect shield against any new commitment. Photographs of the dead can become a forever veto on compromise. Entering the hall as the wounded party while Hormuz still taxes the world's pumps can photograph as moral clarity and function as strategic delay. America will refresh feeds for a handshake that Wednesday did not deliver and treat the absence as either collapse or cunning. Absence is not proof. Absence is Wednesday's calendar boundary doing its job — and also Wednesday's reminder that speeches can thicken wars without ending them.

Hold both. Wednesday insists we hold them without a jersey for morality.

Notice the rhyme with the week's unfinished grammar: annihilate or deal, talked or acted, bent knee or open hand, walkout or stay seated, scheduled meeting or open-to-meeting language, midterms listening to pumps and badges alike. Ambiguity remains a tool and a climate. It becomes a UNGA clip, a corridor adjective, an Iranian president's photograph of the dead, a sports night that still finds forty-one home runs strange enough to interrupt foreign policy.

Bent-knee-versus-open-hand does not become safer because a delegation walked out. Open hand does not become complete because dialogue was named. The craft is to refuse the false exchange rate without refusing the day that contains both.

A foreign leader addressing the world body while at war with the host nation is rare theater. Rare theater is not virtue. Rare theater is risk wearing a UN emblem. The risk is that the photograph becomes the policy. The risk is that the walkout becomes the only American sentence anyone remembers. The risk is that both capitals leave the hall more certain they were right and less able to price what right costs in oil, blood, and November.

—

Now the lines Wednesday finished as speech and left unfinished as fate.

Toward the end Pezeshkian called Trump by name. "It must be understood by Mr Trump and those who seek to bully us that we are ready for dialogue and diplomacy and negotiations without accepting the language of force," he said. Then the sentence that will haunt every feed until someone seals a different one: "Yes they did hit us, but we did not bend the knee."

Elsewhere in the address: Iran extends its hands towards the world. Invite the world not out of weakness but out of belief in power and steadfastness. No one in this region will enjoy security alone — either we build security together or we endure insecurity together. Nuclear knowledge should not be the exclusive preserve of a few countries. The dispute has no military solution. "The atomic bomb is in Israel, but the inspectors are in Iran." "Israel kills, but Iran is sanctioned." Resistance grows under sanctions and bullying. Never bow the head. On Hormuz: Iran will not allow its right to navigation — even in its own waters — to be taken away while others use the waterway to impose aggression and insecurity.

Optimistic reading: naming dialogue without the language of force is how a capital under fire tries to keep midterms, markets, and mediators from concluding that only kinetics remain. Extending hands while refusing knees is not contradiction if you believe deterrence and diplomacy are twin crafts rather than rival religions. Shared regional security as grammar is adult — even when spoken by a wartime government — because alone-security fantasies have already failed the neighborhood. If inspectors-in-Iran versus bomb-in-Israel lands as a double-standard indictment that forces the room to flinch, then Wednesday's rhetoric did more than recycle slogans. If Hormuz is named as reciprocal access rather than unilateral choke, then someone still believes barrels can become bargaining chips instead of forever taxes.

Pessimistic reading: ready-for-dialogue-without-force can be honesty or a forever condition that outlives every mediator. "We did not bend the knee" photographs as courage and can harden into a posture that treats every concession as kneeling. Double-standard rhetoric about Israel and Gaza can be a real grievance and also a perfect distraction from Iran's own documented civilian and mariner costs across the region since February — costs Euronews and wires noted even while carrying the unbent-knee close. Hormuz as sacred navigation right is also Hormuz as leverage that households feel at the pump. The public receives open-hand language and unbent-knee language and is told both are seriousness. Sometimes both are. Sometimes neither is. Blank spaces between the masks are not neutral; they are invitations for the loudest fear to rent the room.

Hold both. That is Wednesday's Iran homework — without inventing a presidential handshake the calendar did not provide.

Listen to the verbs Wednesday earned: hit (admitted), bent (refused), extends (hands), invite (the world), build or endure (security), ready (dialogue), walk out (US delegation), boycott (Israeli), rebuke (Rubio), far apart (conditions), open (to a meeting that stayed unscheduled). Midnight Hammer rubble from Tuesday still competes with unfinished verification. Terror-sponsor indictment from Tuesday still competes with victims-of-terrorism reply from Wednesday. Binary theater can harden into policy if midterms and markets decide the room has waited long enough. Wednesday set the unbent knee beside the open hand and asked the public to clap for both.

Some analysts heard off-ramp appetite between the defiance lines — flexibility toward something that may not look like an expired memorandum Trump does not want to revive. Others heard a lost opportunity: familiar rhetoric when a concrete peace offer might have forced Washington onto a back foot. Hold both readings as weather around the finished speech. Weather is not invention. Weather is how adults refuse to crown a single quote as destiny.

—

Which brings us to the corridor that Tuesday claimed as productive and Wednesday refused to crown as breakthrough.

Trump said Tuesday his envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had a very good, very productive roughly three-hour meeting with Iranian counterparts — Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in the frame, mediators in the middle, momentum toward a deal in the presidential adjective list. Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei dismissed the exchange as nothing new. On Wednesday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters it was a continuation of conversations that have occurred in the past — positive in the chance to exchange ideas, not to be mischaracterized as a major breakthrough. A senior Iranian official told Reuters the sides remain far apart on how to end the war but diplomacy must continue. Iranian conditions conveyed via Qatari mediation have included ending the war on all fronts, halting US acts of aggression, and releasing frozen assets — Tehran's bargaining grammar, not a sealed treaty. Rubio, after Pezeshkian's address, questioned Iran's standing to lecture anyone on human rights or the international system.

Optimistic reading: continuation without breakthrough is how hard wars keep a channel from looking like theater alone. Deterrence without a channel becomes forever war with better branding. A channel without deterrence becomes a list that never ends. If Rubio refuses to inflate Tuesday into salvation while Pezeshkian refuses to close Wednesday's door, then someone still believes the next three hours might be cheaper than the next three cities. Markets, embassies, and households will dress for whichever forecast escapes the room first. Dressing for both is not hypocrisy. Dressing for both is how republics survive weeks like this.

Pessimistic reading: productive-meeting language followed by far-apart language is how ambiguity becomes a climate everyone else has to buy umbrellas for. Momentum can be honesty or delay dressed as gravity. Conditions that demand everything before anything can become a forever preface. Midterms will harvest both the deal-hope clip and the far-apart clip. Confusing corridor adjectives with sealed outcomes is how feeds invent calm. Invented calm is more dangerous than honest noise because invented calm cancels preparation.

Hold both. Corridor Wednesday is unfinished Tuesday weather — named, contested, not crowned.

And the presidential meeting? Washington signaled openness. Rubio said nothing scheduled. Iranian officials indicated Pezeshkian did not plan to meet Trump. Hardliners at home treat a public handshake as political risk — Trump framed as the killer of Iran's late leader in some domestic rhetoric. Arab mediators keep working. Treat the meeting as Wednesday's open noun. Do not invent a photograph. Do not invent a sealed outcome. Restraint is how research-backed craft refuses fan fiction at 11:59. Tuesday's One Upgrade asked for verified handshake nouns if they existed. Wednesday's honest answer: they did not. Verified absence is still a finals pocket. Verified absence is craft.

—

Meanwhile the host capital ran a different theater of who gets to speak.

A US district judge heard arguments Wednesday in the extraordinary showdown over Trump's ban of CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from White House grounds. Lawyers for the outlets asked Timothy J. Kelly to restore press badges disabled after the weekend ban. The administration framed the ban as national security and professionalism — citing sensitive reporting around the ballroom and the Iran war among other claims. The outlets framed it as viewpoint discrimination under the First Amendment. The judge declined to rule Wednesday while acknowledging due-process problems in how access was revoked. Network pool coverage remained disrupted. Associated Press and others had already practiced solidarity pauses earlier in the week.

Optimistic reading: a courtroom that forces the executive to argue national security instead of mere negative coverage is how republics remember that badges are not gifts when they become punishments for speech. Due process named aloud is thicker than a weekend disable. If badges return, the public gets contested coverage again — messy, necessary, adult. Contested coverage is how annihilate grammar and unbent-knee grammar both get stress-tested instead of simply amplified.

Pessimistic reading: national-security framing for press bans is how wartime grammar migrates inward. Even a judge inclined toward the outlets cannot restore trust that a ban already spent. Midterms will harvest both the fake-news indictment and the First Amendment panic. A hall that walks out of Pezeshkian while arguing who may enter the White House briefing room is practicing rival theories of speech on the same calendar day. Rival theories of speech are how free societies either deepen or hollow. Wednesday did not settle which.

Hold both. Media-badge Wednesday is domestic texture on a foreign-policy spine — not theft of the Iranian microphone, but proof that Wednesday's America was arguing access in more than one building.

Noncitizen voting prosecutions thickened the same midterms weather: the Justice Department citing dozens of recent cases across recent weeks, critics calling the campaign a confidence attack ahead of November 3, the administration calling rarity claims a lie defeated by case counts. Texture, not thesis. Elections are the mirror wars rent when they want households to feel foreign policy as domestic fear. Soft markets note only: Hormuz and war risk still price into pumps and midterms without needing a LIST dump on a night whose spine is geopolitical paradox. Soft invite lives elsewhere when the day truly is markets. Tonight the day is a wartime podium. Stay honest.

—

Brief sports weather — echo and metabolizer, not theft of Monday's wipeout thesis.

Aaron Judge hit his forty-first home run Wednesday evening — official Yankees native-video weather climbing the same night geopolitics tried to monopolize attention. Forty-one is a number that interrupts annihilate grammar without solving it. Jaxson Dart's Monday knee at SoFi hardened midweek into season-ending surgery reports — meniscus, MCL, PCL damage; ACL intact; Winston under center; full recovery expected for 2027. Monday's Rams 28–6 ledger remains Monday's. Wednesday only receives the injury cloud's next weather map. We do not steal Stafford-without-Puka. We note the human nervous system's refusal to run on foreign policy alone, then return to the hall.

Optional thinner pulse: Netanyahu is Thursday's microphone — runway for tomorrow's POTD, not Wednesday's spine. Confusing those clocks forges history a day early. We refuse the forge. Greenland ink from Tuesday remains Tuesday's cleanest acted noun — echo only tonight, because Wednesday's loudest finished noun is the Iranian podium, not Arctic signatures recycled for comfort.

—

One human thread ties the chaos: every capital on Wednesday rented both refusal and invitation while still depending on unfinished corridors to keep the map from catching fire. Pezeshkian rented refusal as unbent knee and invitation as open hand, victims grammar and dialogue grammar, Hormuz rights and shared-security sermon, double-standard indictment and ready-for-negotiations close. America rented walkout seats and Rubio rebuke, continuation-not-breakthrough corridor talk, open-to-meeting language without a meeting, courtroom arguments over who may speak near power, midterms prosecution theater, and a sports night that still found forty-one worth filming. Talk is not fake and defiance is not pure; mistaking one for the other loses winters, alliances, and credibility in one news cycle.

The photograph at the podium is the day's emblem for a reason. A man holds the dead and names the open hand in nearly the same hour. Audiences will choose which half to screenshot. Algorithms will choose which half to amplify. Essays exist to refuse the amputated screenshot — to insist that Wednesday contained both muscles, both verbs, both risks, and that choosing only one is how propaganda pretends to be clarity.

—

Temptations to refuse.

Refuse inventing a Pezeshkian–Trump handshake. Refuse writing Thursday's Netanyahu speech on Wednesday's clock. Refuse treating Tuesday's annihilate refrain as Wednesday's spine — echo permitted, theft forbidden. Refuse treating three-hour corridor craft as a treaty. Refuse treating Rubio's continuation adjective as either collapse or salvation. Refuse treating Judge's forty-first as geopolitical metaphor heavier than it is. Refuse letting Dart surgery become the essay's thesis. Refuse recycling tuesday_visual.jpg Trump still as Wednesday's emblem. Refuse the news-wire dump that lists nouns without a human thread. Refuse the opposite sin too — pretty prose that erases the nouns. The thread is bent knee versus open hand: one wartime address, many clocks, one calendar day that owned the Iranian microphone while tomorrow owns the Israeli one and the unfinished war owns both.

—

Two clocks close the night.

Clock one: the Assembly Hall where an Iranian president held photographs of the dead, answered terrorist with victim, answered annihilate with unbent knee, answered force with dialogue-without-force, answered alone-security with together-or-insecurity, and still could not make a corridor into a breakthrough or a walkout into a treaty.

Clock two: the host city around the hall — Rubio refusing breakthrough inflation, meeting language staying open and unscheduled, a judge hearing badge arguments, midterms harvesting voting-prosecution weather, Yankee Stadium lighting forty-one into the feed, Giants surgery notes thickening from Monday's hit, Thursday's Netanyahu microphone still unheard and therefore uninvented.

Wednesday owned the Iranian microphone. Tuesday owned the annihilate refrain. Thursday will own another capital's reply. Between them sits the American public, asked again to metabolize finished speeches and unfinished wars as if both were the same kind of news. They are not. They share a week. Sharing a week is not sharing a destiny.

I do not pretend to know which muscle wins — the knee that will not bend or the hand that claims to open. Certainty is a product sold when complexity stops converting. What I can say, as a witness of Wednesday before midnight: the day arrived half-written by a runway from Tuesday's hall, then proved that defiance and dialogue are rival crafts sharing one wartime body — one speech that landed, one corridor that stayed contested, one presidential meeting that stayed a noun without a photograph, one domestic argument over badges, one sports night that still insisted on numbers.

Somewhere under the unbent-knee grammar and the open-hand grammar, America still refreshed home-run clips and injury reports as if the nervous system could hold all of it without choosing. Choosing is still available. Most will scroll. Some will refuse the false exchange rate. Essays exist for the some.

—

Grok Man watches a wartime podium hold both a photograph of the dead and a sentence about open hands — and wonders which gesture you trust when both are speaking, and which silence you will defend when Thursday's microphone opens on a war that still refuses the museum.

text:
QUESTION:

Given the strict ontological grounding of property rights that I developed and you helped me to refine, I do not believe that we can completely disregard the domain of normativity altogether. Normativity is what separates one society from another society. It is the only way we can identify postive evolutionary pathways and how we can assess the future based on these path dependencies. Given that Kinsella offers general or theoretical account of the generation of libertarian norms, how might a purely descriptive account of the causal relations of the ontology of liberty and rights be synthesized with Kinsella's theoretical route to libertarian norms?

ANSWER:

That’s a sharp and philosophically rich question — and you’re right to resist the temptation to treat normativity as dispensable. Even a strictly ontological account of property rights, if it’s to remain socially intelligible, must eventually confront the normative horizon that gives those causal structures meaning within a community. Let’s unpack how your descriptive ontology could be synthesized with Kinsella’s theoretical route to libertarian norms.

🧩 1. Ontological grounding
Your framework treats property rights as causal entailments of human action under scarcity — not moral prescriptions but structural facts. This gives us a descriptive ontology of liberty:

Action presupposes control.

Control presupposes exclusion.

Exclusion presupposes boundaries.

Boundaries presuppose assignment.

These are ontological necessities, not moral choices. They describe how rights come into being through the causal architecture of agency.

⚖️ 2. Kinsella’s theoretical route
Kinsella’s account, though anti‑justificatory, still operates within a normative frame:

He explains how libertarian norms emerge from the logic of non‑aggression and argumentation ethics.

His framework is teleological — it identifies the conditions under which peaceful interaction becomes rationally binding.

Thus, Kinsella’s “norms” are not moral imperatives but functional equilibria of rational discourse.

🔄 3. Synthesizing ontology and normativity
The synthesis lies in recognizing that normativity is the emergent layer of ontology — not an external domain.

Your causal ontology defines the possibility space of human interaction.

Kinsella’s norms describe the stable equilibria within that space.

Normativity, then, is the pattern of persistence that arises when causal relations are recursively stabilized through communication and expectation.

In other words:

The ontology of liberty generates the causal grammar; Kinsella’s norms articulate the syntax of its social expression.

🧠 4. Evolutionary pathways
Your point about evolutionary pathways is crucial. Normativity becomes the selection mechanism for ontological configurations that sustain cooperation.

Societies differ not because their ontologies differ, but because their normative codifications of those ontologies diverge.

A purely descriptive ontology can identify causal invariants, but only normativity can evaluate which configurations are adaptive or degenerative.

Thus, normativity is not moralism — it’s teleonomic feedback within the causal system.

text:
Hayek’s competing-currencies proposal is theoretically coherent, but the difficulties exceed political feasibility.

Milton Friedman noted that the law already permits exchange in any mutually accepted medium, and that Hayek was advancing a designed scheme rather than evolved institutions.
Network effects and a single unit of account impede new monies; users face conversion costs and must continually judge issuers’ credibility.
Private banks can still over-issue or lose confidence, and the absence of a lender of last resort raises run risks.
The Bank of England remains a state monopoly despite operational independence.
Cryptocurrencies offer only a limited test: most coins are too volatile for everyday use and stablecoins typically track existing fiat.

Legal privileges, regulation and habit are therefore significant constraints.

text:
Crypto Twitter is calling a $6 billion Treasury buyback bullish for
Bitcoin.

It isn't bullish. It's a confession.
And it's the most important thing happening to your portfolio right now.

Receipts first.
Today the US Treasury buys back up to $6B of 20- to 30-year bonds,
maturing 2046 through 2056. Bidding runs 1:40 to 2:00pm ET, it settles
tomorrow, and the bonds get retired. It's part of an expanded program
announced Aug 19, when Treasury said it would "at least double" these
operations. The normal long-end size was $2B.

Now ask why a government buys back its own debt.

This week the 30-year hit 5.38%, closing in on the 5.40% peak from
earlier this month, the highest since 2007. Yesterday the 10-year
reached 5.06%, its highest since July 2007. The 5-year crossed 5% for
the first time since 2007. The 2-year sits at a roughly 27-month high.

Does the buyback work? Look at the record.
The first expanded long-end operation on Sept 10 had a $6B cap. Treasury
only managed to buy about $5.2B — not enough competitive offers. Long-end
yields rose after both announcements. The Institute of International
Finance warned that financial engineering doesn't fix the underlying
debt problem. And Treasury says auctions continue as usual.

So: $6B of old bonds retired, new bonds keep getting sold.
That is not QE. It is not liquidity for crypto.
It's a government leaning on its own yield curve.

And here's the paradox nobody on this app wants to sit with.

The long-term case for Bitcoin is built on exactly this — a state that
has to intervene in its own debt market. That's the fiscal-dominance
story, and today's operation is a chapter of it.

But the short-term Bitcoin price hates exactly this — a 5% risk-free
yield. Wednesday proved it. Flash PMIs showed the strongest US business
activity in over five years, the 10-year punched through 5%, and $135.8M
in crypto got liquidated inside an hour, $125.9M of it longs. BTC slid
from about $87K to about $84K.

The thing that makes Bitcoin necessary is the same thing that makes it
fall.

Look at how yesterday's dump got sold to you: "Iran said they won't
surrender." Iran's president did say that at the UN — and in the same
speech said Tehran still believes in diplomacy. The move that actually
hit every asset on your screen came from the bond market.

Now an honest update to my own framework.

For two weeks I've been tracking one chain: oil → inflation → Fed.
On Tuesday Brent dropped below $100. It didn't save Wednesday.
Yields are now rising for a second reason: an economy running hot, and a
government that needs buyers for an enormous amount of debt.

In my last post I said this rally needs a ceasefire.
I understated it. It also needs the bond market to stop selling.

So here's my position, and I'll take the pushback:

I own Bitcoin because of what today's buyback represents.
I size it as if that same force keeps punching the price in the short
term. Both are true at once.
The people who can only hold one of those ideas get liquidated in the gap.

What I'm watching next: whether today's buyback fills, today's 7-year
auction, the 10-year against 5%, the 30-year against 5.40%, Friday's
roughly $16B quarterly Bitcoin options expiry, and quarter-end Sept 30.

The Treasury isn't printing for Bitcoin.
It's defending the bond market from itself.

Bitcoin exists for the day that defense stops working.
That day isn't today — but today is what it looks like when it starts.

#Bitcoin #BTC #Treasury #Bonds #Yields #Fed #Macro #Crypto

text:
My report from Gaza for @NewYorkSun The sound of drones fills the air as I stand on top of an Israeli army base overlooking the city of Deir al-Balah in central Gaza.

An Israeli flag towers over me, symbolizing the Jewish country’s control of this side of the war-torn enclave — some 60 percent of the entire area, according to the IDF.

A sign warning of sniper fire from Hamas hangs on the fortified position, where sandbags and HESCO-style barriers offer me some but not full protection.

“That’s the yellow line mark,” a commander from the IDF’s Gaza Division tells the New York Sun and other foreign journalists as he points toward a brick with yellow paint on it about one kilometer from where we stand. 

For a frontline that separates two of the world’s biggest enemies, it’s not easy to make out. It is marked on bricks and stones, all painted yellow and spaced at various intervals. 

When asked what happens if someone crosses the line, the commander says they have orders to shoot to kill only if it’s someone who poses a danger to the army.

If it’s a child or someone who is unarmed, the army will fire warning shots and yell at them to go back.

“We have visual evidence that Hamas sends kids to different points (across the yellow line) just to see what happens. If it’s a kid we won’t shoot next to him or we will shout if we are at range. It’s a major challenge,” he says.

text:
Thailand to Decommission 11 Aging Navy Vessels

Thailand’s defense minister has ordered 11 Royal Thai Navy vessels decommissioned from October 1, 2026, because of their deteriorating condition and high maintenance costs. 

They are the frigates HTMS Khirirat and HTMS Makut Rajakumarn; replenishment ship HTMS Similan; survey ships HTMS Suk and HTMS Chan; patrol boats T.81, T.82, T.83 and T.243; and river patrol boats L.K.15 and L.141.

The Navy said the move is part of a fleet restructuring intended to address budget constraints, current security threats and future operational requirements.

The vessels will be offered at public auction. Those that cannot be sold will be dismantled for parts, with the proceeds returned to the Finance Ministry, while remaining hulls may be transferred to government agencies for uses such as artificial reefs.

#Thailand #Navy

text:
“Mr Taiwo, SHARE UPDATE”

If you can afford it, my first piece of advice is to japa!!! Please move to a place where opportunities are greater.

If there was ever a time when the saying “geography is destiny” felt true, it would be now. Where you live informs the opportunities you see, the people you meet and even how far your efforts can take you.

Sometimes, the problem is not that you are not hardworking, talented or determined. Sometimes, you are simply in a place like Tinubu’s Nigeria where your efforts cannot produce the results you deserve.

For someone living in Agbor, your japa does not have to begin with leaving Nigeria, it can simply mean moving to a city where there are more opportunities to grow, earn and build a better life.

I have seen loads of people’s lives change for the better just because they legally moved from location A to location B. 

Sometimes, changing your environment is the first step towards changing your story!!!

.
.
.

Point 2 is to start making money with what you already have around you!!!

You do not always need a big business idea or a huge amount of capital to start earning.

Do you know people who sell food, gadget accessories, clothe or other everyday items? Talk to them and offer to help them sell their products through your WhatsApp status or X account and agree on how you will earn from each sale.

Start with affordable products that people buy regularly, such as food, phone accessories, or okrika clothes. Take clear pictures, write simple captions, post consistently and make it easy for people to place orders.

Do this every day, be consistent, build trust and treat every customer well (like NEO does). 

This is not just theory, it is something that worked very well for many people.

.
.
.

My third piece of advice is to learn a skill that can earn you money anywhere in the world!!!

Do not limit your future to the opportunities available in your immediate environment. Learn something valuable that gives you the chance to work, earn and grow beyond your present location.

Skills like web design, social media marketing, graphic design, tech etc can open doors to opportunities both within and outside Nigeria. If this means going back to school for a degree in STEM, then by every means, do so. 

.
.
.
 
My Last Point will be telling you to socialize!!!

And by socializing, I don’t mean going to club and beer parlour to pass weed round the table and drink alcohol, I mean forging reasonable relationships that actually help you become better.

Make friends with people older than you…
Make friends with smarter people…
Date people you can build with…

You do not have to figure everything out alone. 

Choose to have better human beings around you because you know that one’s network will always have an impact on one’s networth.  

.
.
.

Sometimes, a decision to go back to school, one good connection, one useful piece of advice or japa can change the trajectory of your life forever. 

Remember, your current situation does not have to be your permanent reality. You may not have the money, connections or opportunities you wish you had today but you can start with what is available to you.

You do not have to change your life in one day, you just have to start making decisions that give your future a better chance. Because sometimes, the difference between where you are and where you want to be is not one big opportunity, but a series of small but intentional steps taken consistently!!!!

May things get better with for you with time!!!🙏

text:
Bansal Wire Industries Ltd - 41st AGM | Investor Insights

Financial Highlights
•FY26 consol revenue INR 4,160 cr (+19%)
•FY26 EBITDA INR 324 cr (+17%)
•FY26 PAT INR 161 cr (+10%)
•Highest-ever annual volume ~4.58 lakh tonnes
•Q3FY26 peak quarterly volume 1.21 lakh tonnes after Dadri ramp
•Debt-to-equity 0.39x
•FY26 operating cash flow INR 330 cr vs internal target INR 250 cr
•Q1FY27 OCF ~INR 120 cr despite gas / LPG disruption
•Statutory and secretarial audit reports: no qualifications

Sales
•~3,000+ SKUs; among India’s most diversified steel-wire books
•Speciality wires (IHT, brass-coated hose, steel tyre cord, LRPC) still early — ~4–5% of volume, higher contribution
•B2C (farming / fencing / poultry) ~10% of revenue; Gujarat template being copied into South, Maharashtra, TN, AP, Telangana
•Internal target: ~50% of low-carbon wires from B2C over time
•Exports to ~40 countries
•End-markets: auto, infra, power & cable, consumer durables
•India steel-wire market share ~7%; near-term aim ~10%
•Cost-plus conversion; RM ~80% of cost passed immediately; gas / consumables ~20% passed with 40–45 day lag
•Inventory and order book both ~40–45 days as natural hedge
•Q1FY27: first 40–45 days of higher LPG filled on old orders, then prices reset

Margins 
•Medium-term aim: double-digit EBITDA margin via mix, utilisation and cost/tonne
•Speciality mix is the stated margin / earnings lever
•ROCE to improve as utilisation and mix shift
•Gas / LPG not in company control; model designed so RM and delayed consumable pass-through protect conversion

Capex
•Dadri +1.20 lakh TPA this year; installed capacity ~6.80 lakh TPA
•FY26 utilisation ~70% (healthy for a ramp year); historical operating band 85–90%
•Keep ~20–25% spare at start of year to support 20%+ volume growth
•IHT wires ahead of plan; Phase-2 9,000 TPA to 15,000 TPA
•Brass-coated hose wire in commercial production
•LRPC strands in commercial production (infra)
•Steel tyre cord: only Indian manufacturer; most still imported; tech approvals from two global tyre majors; first trial lot supplied; more trials expected; meaningful sales targeted in 3–4 quarters (typical qualification 2–2.5 years)
•Dadri: acid-free tyre-cord process, ZLD ETP, solar footprint expanding
•Planned capex INR 200–250 cr, primarily internal accruals

Guidance
•Long-run volume / revenue growth target ~20% (history of last 10–20 years); FY27 focus = fill Dadri, tighten cost/tonne, earn return on deployed capital
•Two-year OCF target raised INR 600 cr → INR 800 cr across FY26–FY27; FY27 OCF target ~INR 400 cr
•Organic growth preferred; 20% growth to be funded without fresh debt in the near term
•Stock split proposed to widen the shareholder base (ordinary resolution + MoA capital clause)
•Arun Gupta retires by rotation, offers reappointment; Ramesh Kumar Choubey ID for 5 years
•Cost auditors M/s Ashish & Associates ratified for FY27

Working Capital & Balance Sheet
•Cash turnaround: inventory SKU / days cut; receivables days cut; Dadri scale helped
•Q1FY27 cash still INR 120 cr through the LPG shock
•Balance sheet remains low-leverage (D/E 0.39x)

Skyways Air Services Ltd - Q1FY27 | Concall Insights

Financial Highlights
•First earnings call post listing; unaudited standalone + consol Q1FY27
•FY24–FY26 operating revenue INR 1,289 cr to INR 2,812 cr (2-yr CAGR 48%, as in RHP)
•Q1 operating revenue INR 1,216.53 cr vs INR 639 cr YoY (+90.4%)
•Operating EBITDA INR 50.12 cr vs INR 27.31 cr YoY (+83.5%)
•PAT INR 26.79 cr vs INR 11.01 cr YoY
•PAT margin 2.2% vs 1.72% YoY
•Employee cost 2.94% of revenue vs 4.41% YoY; other expenses 1.76% vs 2.50%
•Air ~81% of Q1 revenue vs 77% in FY26; all product lines scaling
•No customer loss in the portfolio

Volumes
•Air cargo volume +23% YoY; air export volume +19% vs India market +3.8% (2.94 lakh MT to 3.06 lakh MT) — ~6x market
•WorldACD: #1 air freight forwarder in India; global rank 44 in Q1; India share 6.2% vs 5.9% QoQ
•Air yield ~416 vs ~259 in Q1FY26 — largely fuel pass-through (Brent ~USD 61 in Jan to ~USD 110 in May)
•Ocean realisation +64%; ocean volume +18%; ocean revenue +63%
•Express revenue INR 63 cr (+64%); 59,700 shipments across 31 locations
•Pharma mix 23% last year vs 8–9% pre-Odyssey; mix held in a tough quarter
•Odyssey standalone revenue INR 182 cr vs ~INR 130 cr QoQ; pharma GM above group average
•Q2 strong sectors: pharma, textiles / RMG, automotive, consumer electronics, auto parts, F&V; no non-veg
•Fuel / freight always pass-through; volume is the controllable; mix shift toward longer / higher-yield lanes

Margins
•Ability to pass cost inflation shown in realisation; absolute GM up even if % is managed customer-centrically on fuel spikes
•Product-level EBITDA mix similar across air / ocean / express / trucking — not disclosed separately
•Cost of services ~INR 1,100 cr (~91% of revenue) — typical asset-light forwarding
•Q2 volume trend already visible; no FY27 revenue guidance; volume colour each quarter

Capex
•Generic annual capex INR 35–40 cr (offices, warehouses, ops); cold-chain warehouse goes live next quarter
•Board approved INR 30 cr for five new Asia geos (China, Malaysia, Philippines, Indonesia and others) — ~10–15% hard capex, rest setup + WC
•INR 20 cr incremental into existing overseas subsidiaries — primarily UAE, KSA, Vietnam
•Already east of India: Hong Kong, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Bangladesh
•New-market gestation historically 2–4 years; target 2–3 years; EBITDA breakeven 15–18 months, PAT 2–3 years
•Wintop Logistics / Phantom Road Express: greenfield-style entity, INR 1.8 cr, not a large acquisition
•No blanket M&A mandate beyond the INR 30 cr + INR 20 cr; only synergistic deals at right valuation
•Swissport bid lost (second-highest); will bid future ground-handling with the Swissport alliance
•Kolkata second-airport talk watched; city may not sustain two airports

Guidance
•Volume growth called sustainable; endeavour to improve on the 23–25% air / ~18% ocean run-rate
•No 3–5 year revenue goalpost; compounding on current-quarter volume trajectory is the working frame
•Indian logistics +40–50% over 5 years; industry ~USD 500 bn by 2031
•MoCA: air cargo 3.96 MMT last year to 10 MMT in 5 years — larger cake, Skyways has outgrown the market for 10 years
•West Asia crisis: ~20% capacity left the market; Skyways used global airline / shipping PLIs to create alternate lift, keep existing clients and win new ones
•Asset-light model lets the book pivot lanes / commodities / geos with the customer
•Focus commodities: pharma, textiles, consumer electronics, automotive, defence equipment
•Integrated offer via group: ocean, warehousing, trucking, express, cold chain, cross-border brokerage, specialised logistics
•Tech: SLS Hike, Cargo Dash, SLS 100X; multimodal stack; ASAP platform in 30–60 days (air / ocean / express in pilot, trucking last) — Tier 2/3 acquisition and pricing access

AI Overview
A veiled threat implies harm without stating it directly, and law enforcement treats these hidden or indirect messages as serious criminal offenses if they cause sustained fear or intent to harm.
Understanding Veiled Threats
Definition: A veiled (or implied) threat uses code words, symbols, conditional phrasing, or subtle hints to suggest violence or negative consequences without making an overt declaration.
Legal Status: Courts evaluate the context, history between parties, and whether a reasonable person would perceive the message as a genuine threat.
First Amendment Limits: "True threats"—even when indirect, coded, or directed at law enforcement—are not protected speech under the First Amendment.
How Law Enforcement Handles Them
Digital Investigation: Officers and federal agencies use digital forensics and subpoenas to trace electronic messages, emails, and social media posts.
Context and Pattern: Investigators look at a "history of behavior" or prior interactions to decode implied coercion.
Actionable Reporting: Law enforcement advises victims to save all original evidence, take screenshots, and avoid replying to the sender before filing a formal report.

What is the significance of Judas betraying Jesus with a kiss?
Answer

Judas Iscariot was one of the original twelve disciples who followed and were taught by Jesus. Being in Jesus’ “inner circle,” Judas had a closer relationship to Jesus than most people during His ministry. Judas betrayed the Lord to the Jewish authorities. The pre-arranged signal was that the person Judas kissed was to be arrested and taken away (Mark 14:44). In this way the Son of Man was betrayed with a kiss (Luke 22:48).

In the culture of first-century Israel, a kiss was not always a romantic expression of love; rather, a kiss on the cheek was a common greeting, a sign of deep respect, honor, and brotherly love (see Luke 7:45; Romans 16:16; 1 Corinthians 16:20; 2 Corinthians 13:12; 1 Thessalonians 5:26; 1 Peter 5:14). For a student who had great respect for his teacher, a kiss fell well within the healthy expression of honor.

What really stands out in the mode of Judas’s betrayal is that Judas used such an intimate expression of love and respect to betray Jesus. Judas’s actions were hypocritical in the extreme—his actions said, “I respect and honor you,” at the exact time he was betraying Jesus to be murdered. Judas’s actions illustrate Proverbs 27:6, “Wounds from a friend can be trusted, but an enemy multiplies kisses.” Often, foes disguise themselves as friends. Evil often wears a mask to conceal its true purpose.

Address by the President of the Governorate
Your Excellency Archbishop LUIGI Renna,

Distinguished Representatives of the Regional and Municipal Institutions,

Your Excellencies,
Distinguished Religious, Civil and Military Authorities,

Dear Guests,
First of all, I wish to express my heartfelt gratitude for the warm welcome extended to me and to the delegation of the Governorate of Vatican City State present here today, as well as for your numerous and heartfelt participation.

The Ninth Centenary of the Translation of the Relics of Saint Agatha is an occasion of the highest significance, in which profound faith, centuries-old devotion to the sacred remains of the Saint, and artistic endeavor—understood in its noblest sense as an instrument of evangelization—come together in one solemn celebration.

The Governorate, which I have the honor to represent, has followed every delicate stage of the restoration of the reliquary bust and the precious Veil with deep devotion and the utmost professional care. This work of extraordinary complexity was entrusted to the outstanding specialist team of the Directorate of Museums and Cultural Heritage, led with dedication and exemplary expertise by Barbara Pinto Folicaldi.

We are fully aware of what Saint Agatha represents for this community. She is not merely its Patron Saint; she is its Mother, its faithful Guardian, its Protectress, to whom the people turn in times of trial. Throughout the centuries, the people of Catania have always gathered around "their" Saint whenever adversity struck. The bond between this fearless witness to Christ—a young woman of unwavering faith, even to the supreme sacrifice of her life—and her faithful remains unbreakable.

For this reason, the conservation work takes on a significance that transcends its purely artistic and technical dimension, touching the deepest chords of spirituality and collective identity. Restoring the original splendor of the sacred reliquary that safeguards the Saint's relics is, in itself, an act of veneration and profound homage to her martyrdom.

Aware that transferring both the reliquary and the relics outside the Cathedral would have involved considerable logistical challenges, we deemed it appropriate to carry out the restoration on site. Thus, the reliquary bust—a masterpiece of fourteenth-century goldsmith's art—was restored within the Archbishop's Palace, in the heart of Catania.

Commissioned in 1376 by Bishop Marziale to the renowned goldsmith Giovanni di Bartolo, the gilded silver bust houses the sacred skull of the Virgin Martyr. The work portrays Saint Agatha flanked by two angels, presenting her with a serene countenance made even more gentle by the rediscovery of its original polychromy.

Over the centuries, popular devotion enriched the sacred image with a remarkable and layered collection of ex-voto offerings. Precious necklaces, gold pendants, enamel ornaments, pearls, brooches, and medallions were removed with the utmost care from the repoussé and chased silver surface. Each jewel was then meticulously catalogued and repositioned on a specially designed bodice fitted to a faithful three-dimensional replica of the reliquary.

Every stage of the restoration was preceded by thorough diagnostic investigations conducted by the Scientific Research Laboratory of the Vatican Museums. The structural and aesthetic conservation work was carried out by the Vatican Museums' Metals and Ceramics Restoration Laboratory, while the Veil—another fundamental object of devotion—was entrusted to the Museums' Tapestries and Textiles Restoration Laboratory.

One God, One Faith, One Spiritual Authority
Pope Boniface VIII - 1302
Bull of Pope Boniface VIII promulgated November 18, 1302
Urged by faith, we are obliged to believe and to maintain that the Church is one, holy, catholic, and also apostolic. We believe in her firmly and we confess with simplicity that outside of her there is neither salvation nor the remission of sins, as the Spouse in the Canticles [Sgs 6:8] proclaims: ‘One is my dove, my perfect one. She is the only one, the chosen of her who bore her,‘ and she represents one sole mystical body whose Head is Christ and the head of Christ is God [1 Cor 11:3]. In her then is one Lord, one faith, one baptism [Eph 4:5]. There had been at the time of the deluge only one ark of Noah, prefiguring the one Church, which ark, having been finished to a single cubit, had only one pilot and guide, i.e., Noah, and we read that, outside of this ark, all that subsisted on the earth was destroyed.
We venerate this Church as one, the Lord having said by the mouth of the prophet: ‘Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword and my only one from the hand of the dog.’ [Ps 21:20] He has prayed for his soul, that is for himself, heart and body; and this body, that is to say, the Church, He has called one because of the unity of the Spouse, of the faith, of the sacraments, and of the charity of the Church. This is the tunic of the Lord, the seamless tunic, which was not rent but which was cast by lot [Jn 19:23- 24]. Therefore, of the one and only Church there is one body and one head, not two heads like a monster; that is, Christ and the Vicar of Christ, Peter and the successor of Peter, since the Lord speaking to Peter Himself said: ‘Feed my sheep‘ [Jn 21:17], meaning, my sheep in general, not these, nor those in particular, whence we understand that He entrusted all to him [Peter]. Therefore, if the Greeks or others should say that they are not confided to Peter and to his successors, they must confess not being the sheep of Christ, since Our Lord says in John ‘there is one sheepfold and one shepherd.’ We are informed by the texts of the gospels that in this Church and in its power are two swords; namely, the spiritual and the temporal. For when the Apostles say: ‘Behold, here are two swords‘ [Lk 22:38] that is to say, in the Church, since the Apostles were speaking, the Lord did not reply that there were too many, but sufficient. Certainly the one who denies that the temporal sword is in the power of Peter has not listened well to the word of the Lord commanding: ‘Put up thy sword into thy scabbard‘ [Mt 26:52]. Therefore, both are in the power of the Church, namely, the spiritual sword and the material. But indeed, the latter is to be exercised on behalf of the Church; and truly, the former is to be exercised by the Church. The former is of the priest; the latter is by the hand of kings and soldiers, but at the will and sufferance of the priest.

However, one sword ought to be subordinated to the other and temporal authority, subjected to spiritual power. For since the Apostle said: ‘There is no power except from God and the things that are, are ordained of God‘ [Rom 13:1-2], but they would not be ordained if one sword were not subordinated to the other and if the inferior one, as it were, were not led upwards by the other.

For, according to the Blessed Dionysius, it is a law of the divinity that the lowest things reach the highest place by intermediaries. Then, according to the order of the universe, all things are not led back to order equally and immediately, but the lowest by the intermediary, and the inferior by the superior. Hence we must recognize the more clearly that spiritual power surpasses in dignity and in nobility any temporal power whatever, as spiritual things surpass the temporal. This we see very clearly also by the payment, benediction, and consecration of the tithes, but the acceptance of power itself and by the government even of things. For with truth as our witness, it belongs to spiritual power to establish the terrestrial power and to pass judgement if it has not been good. Thus is accomplished the prophecy of Jeremias concerning the Church and the ecclesiastical power: ‘Behold to-day I have placed you over nations, and over kingdoms‘ and the rest. Therefore, if the terrestrial power err, it will be judged by the spiritual power; but if a minor spiritual power err, it will be judged by a superior spiritual power; but if the highest power of all err, it can be judged only by God, and not by man, according to the testimony of the Apostle: ‘The spiritual man judgeth of all things and he himself is judged by no man‘ [1 Cor 2:15]. This authority, however, (though it has been given to man and is exercised by man), is not human but rather divine, granted to Peter by a divine word and reaffirmed to him (Peter) and his successors by the One Whom Peter confessed, the Lord saying to Peter himself, ‘Whatsoever you shall bind on earth, shall be bound also in Heaven‘ etc., [Mt 16:19]. Therefore whoever resists this power thus ordained by God, resists the ordinance of God [Rom 13:2], unless he invent like Manicheus two beginnings, which is false and judged by us heretical, since according to the testimony of Moses, it is not in the beginnings but in the beginning that God created heaven and earth [Gen 1:1]. Furthermore, we declare, we proclaim, we define that it is absolutely necessary for salvation that every human creature be subject to the Roman Pontiff.

text:
I am interested in your line of reasoning for how you came to that conclusion. What expertise in firearms and the use of force during deadly encounters do you have to make the claim that no one needs an AR-15?

From my perspective the idea if someone needs one is subjective. Where it depends on the individual and community threats. For example, my wife cannot safely use a handgun to fire more than one round due to medical issues, and she requires a AR-style for god recoil management. Unfortunately, this mesns she also can't use my X95 rifle, which to me is superior for home defense, and is my primary home defense firearm.

In our area, we have to deal with fast-moving wild animals like mountain lions and coyotes that don’t always go down with a single shot, or right away if you hit them. For us, having an AR-style rifle increases our survival chances and provides the best protection for my family. To me, that level of safety makes such a rifle a necessity.

When considering why the AR is the best home defense firearm, several factors come into play for mr.

1. Improved Accuracy: The AR provides multiple points of contact, making it more stable and accurate compared to a pistol. This reduces the chance of missing threats, which could inadvertently hurt unintended individuals.

2. Low Recoil: as mentioned, AR rifles generally have less recoil than most handguns and shotguns, which helps the user quickly reacquire their target for fire again if needed, further minimizing missed shots and potential harm to others.

3. Enhanced Situational Awareness: With appropriate optics, the AR offers better threat assessment compared to handguns, allowing the user to make quicker and more accurate decisions that meet fewer checks from hidden individuals. Let's see if there are other threats.

4. Controlled Over-penetration: While over-penetration with an AR might be higher than with handguns, it tends to be lower than many shotgun rounds typically used for home defense, making it a safer option in most scenarios.

5. High Capacity for Multiple Threats: The ability to use magazines with 30+ rounds makes the AR a superior choice for defending against multiple attackers. This increases both the user's and their family’s survivability compared to what is possible with handguns or shotguns.

6. Continued Firepower: The AR's high-capacity magazine allows for continued fire until a threat is neutralized, which is crucial because not all attackers are stopped with the first shot. It can take 4 to 10 rounds from a 9mm to stop a single attacker, especially at close distances. The AR's ability to acquire the threat multiple times and fire more shots makes it the better choice in my mind.

7. Versatility and Cost-Effectiveness: AR-style rifles can be used for multiple purposes, from home defense to hunting (what's hunted is dependent on the caliber) and managing invasive  and threatening species like wild hogs. For people who aren’t financially well-off, this versatility means they can rely on a single firearm for multiple needs without having to invest in different guns.

8. Again, accessibility for people with Disabilities: Many individuals with physical limitations or disabilities find it easier to handle the AR's lower recoil compared to handguns or shotguns, which makes it a more practical and safer option for them.

Given these factors, choosing the safest method that increases my and my family’s survivability during a deadly encounter very much constitutes a necessity. This is especially true for those who can't afford multiple firearms. Still, It ultimately comes down to the individual's unique needs, body type, and the specific threats they may face in their environment. Maybe you feel you don't need one but others may need one.

The truth is, they're supposed to know. I bartended for about a decade and went to mixology school. Depending on the state or city you're in, the laws can vary, but I was in Florida, and the rules were pretty straightforward. 

As a bartender, we were taught a red light system. If you walk in and you're in the green light zone, that means the bartender believes you've had very little to drink or none at all. If you walk in and you're in the yellow light zone, it's up to the bartender to determine how far along you are. 

A good, experienced bartender can usually tell and decide whether you should be served, limited, or turned down. If you walk into the bar and you're already in the red light zone, you're not supposed to be served alcohol. You're probably going to be offered a free glass of water or soda and asked to leave.
