text:
#Space #Cosmos
 Could comet 3I/ATLAS teach us about life beyond Earth? Scientists say the story's not over yet.  https://t.co/upstLxCh0R 

In July 2025, a large, bright cosmic object visited from beyond our solar system. Only the third interstellar object ever discovered, the comet — named 3I/ATLAS — swooped through the inner solar system for about four months, briefly making it one of the biggest science celebrities in the world.

The interstellar object's fame stemmed in large part from controversial (and unsubstantiated) claims that it could be a source of intelligent alien technology, even though 3I/ATLAS behaved like a natural comet. However, according to the astronomers who are studying its mysteries in the data collected by dozens of telescopes and spacecraft, the ancient object may still have lessons to teach us about life in the cosmos.

3I/ATLAS is likely a preserved fragment of a planetesimal — a building block of a planet — from a distant system, Martin Cordiner, a researcher in astrochemistry and planetary science at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center, told Live Science. Therefore, the comet's composition could offer clues to the prevalence of life's building blocks around distant stars. Some astronomers even hope this cosmic interloper will help constrain how likely life is elsewhere in our galaxy.

Blast from the past 

Comets like 3I/ATLAS are important because scientists think they help "seed" planets with carbon-containing chemicals, Darryl Seligman, an assistant professor of astronomy at Michigan State University, told Live Science in an email. Some of these chemicals, like methanol, have simple structures. Others, like amino acids, are more complex. Together, these carbon-containing, or organic, compounds form the basis for biomolecules, like proteins and nucleic acids, that interact to produce life.  

Samples returned from space rocks in our neighborhood strongly support the idea that they transported such molecules within the solar system. For instance, fragments from the solar system asteroid Bennu obtained during NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission contain all five nucleotide bases, the building blocks of nucleic acids. Matthew Belyakov, a postdoctoral researcher in planetary science at Caltech, noted that the Bennu samples also contained 14 of the 20 amino acids that form naturally on Earth. 

3I/ATLAS, in its nearest close-up, taken by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter. Observations with space- and ground-based telescopes have found that the comet contains tons of organic molecules. But what does this mean for the prospect of life elsewhere in our galaxy? (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona)

Inferences about such deliveries are possible only because the rocks are like time capsules: They emerge from the same swirling disk of gas and dust from which planets are born, and the chemical compositions of asteroids and comets don't change much after that. So, by studying space rocks that originate in other exoplanetary systems, "we can learn if they also contain the building blocks of life and could have helped to start life in exoplanetary systems," Seligman said.

Simulations suggest that comets that circle one planet before moving to another could similarly deliver such prebiotic molecules to baby exoplanets. However, there was no supporting observational data to back up this claim. 

A chemical potpourri

To figure out which chemicals 3I/ATLAS contains, astronomers have been recording the comet's light intensity across a range of frequencies, using more than a dozen instruments on Earth and around the solar system. This was possible because the comet spewed tons of gas and dust to create a fuzzy bright halo, or coma, after the sun warmed it. Observations of this coma have turned up an eclectic group of chemicals essential for life as we know it.

One is hydrogen cyanide (HCN), which was detected by the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA). Despite its notorious reputation as a poisonous gas, HCN is important for creating life. A commentary noted that laboratory experiments dating back to the 1950s — including the famous Miller-Urey experiment, which attempted to recreate the conditions of primordial Earth — have found that HCN is involved in building molecules like amino acids. 

The list of ingredients goes on. ALMA data also revealed that 3I/ATLAS released gigantic amounts of formaldehyde and methanol. Additionally, observations from the James Webb Space Telescope showed 3I/ATLAS spewing the greenhouse gas methane. This is important because, assuming the methane formed on planets in the comet's home system, it could have trapped heat on those planets, thus warming them and making them more hospitable to life. 

Unlike other interstellar comets, 3I/ATLAS is rich in organic compounds, which NASA's SPHEREx telescope detected in early 2026.  (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech)

The presence of all these molecules is significant, Cordiner said, because they are "heavily implicated in terrestrial prebiotic chemistry studies as key carbon and nitrogen feedstocks [raw materials] for helping build life's molecular precursors," he said. 3I/ATLAS is proof that these "feedstocks" also exist in pastures far beyond our solar system's fences.

These findings are especially important because astronomers couldn't study the previous two interstellar objects to the same extent, Seligman said. He noted that 1I/'Oumuamua, the first interstellar object ever detected in the solar system, was observable for only a few weeks. 

"The second interstellar comet 2I/Borisov was discovered right before COVID, so a lot of observations were canceled because of that," Seligman added. (Cordiner noted that the few observations conducted on 2I/Borisov showed that it, too, appears to contain HCN.) In comparison, researchers had almost a year to study 3I/ATLAS with telescopes. These observations have shown that "3I/ATLAS is unique in terms of the *measured* chemical inventory," Cordiner said.

Not indicative of life

All of the chemicals that 3I/ATLAS appears to possess give us data about just one planetary system. But when combined with observations of other astronomical phenomena, 3I/ATLAS shows that the chemical building blocks of life are abundant across our galaxy. For instance, giant molecular clouds — dense regions of gas and dust that give rise to stars — contain nitriles and sugar acids that can form amino acids. The stuff of life, it seems, is plentiful in space.

James Webb telescope observations showed that 3I/ATLAS has a lot of methane. If its home system's planets contained similar amounts of methane, they may have warmed sufficiently to support liquid water and, possibly, life.  (Image credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, M. Belyakov (Caltech), I. Wong (STScI), Image Processing: A. Pagan (STScI))

Related stories

Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS is rapidly moving away from us. Can we 'intercept' it before it leaves us forever?

The hunt for extraterrestrial life is fundamentally flawed. But there's a fix.

'I have no doubt that life is out there': Why radio astronomers are convinced alien contact is only a matter of time

Ingredients aside, these findings don't prove that life itself has developed in 3I/ATLAS' home system (or anywhere else). All of the organic molecules that 3I/ATLAS appears to contain have simple chemical structures. Cordiner said mixtures of such molecules in the lab have transformed into more complex ones via processes like ice irradiation. However, such compounds have not been found on 3I/ATLAS, despite the billions of years the comet likely spent exposed to the unabated radiation of interstellar space.  

Most of the chemicals 3I/ATLAS released while zipping past the sun come from the comet's radiation-exposed upper layers and not from its pristine interior, a January study found. This would mean that what astronomers have measured may not be present in the comet's home system.

Nonetheless, many astronomers, including Seligman's group, are continuing to study 3I/ATLAS' composition. There is also the exciting possibility of future interstellar visitors, which are all but guaranteed to make an appearance, thanks to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile, which is expected to spot dozens more. The elements and isotopes found in these objects will help in "building a map of where bio-precursors reside, across the history of the Galaxy," Cordiner said.

text:
A few thoughts after reading hundreds of replies to this.

I love FSD. I’ve driven 10,000+ km using it. But loving a technology doesn’t mean defending every mistake it makes.

We cannot know whether FSD would have aborted here because Troy intervened less than a second after the oncoming car became clearly visible. That’s exactly what a supervising driver should do. At ~100 km/h you don’t gamble your life to prove the software would have saved you.

My concern is what happened before that: FSD initiated the overtake while a substantial part of the opposing lane was occluded.

And “humans make the same mistake” is a terrible defence. Autonomy has to become better than humans, not reproduce our mistakes.

This isn’t theoretical either. Fatal crashes have occurred with Tesla driver-assistance engaged, and NHTSA is actively investigating FSD behaviour including vehicles entering opposing lanes. The public data unfortunately doesn’t give us a clean, reliable FSD-only death total.

Meanwhile, look at what’s happening in China. BYD now offers to cover economic losses from legally liable crashes while its qualifying God’s Eye Urban NOA is being used correctly. That’s a manufacturer putting some financial skin in the game.

XPeng is taking another interesting path. VLA 2.0 Ultra hardware runs 2,250 TOPS, alongside a multi-view predictive world-model architecture designed to model how scenes evolve and what may happen next. Its wider camera viewpoints can also help reduce some of the occlusion problem we’re discussing here.

I own zero Tesla shares and have no plans on buying any. I’m interested in whoever builds the safest and best autonomy, not defending a logo.

FSD is extraordinary technology. It is also supervised for a reason.

We should be able to hold both thoughts in our heads at the same time.

text:
Unfortunately this appears inaccurate? Not finding anything on a bankruptcy ruling I finally asked Grok~
There’s a lot more in what was said, but I’ll offer this and suggest you ask for yourself. 

That claim is not true.
A federal bankruptcy court has not ruled that Kamala Harris is personally on the hook for $39 million in campaign debt.
What’s actually on the record:
The $39 million figure is the wrong number, applied to the wrong year.
Her 2019 Democratic primary campaign raised about $39 million and spent about $40 million. It ended with roughly $1.1 million in unpaid vendor bills — not $39 million still outstanding. Those 2019 bills were later paid down, including with transfers from the Biden campaign after she became the running mate. That was FEC campaign-committee debt, not a personal bankruptcy judgment. 
The 2024 campaign is a different story, and still not this claim.
Harris’s 2024 operation spent on the order of $1.5 billion in about 15 weeks. Right after the election, the campaign’s CFO said there were no overdue bills as of Election Day and that the next FEC report would show no debt. That was technically true on the campaign committee’s own line. What happened next: the DNC covered about $20–22 million in leftover 2024 bills under a private “handshake” deal, and more leftover invoices kept showing up into 2025. In early 2026 the DNC also bought her email list for $6.5 million, money that went toward remaining 2024 expenses. None of that is a $39 million personal liability order from a bankruptcy judge. 
Personal liability vs. campaign debt
Under federal campaign-finance rules, leftover bills belong to the committee, not automatically to the candidate. A candidate is personally liable only in specific cases (for example, a loan she personally guaranteed). There is no public bankruptcy-court order making Harris personally responsible for $39 million.
Where the “bankruptcy court” piece likely comes from
Search hits on “Harris” + bankruptcy turn up other people (including an ERISA/fiduciary case involving a different Harris in Minnesota). That is not the former vice president’s 2024 campaign.
Bottom line: leftover 2024 bills were real and the DNC ate a large share of them. The viral version — $39 million, personally, by a federal bankruptcy court — does not match the filings or the court record..

The read for the 9:30am open: the oil scare that knocked markets down before dawn has mostly worn off, and the bond-market problem that started Wednesday has not. Asia closed hours ago, mostly lower. Japan's Nikkei 225 finished at 65,514, +495 / +0.76%, but Tokyo's broader Topix index slipped to 4,075.30, -15.84 / -0.39%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng closed at 24,761, -73 / -0.29%. The Shanghai Composite, mainland China's main index, ended at 3,888.37, -48.15 / -1.22%, right at its low of the day, with mainland exchanges shut Friday for the Mid-Autumn Festival and again October 1-7.

Oil set the rhythm after that. Brent crude (November), the global oil benchmark, is at $104.46 a barrel, +$1.38 / +1.34% from Wednesday's settlement. It touched $106.50 before dawn as talks between Washington and Tehran showed no sign of progress. It is still up on the day, but about 60% of that early jump is gone. Europe's indexes fell as oil climbed and have recovered as it slipped back.

How much of each market's overnight drop had been won back by 7:00am ET, measured from its low:

- London's index: all of it, and then some
- Frankfurt's index: about 77%
- Paris's index: about 70%
- The Dow contract: about 62%
- The Russell contract, made of smaller U.S. companies: about 59%
- The S&P 500 contract: about 45%
- The Nasdaq contract: about 38%

That order lines up with what each market is most exposed to. Germany and France import nearly all their oil, so their indexes fell hardest when oil jumped and bounced when it eased. London's index leans on oil producers, miners and banks - businesses that can live with dearer oil - and never fell far. At the bottom, the Nasdaq contract is built mostly from companies whose profits lie years ahead. Those stocks suffer most when long-term borrowing gets more expensive, because a safe government bond paying over 5% makes distant profits worth less today.

And long-term borrowing is the one thing that has not gotten cheaper since Wednesday. A Treasury yield is what Washington pays to borrow; the 10-year also anchors U.S. mortgage rates. This morning the bond market has split at about the five-year mark, in percentage points from Wednesday's close:

- Shorter loans, cheaper: 2-year 4.87%, -0.025; 5-year 5.00%, -0.005
- Longer loans, dearer: 7-year 5.056%, +0.003; 10-year 5.127%, +0.013, after touching 5.15% overnight; 30-year 5.432%, +0.030, near its highest since 2004

Wednesday's 10-year close of 5.114% was already the highest in nearly two decades. The short end tracks bets on the Federal Reserve's next few decisions, and New York Fed President John Williams gave those bets no new push in London this morning: another rate increase by year-end is "reasonable," he said, but he would not commit to the October 27-28 meeting. The long end answers a slower question - how much extra lenders want before tying up money for a decade or more while oil keeps inflation worries alive - and nothing overnight has settled it.

That split runs straight through the day's biggest test. At 1:00pm ET the Treasury sells $44B of 7-year notes, which trade at 5.056% this morning. A sale above 5% would pay the most for seven-year money since April 1993, when it paid 5.58%. Since the note returned in 2009 the high is 4.908%, in October 2023. Wednesday's $70B 5-year sale drew $2.21 of bids for every $1 on offer, the weakest demand since December 2018. A second soft sale would likely push long-term yields higher again.

The day, Eastern time:

- 8:30am: the Labor Department's first-time unemployment claims for the week ended September 19; about 201k expected, after 196k. A low count means few layoffs - and, in this market, one more reason for the Fed to keep raising rates.
- 10:00am: August new-home sales from the Census Bureau and HUD; about 615k expected at an annual pace, after 607k in July - a direct read on buyers facing mortgage rates tied to that 10-year.
- All day: Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit, with a White House dinner tonight that top U.S. tech executives will join. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has already said the trade truce now runs to January 10 instead of lapsing November 10.

The case against this read: every market on this page is above its overnight low, and the climb has not stopped. Overnight futures trade on thinner volume than the regular session, so a 0.46% gap on the S&P 500 contract can close - or double - on one headline from the Iran talks or one number at 8:30am. What would flip the verdict: the 10-year yield slipping back under Wednesday's 5.114% close before the open, which would mean the bond problem is easing too, not just the oil one. Brent back above $106.50 would put oil back in charge.

Oil made the night's trouble and has already taken most of it back. The 5% yield is America's own borrowing cost, so no market overseas can settle it for New York; a claims count at 8:30am and a 7-year sale at 1:00pm will.

Our firm has already generated returns exceeding $1 million through investments in the semiconductor and AI supply chains. The recent rebound in US AI and chip stocks further indicates that the market is reassessing the sustainability of AI-related capital expenditure.

As major technology companies continue to build out data centers, demand for components such as HBM, enterprise SSDs, MLCCs, packaging substrates, test sockets, and deposition equipment is rising in tandem.

The South Korean stock market is currently closed for the Chuseok holiday and will resume trading on September 28. Market movements in US tech stocks, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, and memory chip companies during this break are likely to be reflected in the opening prices when the Korean market reopens.

In terms of the transmission sequence along the supply chain, the first stage typically sees memory giants like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix being the first to reflect changes in AI demand and product pricing.

The second stage involves memory manufacturers increasing capital expenditure on HBM, DRAM, and NAND, thereby driving new orders for equipment suppliers such as Jusung Engineering, Wonik IPS, and Hanmi Semiconductor. The third phase involves continued growth in AI server shipments, driving demand for Samsung Electro-Mechanics’ high-end MLCCs and FC-BGA substrates, as well as recurring revenue for testing component firms like ISC and Leeno Industrial.

To determine whether this market trend will persist, we need to monitor the following indicators:

→ Whether the rebound in US AI and semiconductor stocks continues
→ Whether Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix attract net buying from foreign investors
→ Whether orders for HBM and enterprise SSDs continue to grow
→ Whether DRAM and NAND prices maintain an upward trend
→ Whether equipment manufacturers' order backlogs translate into revenue
→ Whether lead times for AI server components continue to extend

Our firm assesses that if leading semiconductor stocks rise upon the reopening of the Korean market—accompanied by a significant increase in trading volume and foreign buying—it signals that capital is reaffirming the AI ​​capital expenditure theme.

If capital flows expand beyond Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix to include Samsung Electro-Mechanics, ISC, Leeno Industrial, and Jusung Engineering, it indicates a shift in market momentum from index heavyweights to supply chain companies with tangible orders and earnings upside.

The real focus should not be on every stock associated with the AI ​​theme, but rather on companies capable of converting data center investments into orders, revenue, profits, and cash flow.

When we reviewed the programme in 1989 we found that the British aid funds that had been pledged after independence, which Zimbabwe ministers had criticised as hopelessly inadequate, had not been fully claimed. The Ministries of Land and of Finance had not asked for aid money due for work on approved projects and new proposals were not coming forward. Lynda Chalker, then Minister for Overseas Development, wrote to Zimbabwean ministers reminding them of the debts that Britain owed and promising new money when the post-independence pledges had been used. 

There was no response. This depressing lack of activity continued into the 1990’s while the political pressure built up. Amendments to the constitutional provisions for land purchase changed nothing on the ground. The practical proposals of the commission on land tenure, which might over time have revolutionised farming practices throughout rural Zimbabwe and given renewed impetus for land reform on a sustainable basis, were brushed aside. And the British side, finding little pressure from Harare, buried its head and hoped the issue had gone away. 

Shortly after I became responsible for British aid to Africa in June 1996 the Ministers for Land and for Local Government, Kumbirai Kangai and John Nkomo, arrived unexpectedly in London. They told Lynda Chalker they had come to reopen the Lancaster House settlement on land. Mugabe had, as usual, fought the recent election with grandiose promises of land transfer to be financed by Britain. They wanted the money, would stay as long as it took, and would be reporting back each evening to their President at his London hotel. 
 Three days of discussion followed, during which they were embarrassed to be given copies of the 1989 letter and surprised to discover that the UK Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind had researched the colonial Land Apportionment Acts while at law school in Salisbury in the 1960’s. He knew more than them about the historic wrongs that needed to be put right through land reform. A memorandum signed by both sides promised a fresh pledge of British aid for a renewed joint programme. It offered technical help to develop it. Back in Harare, once again, nothing happened. 
 The following year Mugabe tried again. He hoped the arrival of a Labour government would enable him to tear up the compromises he had made, but never acknowledged, eighteen years before. He wrote to Tony Blair asking for a fresh start based on the British government accepting full responsibility for buying out the white farmers and handing the land to his government to distribute as he thought fit, the position he had consistently taken. He claimed, wrongly, that a previous Labour government had offered such a deal twenty years earlier when David Owen and Andrew Young had proposed a “Zimbabwe Development Fund”. 
 Clare Short wrote a letter in reply that became famous when Mugabe read an extract to his party congress. The reference to her Irish background that he held up for scorn was intended to acknowledge that Zimbabwe is not the only place where land expropriation by the colonial power had had a negative impact on local people. Her encouragement to look forward, to work together to design a land reform programme that would meet Zimbabwe’s needs in the 21st century rather than to focus wholly on the past, was either beyond his understanding or did not suit his political aims. 
 The part of her letter he did not read out offered a fresh start, though not the free hand and unlimited budget that he wanted. She offered financial and technical assistance for an organised, Zimbabwe-led, programme of land purchase and resettlement in partnership with other donors and within the context of a British development effort now being focussed world-wide on eliminating poverty. This was not what Mugabe wanted his people to hear.

Neo Ness sat down with the Plaion team at TGS 2026 for a detailed interview about the Neo Geo AES+, covering the hardware, cartridge compatibility, input latency, the September 2027 delay and the future software lineup.

HIGHLIGHTS:

_ The console uses a custom ASIC running natively at 5V. Plaion confirms there are no voltage level shifters between the console and original NeoGeo cartridges. 

_ Cost, compatibility and the idea of creating a fixed "real console" rather than a reprogrammable FPGA system were all factors behind the decision.

_ Unlike the original AES, it can output stereo from the rear analog connector. It uses the Megadrive 2 pinout rather than the original NeoGeo cable. Plaion also plans to offer scart and component cables.

_ Plaion says no security mechanism has been implemented to prevent third-party cartridges (multicarts included) from running. However, some carts may still have compatibility issues because of timing or power requirements. The team says official AES and MVS cartridges have been extensively tested.

_ The DB15 controller interface is described as electrically equivalent to the original hardware, with no buffering or additional processing when using a wired controller.

_ For wireless, it uses 2.4 Ghz rf rather than bluetooth. The engineer estimates roughly 2 ms of additional latency from the radio link.

_ Why the console was delayed to September 2027?
Plaion says demand was far higher than originally forecast. Within weeks of pre-orders opening, they realized they would need vastly more memory chips than planned.

The cartridges were originally designed around parallel NOR flash, but Plaion says suppliers could no longer provide the required quantities because production capacity had shifted toward other high-demand markets, including AI infrastructure.
One supplier reportedly told them they could potentially take an order in January 2027, followed by another roughly 6-month manufacturing lead time.

_ Plaion initially considered converting serial flash data back into the parallel format required by the NeoGeo, but timing margins were considered too tight.

_ Instead, the CHAR and PROG ASICs inside the cartridges are being redesigned to work directly with serial flash.

_ The team also confirms that production of the first ASIC revision had already begun and had to be cancelled, resulting in a significant financial loss.

_ Plaion says the move from parallel NOR flash to serial flash will not change how the games behave.

_ The serial flash operates internally at 133 MHz, allowing the cartridge to meet the NeoGeo’s timing requirements without additional loading times.

_ The engineering team says data retention should be extremely long under normal storage conditions, with an expectation of around 100 years.
They say temperature is the main factor affecting retention, with storage around 60°C becoming a potential concern.

_ Plaion says the original plan was to announce around 15–20 games at TGS, but after the news of the 2027 delay they felt it would be inappropriate to reveal the entire lineup.

Instead, they announced Zero Wing, with another smaller announcement potentially following soon. [Data East titles revealed on 09/22]

_ Plaion confirms additional third-party deals have been made.

_ They are also talking with independent NeoGeo developers and specifically mention Gleylancer as an example of the kind of project they would like to encourage.

_ The long-term plan is to cover 4 categories:
reissues of existing NeoGeo games, enhanced versions, arcade conversions such as Zero Wing and eventually completely new Neo Geo games developed from scratch.

Rising Fuel Costs Hit Coastal Shrimpers and Fishing Fleets

Rising fuel costs are putting severe financial pressure on commercial shrimpers, deep-sea fishing trawlers, and charter boat operators across coastal communities. Marine diesel prices have experienced sharp surges, in some regions nearly doubling or jumping more than 50% within short windows to exceed $4.50 to $6.50 per gallon at waterfront docks.

Impact on Economy:  https://t.co/PlnC9kggqC

Because fuel is not an optional expense, these price spikes threaten the viability of the entire commercial fishing and charter ecosystem. Residents and visitors alike need to keep the cost of seafood in mind during temporary fuel price hike. The market pricing are controlled by many national factors.

The Fuel Crisis for Shrimpers and Deep-Sea Fishing Fleets

Proportional Expense: Fuel routinely accounts for more than 50% of total operating costs for commercial shrimpers.
Massive Fuel Capacity: Large Gulf freezer trawlers typically burn between 700 and 12,000 gallons of diesel during multi-week offshore trips. Filling a tank prior to departure can cost vessel owners anywhere from $47,000 to over $60,000 per trip in fuel alone.
Fixed Market Prices: Unlike other transportation sectors, commercial fishermen cannot instantly raise the wholesale dockside price of seafood to absorb fuel spikes.
Tying Up at Dock: Operating on razor-thin profit margins means many vessel captains are forced to leave their boats tied to the dock, as heading to sea risks losing money on every trip.

The impact of grounded fishing boats extends far beyond the vessel owners:

The Economic Multiplier: Every dollar generated by commercial fishermen creates approximately six dollars in the broader coastal economy.
Supply Chain Disruptions: When boats remain idle, local seafood processing plants, packaging facilities, dockworkers, ice houses, net makers, mechanics, and freight truck drivers suffer reduced work or layoffs.
Local Seafood Scarcity & Higher Retail Prices: Fewer trips lead to lower landings of wild-caught fish and shrimp. Coastal residents and local seafood markets face higher prices for fresh seafood, and restaurants are forced to rely more heavily on foreign imported farm-raised seafood.
Tourism and Charter Strain: High fuel surcharges increase the cost of deep-sea charter trips, which can deter recreational anglers and tourists, harming coastal hotels, restaurants, and retail shops.

RELATED ARTICLE:  Does Your Favorite Seafood Place Offer Real Gulf Shrimp?

Alabama boasts a rich maritime heritage and operates major fleets

Shrimp Vessels: Bayou La Batre alone—where approximately 85% of Alabama’s wild-caught shrimp is landed—is home to over 300 licensed fishing and shrimping vessels. Additional commercial inshore and offshore shrimping boats operate out of Coden, Bon Secour, and Gulf Shores.
Charter Fishing Fleets: Alabama’s Gulf Coast, particularly around Orange Beach and Gulf Shores, features one of the largest charter fishing fleets in the Gulf of Mexico, with more than 100 active charter boats and experienced captains.

Why Fishing and Charter Boats Rely on Diesel

Commercial fishing and deep-sea vessels predominantly use diesel engines rather than gasoline for several critical operational and safety reasons:

High Low-End Torque: Dragging heavy trawling nets through open water or pushing large, heavy hulls requires immense towing power at low engine speeds. Diesel engines generate significantly higher torque at low RPMs compared to gasoline engines.
Fuel Efficiency and Extended Range: Diesel engines offer 20% to 30% greater thermal and fuel efficiency than gasoline engines. Because diesel fuel has a higher energy density per gallon, vessels can travel much farther on a single tank, expanding their range for long offshore voyages.
Safety at Sea: Gasoline produces volatile vapors with a flashpoint of -40°F, creating a severe explosion risk in enclosed engine compartments. Diesel fuel has a much higher flashpoint (between 126°F and 205°F), making it far less flammable and much safer for vessels operating far offshore.
Engine Longevity & Reliability: Commercial marine diesel engines are engineered for continuous, heavy-duty operation. A well-maintained marine diesel engine typically lasts 5,000 to 8,000+ operating hours before requiring a major overhaul, compared to 1,500 to 2,000 hours for a marine gasoline engine.
Reduced Maintenance Intervals: Diesel engines require less frequent routine servicing (e.g., 200 hours between services versus 100 hours for gas outboards), decreasing costly downtime for commercial crews.

Beyond the technical and economic metrics lies a essential truth: commercial fishing and charter fleets are the backbone of coastal identity and livelihood. For generations, these independent operators and working-waterfront families have fed our communities, sustained local businesses, and anchored the cultural heritage of the Gulf Coast.

Supporting local watermen—by purchasing domestic wild-caught seafood, booking local charter trips, and backing working-waterfront initiatives—is not just an investment in seafood or recreation. It is an investment in the long-term resilience and prosperity of our entire coastal community.

On March 20, 2025, Donald Trump signed an executive order called “Stopping Waste, Fraud, and Abuse by Eliminating Information Silos.” It directed agencies to give officials chosen by the president or agency heads “full and prompt access” to unclassified government records, data, software and information systems. 

It also directed agencies to consolidate information across departments and remove rules that interfered with sharing. The order extended that demand to state program data, including information held in private databases.

Hold onto that, you’ll understand why it matters more than it seems right now. The Epstein files contained more than 3,000 search results for Informa, a British company known for publishing, research and business events. Some results are part of the word “information” but there are plenty related to the business itself. I found this company while researching another one of Epstein’s companies. Instead of what I was looking for, I found a proposed system for collecting government medical and social insurance information across China. Local centers would process the information and send copies to central warehouses. Informa would receive the exclusive right to exploit the data outside China.

Then I found the company Epstein incorporated in the United States. Financial Infomatics proposed identifying American internet users across imperfect databases. It would combine those identities with biomedical, DNA, customer, behavioral and transaction information. Approved clients could then use the combined information to predict outcomes, choose investments and apply artificial intelligence to financial decisions.

So what happened if Epstein died in 2019, but the companies, investments and intellectual property did not end with him?

Financial Infomatics later became Southern Trust which invested in AdFin with Howard Lutnick. It was also an investor in Ehud Barak’s investment company that later financed the emergency technology company now called Carbyne.

AdFin’s patent for a system that collects real-time online advertising data to predict prices, value ad space and select winning bids, was granted in 2021, two years after Epstein died. Carbyne’s emergency-response platform may give government agencies access to callers’ voice communications, text messages, live video, precise location and movement information, incident histories and AI-assisted analysis. The company continues selling this infrastructure to American governments. In March 2026, it was selected as an approved next-generation 911 vendor for local governments across the Washington, D.C., metropolitan region. The final disposition of Southern Trust’s shares, code, contracts, models and data remains unknown.

These businesses removed barriers between databases, matched people across them, turned behavior into predictions and limited the results to approved users. So what does any of this have to do with Edward Snowden? The things Snowden leaked show these functions first developing inside the government before Epstein pursued private versions of them.

What did Snowden actually show us?
After September 11, the phrase “connect the dots” became a government mandate. Agencies held information in separate offices and databases, often under different names or identifiers. The goal was to find the same person across those systems, map that person’s relationships and determine what they might do next.

Snowden’s disclosures revealed how far that work had advanced. ICREACH allowed approved analysts across multiple agencies to search communications and location information gathered from numerous databases. CRISSCROSS and PROTON connected telephone records, devices, locations, travel, visas and intelligence reports. CO TRAVELER analyzed movement and association. DISHFIRE processed text messages. Identity Intelligence combined communications, biometrics, travel records and social relationships to identify people even when names or source records did not match cleanly.

PRISM obtained communications with the compelled assistance of American internet companies. Upstream programs collected information through companies controlling the telecommunications backbone, and OAKSTAR was part of the same corporate access system. The government supplied authority, targets and money, while private companies supplied access to the infrastructure carrying the information.

Across the programs, analysts collected information from separate sources and determined which records belonged to the same person. They then mapped relationships and movement, predicted what mattered and restricted the results to be accessed only by approved users. Epstein’s private companies were designed to perform each of those steps.

Public policy was moving in that direction too. In April 2011, the Obama administration released its National Strategy for Trusted Identities in Cyberspace. It called for an online “Identity Ecosystem” that could support banking, government services, commerce and other transactions. Under the strategy, the private sector would lead, the federal government would support the effort and government would become an early adopter to stimulate demand. Seven months later, Financial Infomatics was incorporated.

I am not saying there is anything that directly links Financial Infomatics to an order from an intelligence agency. The government was nevertheless building the ability to resolve identities across enormous databases while asking private industry to create the identity system used for digital transactions. Why was Epstein creating a private company that combined both functions and added investment selection?

Why was Informa buying access to government medical data?
Before Financial Infomatics, Epstein was already advising David Stern on China Medical Data Services.

Stern called Epstein his boss and mentor. He described himself as Epstein’s soldier and repeatedly sought his approval. In February 2010, Sarah Ferguson wrote that Epstein had introduced her to Stern, who had an extensive network in China and came highly recommended by Epstein. Stern also traveled with former Prince Andrew on official trade missions to Beijing, Hong Kong and Shenzhen. He relayed Andrew’s information to Epstein and discussed using the prince’s “aura and access” in private ventures.

On March 18, 2010, Informa offered $3 million for 50.1 percent of China Medical Data Services and contemplated as much as $16 million in working capital.

An April 30 acquisition plan shows the venture being moved from a British Virgin Islands structure into Hong Kong. Informa would receive 501 of the company’s 1,000 shares, four board positions and approval rights involving data and intellectual property. One provision gave the Hong Kong company the exclusive right “to exploit the data outside China.”

The value lay in the data system. Local collection centers would connect to medical and social insurance systems, while extraction software would clean, validate and standardize the information. Language processing would help make inconsistent records usable. A Beijing processing center would send the results to a central warehouse, replicated recovery warehouses and potentially a separate warehouse selected by Informa. Later correspondence described 36 regional centers financed at $200,000 each.

The proposal defined the system, its ownership and its commercial use. It contains no evidence of how many centers opened, how many people were included or whether identifiable medical information left China. The contracts, server logs, company filings and data licenses that could answer those questions have not been released as far as I could find.

In a February 25, 2011 email, Stern told Epstein that he was completing the Informa health care deal in Beijing and proposed a strategic partnership with JPMorgan. Epstein warned that Asia Gateway, a small firm trying to connect JPMorgan with Chinese state-backed deals, could create legal or reputational problems for the bank if its conduct came under scrutiny. His solution was to place a JPMorgan lawyer, officer or accountant inside the structure. That person would provide “total transparcny, and effective oversight,” while “the chinese would see a small seperate operation.”

Epstein’s proposal would have given JPMorgan practical oversight while presenting Chinese participants with what he described as a smaller operation. Former Prince Andrew supplied official access, Stern operated the companies, Informa obtained the data rights and Epstein advised the people designing the arrangement.

By December 2011, Stern described himself as retaining 100 percent of the equity while Informa became a “normal lender” with “no voting rights, no control.” The revised terms described $3 million in cash, $16 million in loan notes carrying 10 percent interest compounded quarterly and continued financing for the regional centers.

Informa gave up its shares while retaining debt and data-related commercial rights. If a company surrenders its votes but keeps its licenses, financing and influence over the infrastructure, how much control has really disappeared?

What was Financial Infomatics built to do?
Financial Infomatics was incorporated on November 18, 2011, as the Informa relationship was being reorganized. Its application described a population scale information company under Epstein’s ownership.

The company proposed matching identities across databases that contained incomplete or inconsistent information. Once it determined which records belonged to the same person, it could combine that person’s internet activity, DNA, biomedical records, customer information, financial transactions and behavior. Its automated analysis could model disease and predict financial outcomes. It could also run what the application called financial genetic algorithms to help choose investments. The company would sell data, analysis, software and artificial intelligence to approved users.

Financial Infomatics became Southern Trust in September 2012. The following year, Epstein, Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn approved another reorganization. Assets from Epstein’s older Financial Trust business moved into Southern Financial, a subsidiary of Southern Trust. This placed the old money business and the new information company in the same corporate family.

Southern Trust later received $158 million from Leon Black for tax, estate and family office work. The United States Virgin Islands alleged that approximately 85 percent of the company’s revenue came from one source and did not appear connected to informatics or data mining. The settlement acknowledged that Epstein used Black’s money to partially fund his Virgin Islands operations. The Senate Finance Committee later said the evidence showed that Black’s payments financed Epstein’s trafficking activities. The customer contracts, technical files and complete revenue ledger needed to determine what Financial Infomatics actually built are still not public.

Epstein was proposing a private business that could identify Americans across separate databases, combine intimate information about them and predict their behavior and financial value. The results would be reserved for selected clients. A capability used to find threats across government databases could also be sold to private customers and used to select investments.

How did information become something that could be traded?
Through AdFin, Southern Trust entered a business designed to turn advertising and behavioral data into financial products. In December 2012, Southern Trust and a Cantor-affiliated vehicle invested in the same AdFin financing round. Epstein signed for Southern Trust, and Howard Lutnick signed for the Cantor side. Cantor initially invested $350,000. Southern Trust invested approximately $500,000 and later held roughly $875,000 to $889,000 in the company.

AdFin was designed to convert advertising and behavioral information into pricing indexes and financial products. Its patent describes using aggregated information to create securities, futures, options and swaps. A 2016 recapitalization converted approximately $7.3 million in debt and gave Cantor effective control over board and shareholder decisions. By January 2018, Cantor held 60.32 percent while Southern Trust retained approximately 4.5 percent. The patent process continued after Epstein died and the patent was granted to AdFin Solutions on July 20, 2021. Its current public status is expired for failure to pay fees, but the grant confirms that the company’s intellectual property survived him.

Howard Lutnick now serves as Secretary of Commerce. Emails from Ehud Barak’s political intelligence circle includes Scott Bessent and meetings arranged through Barak’s office. Bessent now serves as Treasury Secretary. His name is not tied into the Financial Infomatics application and the Informa agreements. His connection here runs through the Ergo network, which converted political developments into probabilities, sanctions analysis and market consequences for private clients.

Epstein invested through Thiel-associated funds and discussed Palantir. Palantir built commercial systems that allow government clients to connect records, identities and relationships across databases. Carbyne’s current investor page lists Thiel’s Founders Fund.

What continued after Epstein died?
By 2019, the relevant assets were already held through companies, patents, contracts, debts and equity interests that could survive their creator. Financial Infomatics had become Southern Trust. Southern Trust had moved capital into AdFin and Barak’s investment network. Cantor had gained control of AdFin and the AdFin patent remained in process until it was granted in 2021.

Carbyne is still operating and selling to government agencies. The company now says its systems process more than 250 million data points each year. Its early financing came through Barak’s investment company after Southern Trust invested in it.

Epstein’s money flowed into a company that connects people, locations and communications to public agencies, and that company continued expanding after his death. Southern Trust also held approximately 4.5 percent of AdFin in 2018. What the estate did with that interest is not public.

There is no complete public inventory of Southern Trust’s intellectual property, customer contracts, data licenses, source code or models when Epstein died. The missing inventory of what the estate inherited prevents us from following those assets.

Why does Trump’s order change how we read Epstein’s companies?
Trump’s 2025 order requires agencies to remove barriers to sharing and give presidentially designated officials access to records and software. It also directs agencies to consolidate information across departments and obtain data held in private databases.

In April 2026, the Government Accountability Office reported that one Treasury DOGE employee had access to three Bureau of the Fiscal Service payment systems and could view, copy and print the information. The employee was temporarily granted authority to create, modify and delete data in one system. Another employee transmitted unencrypted payment information outside the bureau without obtaining approval.

The government now has an official policy to eliminate information silos. Politically selected personnel have already obtained broad access to systems processing tax refunds, benefits, salaries and federal vendor payments.

Financial Infomatics was designed to identify the people represented in separate records, combine their transactions with other personal information and use automated analysis to predict outcomes. Companies such as Palantir can integrate the data, while artificial intelligence can analyze it. Emergency and communications companies can add location and real-time behavior.

World Liberty Financial applied to operate an uninsured national trust bank in January 2026 and it was approved just this month. Uninsured means the bank will not offer deposits protected by the FDIC. It will issue USD1, manage the assets backing it, process the creation and redemption of the tokens, and hold digital assets for customers. The public application identifies WLTC Holdings as the sole shareholder, but the complete ownership chart, capital structure and business plan are hidden in confidential exhibits. Zachary and Robert Witkoff are among the proposed directors.

The Senate Banking Committee’s published account says a Trump-affiliated entity controlled 60 percent of World Liberty and was entitled to 75 percent of certain revenues. A later Senate letter says a company affiliated with Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan acquired a 49 percent stake for $500 million shortly before Trump’s inauguration. Sheikh Tahnoon is the United Arab Emirates’ national security adviser and the brother of its president. USD1 was then selected for the $2 billion MGX transaction involving Binance.

Emirati state-connected capital entered the company while the Trump administration was making decisions involving Gulf investments, advanced technology and American national security.

The same group of people and investors now reaches across government information, technology that can identify and predict people, public contracts and privately issued money. Some of the people who invested in or controlled these businesses now hold the offices responsible for regulating them.

Was Epstein privatizing what the government had built?
Snowden’s disclosures revealed something relatively simple beneath all the classified program names. American intelligence agencies had built systems capable of collecting information about millions of people, determining which records belonged to the same person, mapping relationships, tracking movement and searching information gathered by different parts of the government.

At the same time, federal policy was assigning private companies a related task: building the systems people would use to prove who they were online. The government was connecting information behind the scenes while private industry was being encouraged to build the digital identification used for banking, purchases and other transactions.

There is no released evidence that the NSA gave its technology to Epstein or that he worked to develop it directly. What I do have in these documents show that Epstein and the people around him were pursuing private businesses that could perform many of the same basic functions with government and commercial information.

The proposed Informa operation in China was designed to collect, standardize and sell access to medical and insurance information. Financial Infomatics described technology that could recognize the same person across separate databases, combine the information and use it to predict behavior. AdFin was built to collect live advertising data and calculate what online attention was worth. Epstein’s investment network also included companies working in political intelligence, emergency communications and financial technology.

These businesses did not need to possess classified NSA software to be valuable. They needed access to large amounts of information, a reliable way to match that information to individual people, and programs capable of finding patterns that ordinary analysts would miss.

Epstein’s businesses added the part a government intelligence agency did not need: private ownership and private profit. A company could own the code, keep its methods secret, sell the analysis, use it to guide investments and collect revenue every time the information became a business decision.

Those companies, patents and investments could also survive Epstein, and it seems they very much did.

The companies are connected through people, money and investments, but the complete trail of technology and ownership is still missing.

Did Epstein understand that the government’s ability to identify and predict people would become far more profitable if private companies owned the programs, contracts and payment systems built around it? If so, did the investments he placed into companies that survived him allow other people to continue that work?

The difference between government and private ownership is central, and part of what the Trump administration is working overtime on. Government agencies are subject to constitutional limits, public-records laws, congressional oversight and rules governing how information may be used, even when those protections fail. A private company can call its software, methods and customer information proprietary. It can sell the company, license the technology or transfer its assets without giving the public a clear account of who now controls them.

The government may still provide the information, contracts and legal authority. The private company owns the tool built around them and profits from its use. A public function can move beyond public view without ever officially leaving the government.

The missing records could show whether that happened here.

DOGE must account for the government information it copied, where that information went and whether any private company received it. World Liberty’s confidential ownership chart and business plan should be examined with the same questions in mind.

Those records would answer three basic questions: Who inherited what Epstein left behind? Who can combine and search this information now? Who gets paid when information about a person becomes a decision about that person?

We have spent years asking what Jeffrey Epstein collected about powerful people but we never considered what he may have collected about the rest of us. Was he helping build a private system capable of collecting, identifying and assigning financial value to entire populations? If so, who controls it now?

REGIONAL SPORTS ROUNDUP
September 24, 2026

COLLEGE

NEW VIDEOBOARD FOR CFSB CENTER
Murray State Athletics has announced the Price Family Videoboard, a new center-hung display that will be installed as part of the ongoing renovation of the CFSB Center. The videoboard will be 60% larger than the current display, with four panels measuring 18.5 feet by 25.5 feet and more than 10 million pixels. Four additional underbelly displays, along with new ribbon boards and LED scorer’s tables, will enhance game presentation and fan engagement. The videoboard is named in recognition of the Price Family and its longtime support of Murray State and the Murray community.

STRIPE OUT AT UK
Kentucky football fans are being asked to participate in a "blue and white stripe out" at Kroger Field on Saturday.  UK is requesting that half of the stadium wear blue, while the other half wears white.  The Wildcats will complement the look on the field while facing South Alabama, with players dressed in the white helmet, blue jersey, blue pants combo.  An image that shows what color fans should wear by seating section is posted on the UK Football X page.

UK WARNS OF TICKET SCAMS
The University of Kentucky Police Department has shared a warning over ticket scams.  Authorities say they have gotten several reports of fraudulent offers being made through social media.  The university recommends buying tickets only through the UK ticket office, Ticketmaster or the verified resale site FEVO.  Anyone who believes they may have been the victim of a ticket scam is asked to contact UK police.

POTUS TO ATTEND VOLS GAME
President Trump is reportedly planning to attend this week's Tennessee-Texas football game.  Clay Travis' Sport-and-State reports the president will be in Knoxville on Saturday for the key SEC clash between the 13th-ranked Volunteers and number one Longhorns.  It's the latest of several sporting events the president has attended this year, but the first since the FIFA World Cup final.

HIGH SCHOOL

THURSDAY PREVIEW
In boys high school soccer tonight, Calloway County will be at Christian County. In volleyball, Marshall County visits Murray High in a key Fourth District matchup while Calloway County travels to Community Christian. 

MAYFIELD CLAIMS FORFEIT WIN
Todd County Central has canceled Friday’s scheduled football game at Mayfield, citing student safety, injuries and a shrinking number of healthy players available to compete. School officials said the decision was made to protect the well-being of the athletes and was not a reflection of their effort or commitment. Because of the cancellation, Mayfield gets a win via forfeit and has moved its Homecoming activities to October 2 when the Cardinals host Caldwell County.

PROS

CARDINALS REPORT
The Cardinals dominated the Pirates in a 5-1 last night to even their series in Pittsburgh. JJ Wetherholt tallied three hits and drove-in a run as Matthew Liberatore gave up one run on six hits over five-plus innings to earn the win. Brandon Lowe launched a solo homer for Pittsburgh's only run as the Pirates five-game winning streak was snapped. The rubber game of the series is set for 11:35 this morning with a 10:40 pregame show airtime on WNBS. 

TITANS REPORT
The Titans are gearing up for their week three matchup against the Giants.  Running backs Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears both did not participate during Wednesday's practice due to ankle soreness, according to head coach Robert Saleh.  Meanwhile, cornerback Cor'Dale Flott, dealing with a quadricep injury, and defensive lineman Solomon Thomas, battling a knee issue, were each limited in practice.  The Titans will look to avoid an 0-3 start to the season when they visit New York this Sunday.

AREA NFL REPORT
Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson is facing uncertainty at his team's most important position.  Johnson said yesterday that he doesn't know yet who will be his starting quarterback on Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles.  Starter Caleb Williams is week-to-week with a hamstring injury and backup Tyson Bagent is in concussion protocol.  Third-stringer Case Keenum took first-team reps at practice yesterday.

TNF PREVIEW
Week Three of the NFL kicks off tonight as the Packers are hosting the Falcons in their home opener on Thursday Night Football at Lambeau Field.  Green Bay is off to a 1-1 start after rallying for an overtime victory against the New York Jets.  Jordan Love hopes to improve his efficiency after completing just over 52 percent of his passes through the first two weeks.  Atlanta is still searching for its first win of the season.  Michael Penix is slated to make his first start of the year after recovering from a torn ACL.

AREA HOCKEY ROUNDUP
The NHL preseason is winding down.  The Predators wrap up the brief exhibition slate against the Hurricanes at home tonight. Also, the Blackhawks face off against the Blues in St. Louis tonight.  It's the last exhibition game of the brief preseason slate for both teams.

Senior Colonel Jiang Bin, Spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defense (MND), answered media queries on September 24.

More information is provided below:

Question: In the wake of the incident provoked by a Philippine government vessel near Xianbin Jiao of China's Nansha Qundao, the Japanese Embassy in the Philippines quickly posted on social media that it's "gravely concerned" over the "dangerous actions" by China, and portrayed itself as "upholding the rule of law and opposing any actions which increase tensions". What is your comment on this?

Jiang Bin: It's clear and evident that the Philippine government vessel made provocations near Xianbin Jiao and deliberately rammed a China Coast Guard vessel. Though Japan is a country outside the South China Sea region, it has actively joined the Philippine side in distorting the truth. Its real intention is to make waves in the South China Sea and fish in muddy waters. The Chinese side firmly opposes this behavior. The Japanese side has been strengthening its collusion with the Philippines by providing weapons and sending troops to the Philippines for joint exercises, during which it launched offensive missiles overseas for the first time. The Japanese side is attempting to break away from the post-war international order and revive its old dream of military expansion. This is a real threat to regional peace and stability. We urge the Japanese side to offer a clear explanation of its accelerating "remilitarization" efforts, and stop sowing discord and undermining peace and stability in the South China Sea.

text:
I wake up and he is screaming hard from his jholi tied to the cot, and Selma is standing beside looking at him in her white dupatta all dressed to go to the school. I gather him out of the jholi and she picks him up, puts him to her chest, kisses his brownish looking thin hair, and hands him over to me, and he looks back at her with his wide arms expecting her to take him alongside, and she feels sad for a moment before I ask her to leave immediately, which she does, and I call her from behind asking I can put him in the highchair and drop you off at the school, which she declines, saying noah is crying today, so it isn't a good idea. I wave my hand and she turns away towards the gate and noah, screaming, looks at her from behind with tears dropping from his tiny beautiful eyes.

“You are going to be extremely fine, my sunshine,” I call him, but he's just not listening, and I fix him in my arm and go to the next room to pick a diaper, and I put him on the cot, and he's screaming loud with an occasional sob, and I sense that his pants is wet, and the diaper when I open it is totally wet. “Molfix is somewhat good,” I think and he waves his legs at me and on the cot, all confused and grey.
I put a new diaper under his legs and use wet tissues to soak up the insides of his thighs, while he goes out of breath crying hard. “It isn't the fever, he's just hungry,” I conclude, and leave him to beat the cot with his tiny beautiful feet, and bring him a new dress. I help his legs in the pants, and he's still crying with the same intensity, which, if one feels, actually intensifies with every second, and but I have to keep a calm face and occasionally call his name to gather his attention and break the continuous, shrilling, burst of chilling baby cry that goes out into the void with a sharp pitch.
His cheeks are wet with tears, and he's been drooling a lot for the past week as there has been sighting of two beautiful moon-looking teeth, and it's the background of his fussiness, and fever and all.

I button up his shirt and force his arms in, and he's curving and pushing and trying out of my hands and I offer him many small things that otherwise would have caught his attention and could have been the reason for his distraction, but today isn't that day.

It's been a week since he's got some viral or bacterial contact from his mother's school and the pediatricians, from different cities, have been unable to diagnose which is it, a viral or bacterial contact, and so both suggested completely different syrups and none of it worked, and I'm pissed off at myself and everyone who is going to talk to me in the next few days.

I set him in the low cot and go out and throw his diaper in the bin and come back to see him crying even harder, and I pick him up to the sink and soap my hands and then his and wash over his face all the drool and the tears, and keep him in the nook of my arm and open the Nestle water bottle and pour six ounces in the feeder, and throw in equal number of powder milk, and shake it up as we both come back to the bedroom, and I lay him down and fix the bottle up to his mouth and he grabs it sharply.

“Oh, shit, I have been thinking he's got fever, and gum swell, and all, but all he is, is hungry, and what a stupid shit I just did, I could have avoided all that screaming had I given him milk first, and the diaper could have been changed later,” I am thinking this all to myself, and he's drinking it ever so fast.

Once he's satisfied, we go to the kitchen again to wash our feeder and I see his boiled egg sitting there on the shelf and I know he won't eat it because he doesn't like it anymore since he's growing the tiny white moons he probably thinks everything he eats isn't going to be swallowable, and so he gags it out, and the sad looking boiled egg sits there, untouched, but his mum still doesn't believe and thinks he might just take a couple of spoons mixed into the banana puree and so she always boils it when she wakes up only for it to be eaten by us in the afternoon.

I lay him down on the cot which he doesn't like anymore since he's grown up and started crawling and all, and I hurry myself to the medicine box and pouch out two syrups, one is supposed to calm his coughing which hasn't worked since this past week, and the other is curing his fever which is just as poor, and I sometimes wonder what the fucking shit they put in the medicine and how guttering the quality of these medicines is even though they fucking know that these are being prepared for the goddamn kids and infants and the newborns.

I place him in his highchair and wheel it to the kitchen for the third time and now I will brew my cup of tea and he will see me do it. He likes to look at things if they are new and out of ordinary activity. I burn the stove, and he looks at the pale fire and the jumping flames make him see it more cautiously, which he does so, and we leave the kitchen and sit on the rug and he crawls about and I finish my breakfast and put the tray up on the table. He nears me, and puts his head in my lap and stills himself, and I straighten his hair, and look at his majestic, magical, looking eyes that when they dip it looks like the darkness is all there is, and when he opens them it feels like the inch long pupils can shelter a lot of the sun-drying mass under them. I gather him up and look at his face and he grinds his teeth and puts all the force he has on his gums, and looks at me in the eye with no thought.

I pick my phone from the desktop and make a call to the nearest hospital in the city, 50kms away.

“Hello, this is Arusha from GMK hospital, how may I help you?” she says as if she has said that numerous times this morning, this week.

I sense she must be wearing a black shirt. “I am Ali, my son is sick, and he's just nine months, and I need him checked earliest if you could, only if, find me a spot early, I could bring him up there in an hour,” I smoothly roll out my sentences hoping it would make an impact on her conscience.

“03:30pm is the earliest I can fix you,” she replies, and her voice comes out as if someone has a foot on her throat, and she hangs up on me.

ah, what a lovely bitch, I think of her to be; what a gorgeous stupid shit piece of a senseless, soulless, dry sounding log she is, I rethink my first thought.

I sit down, grab noah up in my arms and he wraps himself around me as a frog, in hot summer, drops her belly down on the wet mud and spreads her limbs out, and he then sideways puts his tiny rounded face on my shoulder and looks away into the corner of the room.

I take him out on the porch and we sit on the chair and look at the bottlebrush and the birds. He sits quietly and looks at everything and rocks back and forth, and starts humming. Ah, that's all it takes for him to get over this all.

text:
Homily Thursday, September 24, 2026: Where do we look when life feels endless, repetitive, and empty, and how does Jesus change everything?

Readings: (1) Ecclesiastes 1: 2-11 (2) Luke 9: 7-9

My dear brothers and sisters,

On this Thursday of the Twenty-Fifth Week in Ordinary Time, God’s word asks us to look closely at what gives our lives real purpose.

In our first reading from Ecclesiastes, we hear a honest reflection on the sheer fatigue of daily life. The sun rises, the sun sets, the wind blows in circles, and generation after generation passes away. We wake up, answer emails, do chores, pay bills, go to sleep, and do it all over again tomorrow. If this earth is all there is, it’s easy to feel like we’re running on a treadmill that goes nowhere—that everything we chase under the sun just fades away.

In the Gospel, we see what happens when someone looks at the divine through the wrong lens. Herod hears about Jesus and becomes fascinated. But Herod isn't looking for a Savior; he’s looking for entertainment or a quiet conscience after executing John the Baptist. He treats Jesus as just another novelty—another thing "under the sun" to satisfy his idle curiosity. Because he approaches Jesus on his own terms, he misses Him completely.

It’s easy for us to fall into the same trap. We feel the emptiness that Ecclesiastes describes, so we try to fill it with temporary things—promotions, new gadgets, social media validation, or constant busyness. But temporary things can never satisfy an eternal soul. When we expect the world to give us ultimate joy, we set ourselves up for burnout.

Ecclesiastes says there is "nothing new under the sun." But Jesus did not come from under the sun—He came down from Heaven into our world to make all things new. He steps into our daily, repetitive routines and fills them with eternal value. When we offer our everyday tasks to Him, brushing our teeth, driving to work, or caring for a family member ceases to be empty routine. It becomes an act of love.

Saints throughout history discovered this secret. They left behind comfortable lives and faced immense trials, yet they possessed a joy the world couldn't destroy because their hearts were fixed on Christ.

We aren't just passing time. We have a mission: to know God, to love Him, and to bring His life into this world. As we receive the Eucharist today, let’s ask the Lord to heal our restless hearts, pull us out of empty pursuits, and fix our eyes on Jesus, who alone makes our lives complete.

Lord Jesus, thank you for giving us true hope. Deliver us from empty pursuits and center our daily lives on your love. Grant us the grace to seek you not out of mere curiosity, but with wholehearted faith. Amen.

THE WEEK

BOTTOM LINE

Japan is reaching for the sword again
Tomahawks are arriving, hypersonic missiles are in development, and nuclear submarines are under consideration. How far will Tokyo’s military buildup go?
Published 23 Sep, 2026 13:27
https://t.co/gCTcKXUMFb
By Dmitry Kornev, military expert, founder and author of the MilitaryRussia project
-------
In recent months, there’s been a distinct sense of ‘historical déjà vu’ – from Germany’s interest in long-range missiles to the development of hypersonic missile technologies in Japan. The first question that comes to mind is whether revanchism is emerging more than 80 years after the defeat of the fascists and militarists in WWII. However, this question is quite complicated, so for now, we will focus on a more practical issue: Japan’s military-technical buildup. Below, we will attempt to assess the significance of this shift in Japan’s strike capabilities and understand the direction in which the country is heading.
By the end of the 20th century, Japan had become one of the strongest and most loyal allies of the US in the Pacific region. The Japan Self-Defense Forces are equipped with American aircraft, missiles, interceptors, and other weapons. Japan is the first and to date the only country in the world to manufacture Patriot surface-to-air missiles under license, and it is the first foreign recipient of Tomahawk subsonic cruise missiles.
On July 29, 2026, the first test launches of Tomahawk cruise missiles were conducted in the Pacific Ocean from the Kongo-class guided-missile destroyer JS Chokai, equipped with the Aegis system. These tests mark the beginning of the Japanese Navy’s adoption of American long-range cruise missiles. The program to acquire these missiles is quite ambitious: Japan plans to equip four additional Aegis-capable destroyers – JS Kirishima, JS Haguro, JS Myoko, and JS Atago—with these state-of-the-art missiles, with the long-term goal of upgrading all other destroyers of this class. In total, the acquisition of 400 missiles (Block IV and Block V variants) is planned by the end of the 2027 fiscal year. This arsenal significantly alters the capabilities of the Japanese Navy, given that such cruise missiles can strike targets at ranges of up to 1,600 km. Furthermore, this is merely an interim solution pending the adoption of domestically developed missiles with similar or superior specifications.
Japan is currently working on several missile projects, with a particular focus on hypersonic technologies. Japan has already concluded an agreement with Australia to conduct joint tests at Australian missile ranges, which offer the necessary facilities for testing long-range missiles; the development of several strike missile projects is scheduled to begin in 2027.
One of the major initiatives is the project to develop a submarine-launched hypersonic missile capable of striking land-based targets. The missile is expected to be versatile, capable of being deployed from both Japanese Navy submarines and surface ships. Japan justifies the deployment of such missiles on submarines by citing the need for retaliatory strike capabilities in the event of an external attack. Naturally, Japan is pointing to the growing capabilities of China’s navy and missile forces. For its part, China is also actively enhancing its capabilities in light of a possible confrontation with the US and Japan.
While the hypersonic missile project is currently in the preliminary design phase, it draws upon Japan’s existing experience in developing various types of missiles and submarine-based vertical launch systems, as well as ambitious programs to build new missile-equipped vessels and, eventually, nuclear-powered submarines. In 2023, the Japanese Ministry of Defense signed a contract with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries for the development of a submarine-launched guided missile; a separate official program launched that same year is focused on developing an indigenous hypersonic guided missile; the work is set to continue through 2031. These programs are essentially aimed at creating preliminary designs for future missiles and developing hypersonic technologies in general; however, following the research phase, Japan will move on to developing specific missile models. text:
It’s a pretty gloomy start this morning under mostly cloudy skies, with even a few patches of light fog and drizzle hanging around. These clouds have been VERY stubborn over the past 24 hours, and they’re not going to disappear immediately today either. We should eventually begin seeing some decreasing cloud cover this afternoon, with highs reaching the mid to upper 70s. Quite the contrast to this time last week when we were talking about highs in the upper 90s and lower 100s...

So, why have these clouds been so persistent? Behind our cold front, a shallow layer of cool, moist air has remained trapped near the surface. At the same time, slightly warmer and drier air above us has basically acted like a lid, preventing that low-level moisture from mixing out very quickly. That’s a great recipe for stubborn low clouds. As we get a little more daytime heating and the atmosphere slowly mixes out, those clouds should finally begin breaking apart.

From there, we’ll SLOWLY warm things back up over the next few days, with highs generally in the low to mid 80s through the weekend. The good news? Drier air settling into the region, combined with better radiational cooling at night, should give us an opportunity for some pretty chilly morning temperatures. Saturday morning especially could feature low temps in the upper 40s and lower 50s across parts of Southern Middle Tennessee. WOOHOO!

The warming trend continues into early next week, with highs climbing into the upper 80s and potentially approaching 90° by Tuesday. Now, before you show up at my office with pitchforks and torches, kindly remember that 90° with lower humidity is still going to feel MUCH better than the near-100° temperatures and oppressive humidity we dealt with over the past month. DON’T SHOOT THE MESSENGER!

There is also some encouraging news farther down the road... The latest longer-range guidance has become a little more robust with rain chances toward the middle and latter part of next week as another cold front approaches the region. Exact timing is still far from being locked down, but rain chances currently look like they could increase around Wednesday and Thursday. This will be something we can have a much deeper conversation about early next week once the timing and details become clearer.

For now, I’m cautiously hopeful that at least SOME of us can pick up some rainfall. And yes, I’m aware that just yesterday I said the next seven days would likely stay mostly dry. That’s still true! We should remain mostly dry through next Tuesday BEFORE rain chances begin increasing toward the middle of next week.

So, no contradiction here. The potential rain we’re watching is just beyond that original seven-day window. And if nothing else, this next cold front should help keep temperatures from getting too carried away above 90° again!
