text:
- Week 2 Recap - 

Lions
Drew Petzing worries me a bit as a play caller. Predictable at times with his tendencies (LOVES to run on 2nd & long) Pass game concepts are a bit too middle field heavy - that tendency may break once their offensive line solidifies. Jameson Williams should have better outings in the near future as well.

Bills
Dalton Kincaid is the pass catcher to own rest of season. This is the best I’ve seen him look since his Utah days - I had him as a Pro-Bowl caliber prospect coming out, he may live up to that if his PCL holds up.

Panthers
Coker & McMillan are becoming a reliable duo for Bryce Young, who is continuing to improve as a passer. Chuba Hubbard has value as a reliable RB2 with Jonathon Brooks dealing with the same injury he dealt with in camp, which now needs surgical intervention.

Bucs
Baker Mayfield is playing uneven ball through two weeks - he’ll hopefully get back to a solid level of play soon. Bucky Irving continues to look fantastic, if he stays healthy he is going to be the nucleus of the Bucs offense. They should not pitch count him. The playmakers have been troubling as Emeka Egbuka hasn’t taken the step everyone thought he would or at least getting back to the trajectory he was on before his hamstring injury last Fall, Ted Hurst may continue to see more opportunities & be moved around as he gains trust. Jalen McMillan coming back from injury will help open up throwing lanes underneath & give Mayfield a reliable level three option.

Browns
Concerned the most with Quinshon Judkins, the Browns offensive line hasn’t done him any favors & you also have to question whether or not he was rushed back from the Fibula fracture & ankle dislocation he suffered in December. KC Concepcion is most “idiot proof” of the bunch of receivers - Denzel Boston has good standing with Watson & looks the part, may be more volatile once they face higher end perimeter corners.

Vikings
The offense is going to run through Justin Jefferson even more than it has been with the injuries to their running back room. We haven’t seen much with Kyler Murray under center, but can anticipate heavy doses of Jefferson.

Bears
No concern about the Bears playmakers - all we are hearing is about how uninvolved Burden, Odunze, and Loveland have been, but the sample size is way to unique to draw conclusions. They ran for 291 yards & 6 touchdowns week 1 & played in a downpour with 20mph winds in week 2 where completing a forward pass was a pleasant surprise. Caleb Williams projects to miss time with a likely week 5 return & that is when I project the passing offense will begin to click. Buy Loveland & Burden in dynasty.

Falcons
They’ll be in Quarterback territory next Spring with plenty of draftable options in the upcoming class . Even if Penix returns to form quickly, I don’t see their play elevating into a tier two offense. Bijan Robinson’s ceiling goes up & Drake London returns to the WR2 conversation.

Bengals
Chase Brown is a nice buy low after a slow start through two weeks. Tee Higgins is benefiting from schematic changes - touchdowns will come. Mike Gesicki is a sneaky add in TE premium with Iosivas on IR.

Steelers
DK Metcalf has underperformed & is reaching the age apex for his archetype, Roman Wilson is an afterthought, Michael Pittman Jr. is currently battling an undisclosed foot injury and Pat Freiermuth is still a league-average tight end. Germie Bernard saw a massive snap increase from 4% to 79%, and looked good in his opportunities. He’s the easiest to get the ball to out of the pass catchers & their only post catch creator.

Texans
Even when Nico Collins returns, this offense is going to struggle to score points at times. Dalton Schultz is a safe floor-to-ceiling flex play in the meantime, their offensive line needs more time to gel before a rushing attack can be sustained.

Broncos
Will be interesting to see what their running back rotation looks like with all three dealing with some sort of ailment - could be a three-headed monster when all are healthy. Jaylen Waddle had a breakout performance & Pat Bryant is someone to keep an eye on, as he could be a long-term secondary option in Denver when Courtland Sutton leaves.

Jacksonville
Travis Hunter’s usage is likely due to a ramp-up from the LCL procedure he had last Winter, I don’t expect him to be fantasy relevant, but I do expect him to push Brian Thomas Jr. for snaps if he continues to struggle securing passes. Bhayshul Tuten needs to be receiving 75% + snaps moving forward - he looks markedly better than Rodriguez Jr., who should be used situationally in goal-line & short-yardage scenarios.

Chargers
There is a lot wrong. Omarion Hampton is a gap-based runner with an outside zone-based scheme being forced upon him. Would like them to diversify the run scheme a bit while also adding in touches for Keaton Mitchell. Justin Herbert is being asked to do too much post snap - has always been a great thrower, but is a below-average “Quarterback,” and that is showing up through the first couple of weeks.

Raiders
Ashton Jeanty is getting his sealegs back underneath him & his heavily involved as both a runner & receiver - getting Brock Bowers back will help his efficiency. Tre Tucker is going to benefit as well from Bowers return as well as taking pressure off of Bowers himself.

Dolphins
Bobby Slowik & Kevin Patullo are making the Dolphins offense unwatchable. Lacking the playmakers is one thing, but the understanding of how to properly utilize your personnel is another. First week it was the lack of De’Von Achane involvement, and in week two we saw another game of little to no designed runs with Malik Willis. When evaluating Willis out of Liberty the biggest impact he could have on your run game was how good of a decision maker he is in zone reads. This is a struggling offense that neglects to adapt to the strength of their players.

Jets
Adonai Mitchell has been a nice surprise & may have found the consistency that has been plaguing him throughout his young career. Breece Hall looks more explosive than last year - like this offense more than I anticipated .

Packers
Another injury upfront combined with Jayden Reed’s potential season-ending absence is a difficult combination. Tucker Kraft likely sees a bump in underneath utilization, with a greater role in store for Matthew Golden.. who is their best three-level receiver. *pounds table again*

Saints
No idea what this backfield will look like week to week with Kamara healthy - Etienne isn’t getting the volume everyone anticipated after getting paid. Vele is turning into a nice secondary piece, especially with Tyler Shough’s improvements.

Ravens
With Zay Flowers, this is a top four offense in football. Without… it’s a bit difficult to find consistency. May have to lean more on Lamar in the run game to get on track if Flowers misses more time. Rashod Bateman has a solid floor in Flowers absence.

Eagles
Jalen Hurts looks comfortable in Sean Mannion’s system & DeVonta Smith looks like a Superstar as the WR1. Dontayvion Wicks has been a pleasant surprise & he looks to have cleaned up the drops that plagued him in Green Bay - will likely pick up a higher Redzone share with Goedert out for the near future.

Titans
Again, Daboll needs to start giving Carnell Tate more layups & getting Cam Ward comfortable getting the ball out quick. Both Running Back’s are dealing with ailments, Nick Singleton could have some value down the road if he can get acclimated to the speed of the NFL game.

49ers
Will be interesting to see who steps up next in wake of another injury to their core of receivers. Jacob Cowing is a fun name who is a legitimate field stretcher that can help George Kittle & Mike Evans operate underneath. Jordan Watkins should see opportunity as well.

Seahawks
The offense flows through JSN - if healthy, Jadarian Price will continue to improve. Sam Darnold is a huge boost to their overall efficiency & may get Rasheed Shaheed going.

Cardinals
Jeremiyah Love’s involvement will see an uptick, likely similarly to Jahmyr Gibbs during his Rookie year in Detroit who didn’t see consistent volume until around week 5. Marvin Harrison Jr. looks disinterested from down to down - a change of scenery may be best if this continues.

Commanders
There isn’t much to say other than there is not much this offense will produce without Jayden Daniels. Antonio Williams is an incredible buy low candidate.

Colts
Josh Downs should see an uptick in overall targets & level three opportunities. I would like to see Tyler Warren to see more involvement as an intermediate route runner - right now, Steichen is utilizing him as a delay/flat/screen based option. Not going to work if their offense is going to get on track consistently.

Chiefs
Surprisingly enough, Xavier Worthy got a lot of the “layup looks” that Rashee Rice received during Nagy’s tenure as Offensive Coordinator - Worthy doesn’t offer the play strength that Rice does, and if he doesn’t prove effective, they could look at either giving Rice back that role… or inserting Cyrus Allen (finally). Patrick Mahomes is benefiting from Kenneth Walker & had a career-high 14 completions on play action this past week - love to see this as Mahomes grows comfortable off of the ACL.

Giants
Jaxson Dart’s injury pushes this whole offense down - Malik Nabers doesn’t look like himself. Matt Nagy is going with a three-headed monster at Running Back for whatever reason when Cam Skattebo is their best offensive player, currently. Rough.

Rams
DeVante Adams had a nice throwback game, and is aging gracefully, as is Matthew Stafford. Blake Corum looks markedly better than Kyren Williams again. Terrance Ferguson is in line for nice floor weeks with Puka Nacua nursing a hip injury.

text:
What happens when more of the world’s markets move on chain and become directly accessible to software?

AI can research, allocate and execute. Crypto provides programmable settlement. Stablecoins already settle about $35 trillion a year, and estimates put their value at $2 to $4 trillion by 2030. Tokenised assets could be much larger. McKinsey estimates $2 trillion by 2030, while BCG’s base case is $14 trillion. The exact number matters less than the direction. More equities, bonds, commodities and funds are becoming accessible to software, on chain and around the clock.

Vaunt is being built for that transition. Today it learns in crypto and perpetual markets, where automated execution and 24 hour trading already exist. Every new asset that moves onto similar infrastructure expands the market the same underlying system can potentially trade.

We now have 70 days of live capital behind the idea. Since July 17, the real money account has grown about 0.23% a day with a 66% win rate across 2,577 trades and several strategies.

What matters more is what happens underneath. Every trade is stamped with the market conditions it entered in and graded against what happened next. Over the last 28 days, the two largest lanes averaged +1.1% and +0.9% per trade. Their strongest cohorts have exceeded 1.5%. A replay of nearly 1,000 positions identified an add rule worth another 0.36 percentage points per trade, with a t statistic above 8. It is now being tested live before it earns more capital. Strategies that stop working are cut to probe size within days. Strategies that continue proving an edge get more.

That loop is the important part. Measure the edge. Test it with live capital. Move money toward what continues to work and away from what does not. Then carry the same process into each new market as it comes on chain.

For users, the offer is simple. A small group gets access to a system that is continuously learning these markets without having to build the data, research and execution stack themselves. For Vaunt, the opportunity extends beyond a trading subscription into infrastructure: decision APIs, agent access and automated execution across a growing universe of markets.

We just passed September 10, the statistical peak of Atlantic hurricane season. This is the part of owning on the Gulf that never makes the brochure.

In Florida, your hurricane deductible can be a percentage of your dwelling coverage, not a flat dollar amount. The choices insurers have to offer are $500, 2%, 5% or 10%.

On $300,000 of coverage, 2% is $6,000 out of your pocket before the policy pays a dime. 5% is $15,000.

So before I help anybody buy a beach place, I want three numbers written down: that deductible in dollars, the cash in reserve to cover it, and what the HOA's master policy leaves on the owner if it's a condo.

If those numbers scare you, that's not a no. That's the budget.

Owners: do you know your hurricane deductible in dollars without looking?

text:
Nobody Walks To The Ring. 

Last week I published my numbers. 80 users, 3 paid subscribers, one of them me. Kill criteria written in public. 30-day clock running. 

This week I shipped nothing. No new subs. The offer platform is still being designed. I showed a friend around Texas.

But something happened that matters more than anything I could have built. A few people found @rayadotai . They looked at it. They told me the logic is sound. They told me they believe it works. 

Then they told me why they won't use it. 

Using it means admitting the future they spent their entire lives preparing for is no longer relevant. 

So they chose not to acknowledge it exists. 

I've seen this before. Ten years ago I offered to walk everyone I knew into blockchain and decentralized networks. Most people used me for information, laughed, and never joined. Almost all of them have since told me I was right. 

Same pattern. The fear is accurate. The avoidance is not. Same people who believe it works but cannot act on it. 

The only difference is the technology. The timeline is faster. 

Here's what I learned this week that no feature launch could have taught me:

The bottleneck isn't the product. It's the moment before someone walks through the door. The moment where they have to admit the world they planned for is not the world they're in. That admission is the real cost of entry. Not the subscription. The admission. 

And here's the part that stings: 

Some of the people who said no are friends and family. One of them asked me, "If you have something that works, why pressure others to use it?" 

They're right. The system works with or without a community. But I didn't reach out because I need them. I reached out because I wanted to explore the future together. 

That was the mistake. The correct approach was never to explain. It was to show. A record, not an argument. 

So I'm going back to building. 

My path is open now. It's mine to walk first, in public. Yours is open too. What that looks like is for you to decide.

text:
Lowe's has added drone delivery to its fulfillment mix, launching a pilot that can bring select home improvement products to customers near Matthews, N.C., in as fast as 20 minutes.

The service, announced September 24, 2026, is aimed at both DIY shoppers and Pro customers. It builds on drone operations already run by Wing and DoorDash in the Charlotte area, while giving Lowe's a new way to handle small, time-sensitive orders that do not justify a drive to the store or a conventional delivery route.

Customers access the service through the DoorDash app. If an address is eligible, drone delivery appears as an option, and the shopper can enter the dedicated "Lowe's by Drone" storefront. Wing then transports the order, subject to a current payload of approximately 2.5 pounds per flight.

That weight limit shapes the business case. This is not a service for lumber, large power tools, or bags of concrete. The retailer has instead assembled a selection that includes hand tools, paint products, soap, tape, all-purpose cleaner, and batteries. These are comparatively small products, but forgetting one can interrupt a repair or leave a crew waiting.

Home improvement projects are particularly well suited to urgent, lightweight delivery. A missing roll of tape or set of batteries can have more operational value in the middle of a job than its retail price suggests. Rapid 20-minute delivery offers distinct utility when a contractor's time, or an entire weekend project, is stalled.

The pilot also illustrates how drone delivery is moving from a technology demonstration toward a narrowly defined retail service. The Federal Aviation Administration treats package delivery as an advanced drone operation, with operators working within federal aviation requirements rather than simply extending ordinary courier activity into the air. That regulatory layer can affect where services operate, how they scale, and which partners retailers select.

State and local considerations remain part of the picture as well. The National Conference of State Legislatures tracks a varied state policy landscape for unmanned aircraft, including issues involving operations, privacy, and public safety. For a national chain, successful performance in one market does not automatically translate into identical operations everywhere. https://t.co/4TXSIwm9xz

text:
Novena to Saint Michael and All the Holy Angels Day 9 Sept. 28
.
Novena Prayer:
.
V: O all ye Holy Angels, who contemplate unceasingly the uncreated beauty of the Divinity, in company with our ever glorious Queen,
R: We present and offer to you this novena not only as a means of obtaining favors
V: (here specify your request), but also as a reparation for our past ingratitude, and that of all men.
R: Deign to accept it, O amiable Spirits, in union with the love and devotion of such saints as were especially devout to you, and obtain for us the grace to spend this life fervently that it may be the commencement of that blessed life which we hope to live forever with you in heaven.
.
V: Let us pray
.
O God, Who with wonderful order has regulated the functions of angels and men, grant that those who always assist before Thy throne in heaven may defend our lives here on earth, through Jesus Christ, Thy Son, our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with Thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, one God, world without end.
R: Amen.
.
Ninth Day:
.
V: Most holy Angels, ye whose zeal for the interest of God, wherever they need to be defended,
R: Carries ye through the universe more rapidly than lightning, protect His cause in our souls, and in virtue of the Divine Blood, obtain for us the signal grace of final perseverance.
.
V: St. Michael, the Archangel,
R: Defend us in battle. Be our protection against the wickedness and snares of the devil. May God rebuke him, we humbly pray; and do Thou, O Prince of the Heavenly Host, by the Power of God, cast into hell, Satan and all the evil spirits, who roam throughout the world seeking the ruin of souls.
V: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
R: As it was in the beginning, is now and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
V: O most glorious Prince, Michael, the Archangel,
R: Be mindful of us, here and everywhere, and always pray to the Son of God for us.
V: I will praise Thee, O God, in the sight of Thy Angels.
R: I will adore Thee in Thy holy Temple and I will confess Thy Name.
.
V: Let us pray
.
O God, Who hast in an admirable order disposed the ministry of angels and of men, grant in Thy goodness that our life on earth may be protected by those who in heaven always assist before Thy throne ready to do Thy will. Through Our Lord, Jesus Christ.
R: Amen.

PART 2 – DAY OF ATONEMENT – FIFTH STEP IN GOD’S PLAN OF SALVATION FOR MANKIND

Harmanjit Singh Saini
September 24, 2026

God’s seven annual holy days picture God’s Plan of Salvation for Mankind. The autumn holy day season is upon us, and we have already celebrated the first holy day of the season called the Feast of Trumpets or Rosh Hashanah by the Jews on September 12th this past Saturday. It pictures the return of Jesus Christ to earth in almighty power, like the God of the Old Testament, accompanied by the resurrected saints to save humanity from annihilating itself in the soon coming world wars and global catastrophes and then establish the Kingdom of God over all the earth.

God’s next holy day is called the “Day of Atonement”, or Yom Kippur as the Jews call it, and it was celebrated this past Monday, September 21st this year.

After the nations of the world are subdued by Jesus Christ pictured by the Feast of Trumpets, the next step in God’s Master Plan of salvation for all mankind is to redeem mankind to Himself and for the peoples of the earth to become “at one” with Him, as symbolized by the Day of Atonement. That is necessary because the sins of the world have cut us off from God as says Isaiah. 59:1-2: “1 Behold, the Lord's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; nor His ear heavy, that it cannot hear. 2 But your iniquities have separated you from your God; and your sins have hidden His face from you, so that He will not hear.”

In Part 1 we discussed Satan’s incredible ability to deceive and destroy and how he will still be able to deceive human beings when he is released from the abyss for a short time even after they had been living in God’s kingdom for 1,000 years. Therefore, if the world is to have peace, Satan must be removed to stop him from influencing mankind. That event is pictured by the Day of Atonement.

God’s specific instructions for keeping the Day of Atonement are stated in Leviticus 23:27-28: "Also the tenth day of this seventh month [of God’s sacred calendar] shall be the Day of Atonement," God says. "It shall be a holy convocation [or Church service] for you; you shall afflict your souls...And you shall do no work on that same day, for it is the Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the Lord your God."

The word “afflict” comes from the Hebrew word anah which is used in connection with fasting in Psalm 35:13 and Ezra 8:21. Fasting means abstaining from food and drink, including water (Esther 4:16). Therefore, God commands us to celebrate this day by fasting for 24 hours by abstaining from food and drink, including water.

SATAN’S INFLUENCE WILL END

Christians who struggle to resist Satan and overcome sin fight a spiritual battle against the devil and his demons. Paul explains in Ephesians 6: "For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the powers, against the world forces of this darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places" (Ephesians 6:12, NASB).

Therefore, at the beginning of Christ’s reign on earth, if there is to be genuine peace among men, Satan the devil must be banished. The Day of Atonement looks forward to that time as Revelation 20:1-3 states: “Then I saw an angel coming down from heaven, having the key to the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. He laid hold of the dragon, that serpent of old [meaning the serpent in the Garden of Eden who deceived Eve], who is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years; and he cast him into the bottomless pit [or abyss], and shut him up, and set a seal on him, so that he should deceive the nations no more till the thousand years were finished.”

OLD TESTAMENT SYMBOLISM

God’s additional instructions to ancient Israel in Leviticus 16 about the Day of Atonement contain very important symbolism that helps us further understand the significance of this day in God’s plan of salvation for mankind. It describes a very important ceremony that was enacted every year in ancient Israel on the Day of Atonement. Verse 5 states, “And he [i.e., the high priest] shall take of the congregation of the children of Israel two kids of the goats for a sin offering, and one ram for a burnt offering.”

Then verses 7-8 state: “And he shall take the two goats and present them before the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. And Aaron shall cast lots upon the two goats; one lot for the Lord, and the other lot for the scapegoat.”

The original Hebrew word translated “scapegoat,” is Azazel. It is plain from the text that one goat represents the Lord, or Jesus Christ. But why would God have a second goat represented in the symbolism? While some explain the second goat as also referring to Christ, virtually every respected commentary affirms that the Jews and knowledgeable Bible students recognize Azazel as Satan the devil, as will become clear from the symbolism in the ceremony.

Of course, both goats are types. But why is it that lots must be used—which are a solemn appeal to God in any doubtful matter—to determine which goat should represent Satan and which should be Christ? 2 Corinthians 11:13-15 tells us that Satan transforms himself into an angel of light and his ministers transform themselves into ministers of righteousness. Therefore, it is difficult for human beings on their own to discern the difference between Satan’s counterfeits from God’s truth. All of mainstream Christianity does not have all the truth. Even in our time, God had to send a special prophet in the spirit and power of Elijah, Herbert W. Armstrong, to restore all His truths. God had to reveal the truth and proper understanding of every small and great doctrine one at a time through Mr. Armstrong. Humans even in God’s Church would not have been able to come to the truth with their own understanding of the Bible.

Thus, in the ceremony on the Day of Atonement men on their own were not capable of discerning which goat should represent Jesus Christ and which should represent Satan the devil. A sincere solemn appeal to God was required to intervene and reveal the truth through the casting of lots in this unclear matter.

The high priest was instructed to first offer a bullock for himself and his family in verse 11 to purify himself from his sins.

HIGH PRIEST REPRESENTED CHRIST

The high priest was then to offer the goat that represented Christ as stated in Leviticus 16:15-16: “Then shall he kill the goat of the sin offering, that is for the people, and bring his blood within the veil, and do with that blood as he did with the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it upon the mercy seat, and before the mercy seat: And he shall make an ATONEMENT for the holy place, because of the uncleanness of the children of Israel, and because of their transgressions in all their sins…”

After His resurrection, Jesus ascended to heaven. Some have misunderstood the Azazel goat to be a representation of Christ, who went to heaven. This is wrong. The Azazel goat was taken to an uninhabited wilderness. Heaven is not an uninhabited wilderness. It is inhabited by God and hundreds of millions of holy angels. It is clear that the high priest represented Christ’s role as High Priest in bringing the offering of the slain goat (Christ, the Lord) before the mercy seat of God.

Christ now sits at the right hand of God as our High Priest as stated in I Peter 3:22 and in Hebrews 6:20.

The goat that was offered cannot be a type of Christ as High Priest. This goat was slain each year for centuries until the real Christ was slain and went to heaven to become our High Priest. Until Christ’s actual sacrifice, the Levitical high priest was a type of Christ as the High Priest.

Thus, the first goat represented the sacrificed Christ. The Levitical high priest fulfilled the role of Christ, as our resurrected High Priest. Finally, let’s see why the second goat must be the devil.

ROLE OF THE AZAZEL GOAT

Here is what the high priest did next. Leviticus 16:20-24, 26 states: “And when he has made an end of reconciling the holy place, and the tabernacle of the congregation, and the altar, he shall bring the live goat: And Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions in all their sins, putting them upon the head of the goat, and shall send him away by the hand of a fit man into the wilderness: And the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities unto a land not inhabited: and he shall let go the goat in the wilderness. And Aaron shall come into the tabernacle of the congregation…and he shall wash his flesh with water in the holy place…and offer his burnt offering, and the burnt offering of the people, and make an ATONEMENT for himself, and for the people…And he that let go the goat for the scapegoat [or Azazel] shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward come into the camp.”

The symbolism of the live goat parallels the fate of Satan and the demons, whom God will bind by the hands of an angel and remove after laying all the sins of humanity on his head, before Jesus Christ's millennial rule is established as already mentioned from Revelation 20:1-3. And the goat being sent into an uninhabited wilderness parallels Satan’s fate to be in solitary confinement for the entire 1,000 years of God’s Kingdom.

We need to make this critically important distinction: Christ willingly bore our sins, even though He was completely innocent. The devil is not innocent!  He is a murderer and a liar as John 8:44 states, a deceiver as Revelation 12:9 shows and a destroyer as Revelation 9:11 shows, and far from innocent. As the author of confusion, he is guilty of enormous transgressions and has much to be indicted for.

The devil is the one who is truly the ultimate author of the world’s sins. The true God is a God of justice and equity. He would never require an innocent Christ to die for sins that He had not committed, and, at the same time, require no accountability on the part of the devil. God always places blame squarely on the shoulders of him to whom it belongs.

Of course, all human beings have sinned as Romans 3:23 shows and are responsible for these sins. None can say he is innocent. But the devil influences and tempts all those who willingly commit sins of their own volition.

The world could never be at one with God if Satan remained free to roam the earth, tempting, deceiving, confusing, destroying, lying, murdering and leading humanity to envy, jealousy, treachery, division, violence, war, bloodshed and death. As the ultimate cause of the world’s sins and problems, he must be removed from earth, from heaven and any part of the inhabited universe. As the high priest confessed the sins of Israel over the head of the Azazel goat and sent him away bearing those sins, the devil will carry the sins of mankind that he induced them into committing to the abyss with him? Now we can see the deep meaning of these ceremonies on the Day of Atonement in ancient Israel.

The Day of Atonement thus pictures the removal of Satan and his demons to a place of restraint.

MODERN APPLICATION OF THIS FESTIVAL

Yet another important lesson comes to us through the Day of Atonement. After His sacrifice Jesus Christ did not stay dead; He came back to life. What does the Day of Atonement teach us about Christ's role after His resurrection?

Leviticus 16:15-19 describes a solemn ceremony that was carried out only once each year, on the Day of Atonement. The high priest was to take the blood of the slain goat into the Holy Place—the most sacred part of the tabernacle—and to the mercy seat. The mercy seat was symbolic of the very throne of Almighty God.

The book of Hebrews 9:11-12 makes this symbolism clear. "But Christ came as High Priest of the good things to come, with the greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hands, that is, not of this [physical] creation. Not with the blood of goats and calves, but with His own blood He entered the Most Holy Place once for all, having obtained eternal redemption.”

The Day of Atonement thus pictures the loving reconciliation we have with God, made possible through Christ's sacrifice. It also shows the remarkable truth that Satan, the author of sin, will eventually be removed so that humanity can at last attain reconciliation with God on a universal basis. It also shows that Jesus Christ as our High Priest is our advocate daily with God as stated in 1 John 2:1, interceding and pleading for us with God the Father to forgive our sins and give us the help to overcome them. And because we now have direct access to God the Father as pictured by the tearing up of the massive veil from ‘top to bottom’ in the Temple at Jerusalem at the moment of Christ’s death, as stated in Mark 15:38, “And the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom,” we can now pray directly to God the Father.

HOW THE DAY OF ATONEMENT IS KEPT

God’s Church follows God’s specific instructions in Leviticus 23:27-28 on how we keep this festival. God says, “It shall be a holy convocation for you; you shall afflict your souls...And you shall do no work on that same day, for it is the Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the Lord your God."

The phrase "afflict your soul" on this day means to fast or abstain from food and drink. The proper reason for fasting is not to bend God to our will. Fasting helps us remember how temporary our physical existence is. Without food and water, we would soon perish. Fasting helps us realize just how much we need God as the giver and sustainer of life. Thus, the purpose of fasting is to humble ourselves before God, as David said in Psalm 35:11, “I humbled my soul with fasting…” and Psalm 69:7, “…I wept, and chastened my soul with fasting.”

Jesus Christ gave examples of the wrong ways and reasons to fast in contrast with humbling ourselves. In Luke 18:12, Jesus described how the Pharisee prayed: “11 The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank You, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican. 12 I fast twice in the week.” Here Jesus described how the Pharisee fasted twice a week, all in vain.

Then Jesus described how to fast properly in Matthew 6:16-17, “16 Moreover when you fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily [or truly] I say unto you, they have their reward. 17 But when you fast, anoint your head, and wash your face; 18 That you appear not unto men to fast, but unto your Father which is in secret: and your Father, which sees in secret, shall reward you openly.”

We should always fast on the Day of Atonement in a repentant frame of mind, confessing our sins. Notice Daniel's exemplary attitude while fasting in Daniel 9:3-4: "Then I set my face toward the Lord God to make request by prayer and supplications, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes. And I prayed to the Lord my God and made confession."

Day of Atonement should be a time of inner reflection. While during Passover and the Days of Unleavened Bread we examine our inner thoughts, attitudes and actions to root out sin out of our lives, the Day of Atonement is a time to examine ourselves on how we deal with the poor, needy and afflicted, or our neighbor, as a way to get closer to God. Unless we are loving our neighbor as ourselves, including providing help in need, we will be fasting on the Day of Atonement in vain. Remember, the Jubilee, or release of debts every 50 years was proclaimed on the Day of Atonement, as stated in Leviticus 25:10, “ 10 And you shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubilee unto you; and you shall return every man unto his possession, and you shall return every man unto his family.” Thus, day of Atonement teaches us to release the burdens on our fellow human beings.

The way such self-examination is to be conducted is described in Isaiah 58:3 (NLT): 3 ‘We have fasted before you!’ they say. ‘Why aren’t you impressed? We have been very hard on ourselves, and you don’t even notice it!’ “I will tell you why!” I respond. “It’s because you are fasting to please yourselves. Even while you fast, you keep oppressing your workers. 4 What good is fasting when you keep on fighting and quarreling? This kind of fasting will never get you anywhere with me. 5 You humble yourselves by going through the motions of penance, bowing your heads like reeds bending in the wind. You dress in burlap and cover yourselves with ashes. Is this what you call fasting? Do you really think this will please the Lord?”

God here describes fasting very similar to the way the Pharisees fasted, all for show and vanity, to appear to be righteous to get the praise of men.

Isaiah continues: 6 “No, this is the kind of fasting I want: Free those who are wrongly imprisoned; lighten the burden of those who work for you. Let the oppressed go free and remove the chains that bind people. 7 Share your food with the hungry and give shelter to the homeless. Give clothes to those who need them, and do not hide from relatives who need your help.” If we reflect on these things while fasting and then take action, here then are the benefits God promises:

8 “Then your salvation will come like the dawn, and your wounds will quickly heal. [Here is one way to get prayers for healing answered quickly]. Your godliness will lead you forward, and the glory of the Lord will protect you from behind. 9 Then when you call, the Lord will answer. ‘Yes, I am here,’ he will quickly reply. [This is the way to get prayers answered quickly.]

God continues: “…Remove the heavy yoke of oppression. Stop pointing your finger and spreading vicious rumors! 10 Feed the hungry and help those in trouble. Then your light will shine out from the darkness, and the darkness around you will be as bright as noon. 11 The Lord will guide you continually, giving you water when you are dry and restoring your strength. You will be like a well-watered garden, like an ever-flowing spring. 12 Some of you will rebuild the deserted ruins of your cities. Then you will be known as a rebuilder of walls and a restorer of homes.”

Thus, merely going hungry and thirsty on the Day of Atonement is not how this holy day is kept. One can go hungry and thirsty for a day without deriving any spiritual benefit from it or getting any closer to God. In fact, if fasting is done for vanity, to appear to men to be righteous, then the person is actually drifting further away from God. This means that one has to prepare to keep the Day of Atonement by self-examination on how one is treating the poor, needy and oppressed, and by actually taking action to relieve their suffering and help them in meeting their basic needs. Nine days between the Feast of Trumpets or Rosh Hashanah and the Day of Atonement is a good time to conduct this self-examination and resolve to take action.

In addition to fasting on the Day of Atonement, God’s Church also attends Church services for about two hours during which we learn more about the meaning and significance of this day, and how best to keep it. This is also one day in seven such days annually that we give freewill offerings for furthering God’s work of preaching the gospel, or good news of the soon coming kingdom of God to all the world as a witness.

DAY OF ATONEMENT KEPT BY THE EARLY CHURCH

An important question is, “Did God’s Church in the days of the apostles keep the Day of Atonement?” since mainstream Christianity does not keep any of the holy days. The answer is, “Yes!” Notice in Acts 27:9: “Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them.” The margins of most Bibles note that Paul’s reference to the “fast” is a direct reference to the Day of Atonement.

Paul here was referring to a time of dangerous sailing – which in the Mediterranean is the autumn season – it becomes quite clear that Luke, the writer of the Book of Acts was referring to the Day of Atonement. The New Testament Church could not have been keeping track of time by referring to the Day of Atonement if they were not observing it. When the timing is carefully checked with the understanding that Paul was referring to a time of dangerous sailing—the autumn in the Mediterranean Sea—it becomes apparent that the New Testament Church was, in fact, marking time by this Day of Atonement. God’s holy spirit would not have inspired a reference to a holy day if it was done away with!

In summary then, the Day of Atonement pictures first, the removal of Satan and the demons from rulership over the earth, after Jesus Christ returns to the earth to set up His kingdom. Second, all of humanity’s sins will be placed on the head of Satan and he will be imprisoned in the bottomless pit or abyss in solitary confinement, while the demons will be imprisoned separately from him. Thirdly, removal of Satan, the source of all the world’s sins, and the demons means that they will no longer be around to influence humanity into sin during the 1000 years of God’s Kingdom. Fourth, because of Satan’s removal and his sinful influence, all of humanity can be reconciled to God the Father on a universal basis and become at-one with Him. Fifth, Jesus Christ as our High Priest now advocates on our behalf with God the Father. Sixth, we now have direct access to God the Father, not only through the High Priest, but we can go to Him directly in prayer. And finally, because of the removal of Satan and his demons, lasting peace will be possible on earth.

If you would like to learn more about God’s holy days and keeping the Day of Atonement, please read my book “God’s Plan of Salvation for Mankind”, available free at my web site https://t.co/4SUTbycEiS. A great deal of unique information on Bible prophecy, particularly in my eBook “World in Bible Prophecy,” comparison of different religions and what you should do to receive God’s help during the soon coming global catastrophes is also available on my religion website.

Lakewood-Amedex Biotherapeutics Inc. (@LakewoodAmedex)  (@Nasdaq: $LABT) reported on September 24 that the first patient has been dosed in its Phase 2a clinical trial evaluating Nu-3 for the treatment of patients with mildly infected diabetic foot ulcers (iDFU). Nu-3 is a topically applied antimicrobial gel designed to rapidly eliminate microbes directly at the site of infection.

Lakewood-Amedex Biotherapeutics Inc. is a B2i Digital (@b2idigital)  Featured Company. See the company's in-depth profile at: https://t.co/RFXWHGwSv7

Now under way, the multicenter, single-blinded, dose-finding study is designed to evaluate three concentrations of Nu-3 and inform dose selection for the company's continued clinical development program:

• Adult patients with Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes and mildly infected diabetic foot ulcers will be evaluated at Nu-3 gel concentrations of 2%, 5% and 10%

• Safety and efficacy assessments will include Nu-3's ability to reduce microbial burden and resolve infection

• Topline data from the Phase 2a study are expected in the first quarter of 2027

Chairing the study is David G. Armstrong, DPM, M.D., Ph.D., Distinguished Professor of Surgery and Neurological Surgery at the Keck School of Medicine of USC, who spoke to the clinical need behind the trial. text:
As always, the author of the post nails the structural essence of this historical juncture. While my own conclusions do not always rest in absolute, seamless alignment with the author’s  overarching framework, her erudite and remarkably discerning approach to history is consistently captivating. There is an intellectual depth to her work that makes one eager to examine what subtle dimensions can be brought to the conversation. It is in that spirit of scholarly appreciation that I will try to offer my own humble attempts to add to what she has put forward, and it is with that respect for her scholarship that this analysis is offered.

The political trajectory of Francis Preston Blair Jr provides a definitive window into the fragile architecture of the wartime Unionist coalition and the ultimate disruption of Abraham Lincoln’s counterfactual blueprint for Reconstruction. In assessing the postwar realignment of conservative Unionists, a critical distinction must be maintained between a principled rejection of the Radical Republican program and an abandonment of the Union itself. Blair’s postwar migration to the Democratic Party does not denote an ontological error in his wartime allegiance, but rather highlights the severe institutional friction that occurred when the executive consensus under Lincoln was forcibly supplanted by the legislative radicalism of Thaddeus Stevens.

This complex political transition cannot be decoupled from the deeply intimate personal relationship between Abraham Lincoln and the Blair family dynasty. Far from being a mere distant appointee or an opportunistic ally, Frank Blair, along with his brother Montgomery, who served as Lincoln's Postmaster General, and their father, Francis Preston Blair Sr, formed an indispensable inner circle of confidantes for the wartime executive. The Blairs possessed direct access to the president’s private quarters, and Lincoln frequently crossed Pennsylvania Avenue just to have informal, late night strategic chats at the Blair mansion. When Radical Republicans aggressively targeted the Blairs for their highly conservative stances on gradual emancipation and state level suffrage, Lincoln continuously weaponized his own executive capital to shield them, actively coordinating Frank Blair's fluid transitions between his congressional seat and his military commands. The deep structural trust between them proved that the Blair family's conservative unionism was not an administrative liability, but rather a central, defining pillar of Lincoln's long term governing consensus.

Lincoln’s Proclamation of Amnesty and Reconstruction, which established the Ten Percent Plan, was fundamentally anchored in an executive pragmatism designed to prioritize national cohesion over immediate, systemic societal transformation. Lincoln’s executive framework was defined by an unbroken commitment to constitutional continuity, viewing the rapid re establishment of loyal civil governance via a low threshold loyalty formula as the fastest mechanism to shorten the conflict and stabilize the republic.

This diplomatic and executive flexibility found its ultimate expression in the Hampton Roads Conference of February 1865. Arranged through the personal diplomacy of the elder Francis Preston Blair Sr, Lincoln met directly with Confederate commissioners, including Confederate Vice President Alexander H Stephens, signaling an unmistakable willingness to negotiate a peaceful transition back into the constitutional fold. This pivotal conference demonstrated that his primary objective remained the immediate restoration of federal authority and national stability, rather than an unconditional subjugation or an immediate, state imposed social upheaval of the region. By engineering this low threshold mechanism for state re admittance, Lincoln sought to bind the constitutional fabric rapidly and with minimal friction. 

This conservative framework deliberately left the existing social and economic hierarchy open to gradual, localized evolution rather than immediate federal dismantling. Within this precise paradigm, conservative nationalists like the Blairs were not anomalies, they were the absolute bedrock of Lincoln’s strategy. Frank Blair’s fierce commitment to the preservation of the Union was structurally compatible with his deeply conservative opposition to black suffrage and federal intervention in the Southern electorate. Under a surviving Lincoln administration, the executive branch would have maintained a coalition broad enough to accommodate Blair’s brand of conservative Unionism, utilizing it as an administrative bridge to restore stable civil government across the fractured South.

Crucially, Lincoln’s blueprint represented a unique mechanism designed to deliver a legally continuous transition that aimed at balancing regional interests. For the white South, despite Lincoln's unprecedented wartime expansion of executive power and the perceived usurpation of traditional constitutional authority, his specific vision for rebuilding the nation was deeply conciliatory. The plan offered an orderly path out of the ashes of defeat, sparing the region from the devastating economic paralysis and localized political instability that characterized the subsequent era of military occupation. By avoiding the sweeping disenfranchisement of the traditional leadership class, Lincoln's policy would have been a welcome alternative for an exhausted Southern population eager for the restoration of local civil governance and economic stability. This approach might have mitigated the intense, desperate bitterness that later fueled the rise of insurgent violence and paramilitary organizations.

Simultaneously, this rapid stabilization would have altered the trajectory for the freedmen relative to the volatile, short lived experiments of the Radical era. A gradualist proclamation of giving rights step by step establishes a much firmer, more resilient foundation for true civic absorption. 

It is historically illuminating to parallel Lincoln's incremental framework with the constitutional deliberations of the mid twentieth century, specifically the tactical consensus engineered by Supreme Court Justice Felix Frankfurter during the Brown v Board of Education implementation debates. Frankfurter famously recognized the severe institutional and cultural dangers of enforcing sudden, sweeping structural overhauls all at once across a deeply resistant Southern landscape. By advocating for the metric of all deliberate speed, Frankfurter sought to avoid an immediate systemic collapse of local governance, aiming instead for a legally enforceable, step by step transition.

This parallel underscores a foundational philosophical reality: you cannot legislate morality, you must enforce the law. Sovereign power can and must execute just, objective laws that reflect the organic structure of the populace, but attempting to use raw federal coercion to instantly mandate an inner moral transformation is an exercise in institutional futility. When the legislative apparatus ignores this boundary, it merely invites catastrophic backlash.

The supreme irony of history, however, is that John Wilkes Booth single handedly destroyed the very path to local autonomy he claimed to defend. Driven by a fanatical, reactionary zeal, Booth’s assassination of Lincoln stands as one of the most short sighted tactical disasters in American political history. By striking down the one executive leader who possessed the immense political capital, administrative flexibility, and magnanimous intent necessary to shield the defeated states, Booth completely upended any hope for a smooth, conciliatory return to local governance. His bullet cleared the path for the total dismantling of the traditional Southern social fabric, removing the only buffer between a conquered region and a vengeful legislative branch.

In the chaotic vacuum that followed, the presidency fell to Andrew Johnson whose political ineptitude and stubborn defiance of the federal legislature quickly triggered a catastrophic institutional crisis. Johnson’s bungled stewardship utterly alienated moderate elements within the government, providing the Radical Republican faction under Thaddeus Stevens and Charles Sumner with the perfect pretext to seize absolute control of the legislative apparatus. Consequently, Booth's desperate act of violence directly catalyzed the advent of Radical Reconstruction, resulting in the exact outcomes the white South dreaded most: a protracted military occupation, sweeping disenfranchisement of the traditional leadership class, and the rapid, federal enforcement of universal male suffrage.

The crisis of the late 1860s was generated not by the initial Unionist consensus, but by its catastrophic fracture under the pressure of Congressional Radicalism. This structural reality is clearly evidenced by the early Southern institutional responses in states like Louisiana, Arkansas, and Tennessee . Prior to Lincoln’s assassination, these states were already actively organizing loyal civil governments under the Ten Percent guidelines, establishing a cooperative pathway that was actively being integrated into the wartime Union structure. The localized legislative alignments in these states proved that a viable, executive led reconstruction was entirely possible when grounded in mutual institutional interests rather than sudden, federal diktats.

When the Radical Republican wing subsequently seized control of the legislative apparatus, they weaponized federal authority to initiate a profound political and social reconfiguration of the conquered states, an institutional shift that Blair and his contemporaries viewed as an unconstitutional overreach and an existential betrayal of the original war aims. The conservative reaction within the Republican party was a defense of traditional federalism against what was perceived as an unprecedented distortion of the constitutional balance. Blair’s eventual position on the 1868 Democratic ticket alongside Horatio Seymour represents a logical, defensive realignment to preserve his foundational tenets of white constitutionalism and state autonomy against the ascendancy of Thaddeus Stevens.

Consequently, a rigorous structural reading confirms the precision of the mechanics underlying this transition. Lincoln’s blueprint represented a viable mechanism capable of preserving the wartime coalition while fostering a stable, lasting peace. By prioritizing the rapid restoration of the Union and building a bridge of mutual interest between the regions, Lincoln’s policy would have retained conservative stalwarts within the governing paradigm, avoiding the stark political polarization and systemic abandonment that displayed itself in the postwar decade.

There remains a deep, lingering recalcitrance toward Abraham Lincoln’s memory in modern historical discourse, particularly across the American South. Much of this regional estrangement stems directly from the tragedy of his abrupt assassination. Because John Wilkes Booth cut his life short precisely at the moment of military triumph, Lincoln was structurally prevented from unfolding the secondary phase of his grand strategy, the deeply conciliatory, protective executive policy designed to shield the defeated states from 
systemic legislative retribution. 

The average observer today evaluates Lincoln purely through the lens of wartime devastation, entirely unaware of the administrative mechanics of the Ten Percent Plan or his willingness to compromise at Hampton Roads. Had Lincoln lived to execute his postwar blueprint, it is highly probable that regional memory would have evolved along a more nuanced trajectory. Rather than viewing him with unyielding hostility, the South might have treated his memory a little better, recognizing the structural insulation his administration provided during the transition back to civil rule. This potential shift finds an instructive historical parallel in the post World War II occupation of Japan and the enduring reputation of General Douglas MacArthur. MacArthur was a commander who directed the total logistical decimation of the Japanese Empire, reducing its major cities to ash and driving the population to absolute exhaustion.

Yet, because MacArthur presided over the postwar transition with profound institutional magnanimity, preserving local cultural symbols, preventing widespread domestic starvation, and acting as a vital administrative buffer against harsher retributive forces from Washington and the international community, his historical standing in Japan remained remarkably sophisticated and often favorable. The implementation of his authority was viewed as necessary to transition the nation away from complete destruction toward functional, domestic sovereignty.

Interestingly, this connection carries a striking generational echo: MacArthur’s own father, Arthur MacArthur Jr, was a celebrated Union hero who fought directly in the Western Theater of the Civil War. As a young officer in the 24th Wisconsin Infantry, the elder MacArthur charged up Missionary Ridge and fought through the Atlanta campaign, experiencing firsthand the raw devastation required to preserve the Union. This familial baseline of wartime sacrifice underscores why a figure like MacArthur understood the immense weight of post conflict governance. He had grown up in the shadow of a conflict that succeeded in preservation but fractured in its peace.

One cannot draw a definitive conclusion about how universally popular Lincoln might have eventually become in a reconstruction context, nor should we attempt to oversimplify the genuine grievances of a defeated populace. However, it is reasonable to suggest that a living Lincoln would have been recognized as a necessary shield against the far harsher realities of Congressional radicalism. Because Lincoln was assassinated before he could fulfill that protective role, the South was left with only one image burned indelibly into its collective consciousness: that of the conquering executive who unlocked the gates to a punishing military occupation. Ultimately, Booth's bullet permanently froze Lincoln's image at the apex of conflict, depriving the nation of a gradual, executive led reconciliation that might have softened the sharp edges of regional memory.

As an aside, the immense structural friction of this era invites a deeper evaluation of Thaddeus Stevens himself, a highly compelling yet polarizing architect of the period whom I intend to write about at length in a future piece. To be entirely candid, I am truly not a fan of his approach or his legacy. History continuously demonstrates that whenever a political figure leans too deeply into radicalism on any front, the outcome is inherently destructive. 

The tragic paradigm of human governance is that when an extreme radical captures one end of the spectrum, whether it manifests as the revolutionary socialism of Karl Marx or the aggressive, punitive legislative engineering of the Radical Republicans, it inevitably triggers an inescapable counter reaction.

Just as Isaac Newton established that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, political physics dictates that extreme actions on the left or within a radical vanguard will unfailingly generate an aggressive, destabilizing overreaction from the right. Neither extreme is healthy, and neither yields a sustainable civilization. To safeguard a republic, a society must consciously choose to moderate its course with purposeful, explicit intent. We must remain perpetually vigilant against the erosion of the center, which is precisely why maintaining an unwavering value system grounded firmly in personal honor, human dignity, an authentic love of country, and basic fairness remains an absolute necessity for survival. I humbly offer these observations for the consideration of the audience. Thank you for your indulgence.

The NUFDI Iran Conference is still live, but this extraordinary panel has just ended. If you missed Ilan Berman, Danielle Pletka, Alex Winston, and Khosro Isfahani, watch the replay. Trust me—you do not want to miss this discussion.

I’ve summarized the comments of my new hero—for today, anyway 😏—@Pletka below:

Danielle Pletka’s message was blunt: Washington continues to misunderstand the Islamic Republic because it assumes that everyone ultimately thinks like a businessman.

The regime’s leaders certainly enjoy money, luxury and the wealth they have stolen from Iranians—but they are ideologues first. Profit matters, but ideology determines their red lines. The same mistake is often made with Vladimir Putin and other ideological adversaries: Western officials assume that every conviction can eventually be negotiated away if the economic incentive is attractive enough.

But the Islamic Republic does not regard control of the Strait of Hormuz, its nuclear and missile programs, or its support for Hezbollah, Hamas, the Houthis and Hashd al-Shaabi as ordinary bargaining chips. These are pillars of its identity, power and revolutionary mission.

So what exactly are Western negotiators negotiating?

Pletka argued that the cycle repeats because transactional policymakers treat every meeting as a fresh start. The same officials return to the same table, through the same mediators, discussing the same issues—while disregarding decades of deception and failed agreements.

Washington also keeps convincing itself that time is on its side and that the regime must eventually compromise to survive. Yet the Islamic Republic has repeatedly used time to rebuild, reorganize and test how much punishment its adversaries are actually willing to impose.

Pletka compared this to repeatedly believing an unfaithful spouse who comes home promising that the affair is over. Western governments want to believe the regime’s assurances, even when its conduct tells them otherwise.

She was equally dismissive of Washington’s obsession with supposed factions inside the Islamic Republic. Analysts endlessly classify officials as “moderates,” “pragmatists,” “reformists” or “hard-liners,” creating the impression that somewhere inside the system there must be someone with whom the West can do business.

In her view, that distinction becomes largely meaningless on the issues that matter most: regime survival, nuclear weapons, ballistic missiles, terrorist proxies and hostility toward the United States and Israel. Officials such as Zarif and Araghchi may be personable, polished and skilled at charming Western audiences, but they still serve the same system.

Unless a genuine Iranian Gorbachev emerges—someone willing to preserve the state by fundamentally changing the nature of the regime—searching for the next “moderate” only traps the West in another round of wishful thinking. Pletka sees no such figure inside the present system.

The war, she argued, should also force analysts to discard many of their old assumptions. She candidly acknowledged that she had believed the regime would never close the Strait of Hormuz because it needed oil revenue and feared the consequences.

That assumption proved wrong.

When the regime believed its survival was threatened, it was willing to cross red lines previously considered irrational. It discovered that it did not need to defeat the United States militarily or seal the Strait perfectly. It only needed to raise the danger enough that insurers and commercial carriers would refuse to enter—even if Washington offered military protection.

The same logic applies to Bab el-Mandeb and to pipelines that can be targeted by drones. The regime has learned that risk itself can be weaponized.

Having survived enormous military pressure, the Islamic Republic may now believe that it can absorb far greater costs—and impose far greater costs—than Western policymakers previously assumed.

text:
In April, I asked U.S. officials what a first concrete step towards multilateral nuclear talks would be.

The response: “We’re not in negotiations right now. We’re in exploratory discussions.”

Five months later, what has changed?

I appreciate @RobbieGramer and @MGordonWSJ pursuing this story on the CTBT’s 30th anniversary and ahead of renewed P5 talks after a much-needed break following what was an exhausting NPT Review Conference. But the @WSJ report leaves key questions unanswered about how substantive and reciprocal these U.S.–China exchanges actually are.

Having followed the P5 Process for years and participated in both P5-mandated and bilateral U.S.–China Track 2 dialogues, I welcome sustained engagement at both levels. The U.S. and China have been discussing their nuclear doctrines and, more recently, specific risk-reduction measures within the P5 for years. The question is what these reported bilateral exchanges add.

Has Beijing agreed to a substantive bilateral agenda on testing? Within the P5, has consensus been reached on discussing testing concerns and related confidence-building measures in their agenda moving forward? Are reciprocal proposals being developed? What is Washington prepared to offer and accept itself?

Washington has been pressing its testing allegations while encouraging dialogue for months. The U.S., UK and France publicly called in May for confidence-building measures on nuclear explosive test monitoring, alongside a ballistic missile and space launch notification mechanism. What remains unclear is whether these efforts have secured agreement on a process for developing such measures.

Confidential diplomacy deserves room to work. Exploratory exchanges can be valuable in their own right. But readers need enough substance to assess whether continued contact is producing diplomatic momentum. The report gives us too little to make that judgment.

As I argued in @ForeignPolicy last October (https://t.co/RCdQhstgf3), ambiguity over Washington’s own testing intentions carries serious risks. Leaving other governments guessing can fuel the miscalculation and reciprocal escalation these discussions should help prevent. Has Washington clarified to Beijing what Trump’s testing directive means in practice? Has the administration even settled that question internally almost a year later?

I also warned last October that China could benefit most from a return to explosive testing. Washington should explain how reopening that competition would serve American security, given its success in maintaining confidence in its arsenal without nuclear detonations for decades.

There is a real opportunity to strengthen confidence in the testing moratoria through technical clarification, reciprocal transparency and sustained expert engagement. I want these discussions to succeed, but Washington needs to explain how threatening to resume nuclear explosive testing helps preserve the restraint it is asking others to demonstrate.

text:
Washington State 

NEW 9.9% STATE INCOME TAX 

Washington State Dept. of Revenue (DOR) warned income tax provisions could ‘cause political and optics issues’

By TJ Martinell 
Sept. 24, 2026

Washington Department of Revenue officials warned during the legislative session that provisions in the proposed income tax could present not just enforcement complications, but invite legal challenges aside from those it currently faces, new records obtained by The Center Square show.

While some of the advice offered was later reflected in changes made to the bill, other concerns went unaddressed. One key lawmaker on the new income tax advisory group says they intend to tackle those issues.

According to the public records, James Samans with DOR’s Legislative and Policy Division sent feedback to Senate Bill 6346’s sponsor Sen. Jamie Pedersen, D-Seattle, on Jan. 23 expressing concerns over its “complexity and the potential for unforeseen applications of the tax that could give rise to administrative issues and/or legal concerns.”

SB 6346 is currently facing a lawsuit by the Citizen Action Defense Fund alleging it violated the state Constitution's requirement that all property taxes be uniform in nature. Since the 1933 Culliton decision, the State Supreme Court has repeatedly ruled that income is property as defined by the Constitution.

However, SB 6346 imposes a 9.9% tax on annual income of $1 million or more; some tax experts recently warned that due to the state’s capital gains “excise tax” imposed on income, that total percentage might be even higher.

The Center Square reached out to CADF for comment on DOR's feedback but did not receive a response.

The Center Square reported in April that email communications between Pedersen and the State Attorney General’s Office reveal the primary intent of the bill was to overturn Culliton, something the DOR feedback implicitly acknowledge.

“Specifically, we have concerns that the complexity will make it harder to explain the tax in litigation and could give rise to additional challenges beyond overturning Culliton,” the DOR email states.

When The Center Square reached out to DOR for comment on the statement, Communications Manager Mikhail Carpenter wrote in an email that “this sentence is alerting the sponsor that as presently constructed the bill has complexities (identified in the feedback document) that could result in additional legal challenges beyond Culliton. The agency can, and does, provide this type of feedback to lawmakers when it identifies possible technical challenges and/or unintended consequences.”

He added that “the Department of Revenue is statutorily required to provide tax policy guidance to the legislature on proposed legislation that may impact the taxes the agency is responsible for. Feedback is provided in several ways but the most common is a sponsor feedback letter where the agency identifies potential administrative or technical issues. The agency’s role in providing feedback is to ensure that the proposed legislation is administrable, but it is not legally binding and what is incorporated is at the discretion of the Legislature.”

Income tax advisory group member state Rep. Ed Orcutt, R-Kalama, told The Center Square that the complexity of the law as written, combined with DOR’s lack of experience with an income tax, lends itself to a multitude of problems. DOR intends to hire around 300 new employees by 2030 to enforce the tax.

“One (DOR employee) may interpret it differently than another,” Orcutt said. “I’m really concerned not just about the court system, but about the administrative...and everything else. There’s going to be a horrendous opportunity for errors. And I say errors, not evasions. Will the department interpret it the same the CPA is interpreting it?”

text:
IF OIL WAS THE PROBLEM, WHY IS THE 10-YEAR YIELD MAKING NEW HIGHS WHILE CRUDE EASES?

The lunchtime explanation for today's market no longer fits. At 2:05pm ET the 10-year Treasury yield - what Washington pays to borrow for ten years, and the base for mortgage rates - is 5.173%, up 0.059 percentage point from Wednesday's close, after touching 5.181%, its highest since 2007. It got there while US crude oil (November) eased from $95.62 a barrel at 1:45pm to $95.24, still +$3.08 / +3.34% from Wednesday's settlement. Stocks are following the yield, not the barrel: the S&P 500 at 7,688.32, -17.71 / -0.23%; the Nasdaq-100 at 30,340.77, -129.52 / -0.43%; the Dow Jones Industrial Average at 51,282.15, -229.44 / -0.45%.

The afternoon verdict: the Hormuz report bought stocks about 45 minutes. Since the Treasury's 1:00pm bond sale, borrowing costs are back in charge, and the last two hours come down to how much of the midday bounce the bond market lets stocks keep. So far, about a third.

The day has run in three acts. In the morning, stocks followed bonds. The 10-year climbed from 5.087% just after 10:00am to 5.154% by 11:15, and in those same minutes the S&P 500 hit its low, 7,662.57, -0.56%. At 12:14pm Reuters reported that US and Iranian negotiators are discussing a step-by-step deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Crude fell from $96.64 to about $94 within five minutes, the 10-year dropped to 5.127%, and the S&P 500 climbed to 7,719.01, +0.17%, just before 1:00pm.

Then the Treasury sold $44B of 7-year notes at 5.085%, the highest yield at a 7-year sale since 1993. Buyers bid $2.42 for every $1 on offer, vs $2.50 in August, and took the notes only at a yield a little above the 5.078% they traded at just before the sale - a sign they wanted extra pay. The 10-year has climbed almost without a pause since: 5.137% at 1:05pm, 5.158% at 1:45, 5.181% just after 2:00.

Stocks gave ground in step. The S&P 500 has handed back about two-thirds of its Hormuz gain, and the Nasdaq-100 about the same. Technology gave the most. The Technology Select Sector SPDR (XLK) at $193.66, -$1.68 / -0.86% today, was down less than 0.1% at 1:05pm; the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) at $595.26, -$6.15 / -1.02% today, had briefly traded above Wednesday's close. Tech companies are valued on profits years away, and a higher 10-year yield shrinks what those future profits are worth today, so they feel it first.

Three facts point at the bond market itself, not at oil:

- The cleanest test came just after 2:00pm. The 10-year jumped from 5.160% to 5.181% and the S&P 500 fell about 9 points, while crude sat near $95.10, below its 1:45 level.
- The selling is in long-term bonds, not the ones that track the Federal Reserve. The 2-year, which moves with bets on the Fed's next few decisions, is 4.906%, +0.011; the 30-year is 5.468%, +0.066.
- It is American. Britain's 10-year government bond yield is 5.377%, -0.008, and Germany's is 3.600%, -0.011. Washington is selling a lot of debt this week - Wednesday's $70B sale of 5-year notes drew $2.21 of bids per $1, the thinnest since December 2018 - and buyers want more pay to hold it.

The market's winners and losers this afternoon line up with that. SPDR S&P Regional Banking ETF (KRE) at $70.74, +$0.36 / +0.51% today, is up: banks pay depositors rates that follow short-term Treasuries and lend at rates that follow long-term ones, so long yields rising with the 2-year flat helps what they earn on new loans. iShares U.S. Home Construction ETF (ITB) at $88.08, -$0.71 / -0.80% today, is down, because mortgage rates track the 10-year.

The strongest fact against the verdict: stocks are not fully obeying bonds either. At the 11:15 low the 10-year stood at 5.154%. It is higher now, yet the S&P 500 sits about 26 points above that low. Oil is the likeliest reason. Crude has rebuilt only a little over half of its Hormuz drop - $96.64 before the report, $93.37 at the 12:40pm low, $95.24 now - so part of the relief is still in the price. And the VIX, the options market's gauge of expected swings in the S&P 500, is 15.96, +0.78 / +5.14%, well under its long-run average near 19.5. Investors are marking prices down, not running.

What the final two hours turn on, Eastern time:

- 2:30pm: US crude settles - the official end-of-day price for oil futures. Wednesday's was $92.16; today's high is $96.78.
- Before the 4:00pm close: whether the 10-year pushes past 5.181%. A yield that keeps climbing while oil holds still would confirm the pressure on stocks is about borrowing costs, not the war.
- Any time: an on-the-record word on the talks. The Reuters report rests on unnamed sources; the White House and the State Department did not immediately comment.
- Friday, 10:00am: the University of Michigan's final September consumer survey. The early-month reading was 47.8, the weakest since May's record low, with shoppers expecting 4.6% inflation over the next year - the number a bond buyer reads first.
- Wednesday, September 30, 8:30am: August PCE inflation from the Bureau of Economic Analysis, the Fed's preferred price gauge, on the last day of the quarter, when funds rebalancing their holdings can move prices with no news behind them.

What would hand the afternoon back to stocks: the 10-year slipping back under 5.137%, where it sat right after the auction, or either government confirming the talks on the record. What would erase the rest of the Hormuz bounce: the S&P 500 back under this morning's 7,662.57 with the 10-year above 5.181%.

At lunch the market was asking whether Iran will reopen a shipping lane. At 2pm it is asking how much Washington must pay to borrow for ten years, and that question gets a new answer every minute until the close.

text:
When George Washington had a captured British spy in his hands and knew the real traitor was just out of reach, he made a quiet, desperate offer: give me Benedict Arnold, and I will give you back John André. The British said no. And so the wrong man hanged.

Here was the terrible math Washington faced. His men had caught Major André, a likeable, honorable young British officer, and the rules of war left Washington no choice but to hang him as a spy. But André was really just the go-between. The true villain, the American general who had actually sold out his country, was Benedict Arnold, who had escaped clean to the British and was now sitting safe behind their lines, wearing a red coat. It galled everyone. The decent man was going to die while the traitor walked free.

So Washington quietly tried to fix that. He could not openly propose a straight trade, that would have looked like bargaining over a man's life, and André himself, ever the man of honor, would not lend his name to a scheme to have someone else killed in his place. So the message went through unofficial back channels to the British commander in New York, Sir Henry Clinton. The meaning was unmistakable: hand over Arnold, and André lives. Washington would take the traitor and spare the spy.

It was, in cold terms, a completely fair swap, and Clinton was agonized, because he genuinely loved André almost like a son. But he refused. And his reasons, from the British side, were ironclad. Arnold had come over to the British under Clinton's personal protection and assurances. If Clinton now surrendered him to be hanged the moment it became convenient, he would be branding himself a man who betrayed those who trusted him. And beyond honor, there was cold strategy: the British wanted to encourage other Americans to defect. If they handed Arnold to the gallows, they would be sending a message to every potential turncoat that Britain would sell you out the instant you were no longer useful. No defector would ever trust them again.

So Clinton would not make the trade, even to save the young man he adored. He protected the traitor and doomed the spy. On October 2, 1780, John André was hanged, and Benedict Arnold lived on in comfort for decades.

It is one of the great bitter ironies of the Revolution. Washington was willing to let the honorable enemy go and take the guilty American in his place, the exact right outcome by any measure of justice. It was the British who insisted on keeping the traitor and sacrificing the gentleman. Two commanders, both of whom admired André, both trapped by the rules of honor and war, and between them a good man died so that a bad one could go free.

🇺🇸 🇪🇺 🇷🇺 A sharp transatlantic disagreement is emerging over Washington's decision to invite Vladimir Putin to the G20 summit in Miami this December.

Marco Rubio confirmed that the invitation has been formally extended: “We think it's an opportunity for him to engage not just with the president, but with other world leaders. We hope that's an invitation he'll accept.”

Asked about the decision, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas gave a very different response: “It was very hard to hear.”

Kallas pointed to the recent U.S. indictment of alleged Russian intelligence operatives accused, among other offenses, of involvement in a murder-for-hire conspiracy on American soil.

“Do these intelligence officers operate alone or do they get orders from Putin? And I can tell you: they get orders from Putin.”

Kallas went on to question the political normalization that a G20 appearance could offer Putin, while Rubio defended engagement as necessary precisely because Washington needs to negotiate with governments with which it has serious disagreements.

The Kremlin says it is considering the invitation.
