STATE HOUSE PRESS RELEASE

President Tinubu To UN: We Can't Rule 2026 World With 1945 Distribution of Power

** *Warns Africa can't continue to fill UN agenda without permanent membership at Security Council

** *Calls for immediate end to global warfare, respect for UN Charter

** *Demands radical shakeup of global financial system, equitable participation in economic decision-making

** *Says Africa deserves fairness In climate financing, reaffirms commitment to Paris Agreement, fair energy transition

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has renewed calls for a radical shake-up of the United Nations (UN), insisting that reforms must start with reconstituting the Security Council to grant Africa permanent seats.

He warned that the continent can no longer afford to fill the Council's agenda from the margins, pointing out that the world of 2026 cannot remain captive to the distribution of power in 1945.

The Nigerian leader made the position in his address delivered by his deputy, Vice President Kashim Shettima, during the General Debate at the ongoing 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, United States.

Specifically, he demanded at least two permanent seats for the continent—including full rights, responsibilities, and veto power—along with a total of five non-permanent seats.

"The reform of this institution must begin with the reconstitution of the Security Council, for the world of 2026 cannot remain captive to the distribution of power in 1945. Africa cannot continue to fill the Council’s agenda while remaining absent from its permanent membership.

"Nigeria demands, in accordance with the Ezulwini Consensus and the Sirte Declaration, at least two permanent seats for Africa, with all the rights and responsibilities of permanent membership, including the veto for as long as it exists, and five non-permanent seats in total. The authority to speak for humanity carries an obligation to represent it," he stated.

President Tinubu also issued a wake-up call to world leaders, demanding an immediate end to global warfare and a total rejection of the rising tide of nationalism.

With urgent moral clarity, he warned that the global order hangs in the balance, while fiercely rallying the international community to dismantle unilateral aggression, resurrect the foundational principles of the United Nations Charter, and forge an unyielding, unified front through a recommitted era of global multilateralism.

The Nigerian leader categorically told the global leaders not to pretend that distant or domestic conflicts do not exact a price from other nations, underscoring the UN’s urgent duty to restore trust in institutions built to reconcile differences and advance global common interests.

"The persistence of conflict across the world recalls the purpose for which the United Nations was founded: to spare succeeding generations the devastation of war. We must therefore return to the founding principles of dialogue, mutual respect and collective responsibility.

"Nigeria stands by the Charter and its promise of a world in which diplomacy prevails over coercion, cooperation over isolation and international law over the arbitrary exercise of power," he declared.

The President framed Nigeria's peacekeeping efforts in Africa as a model, noting that the nation stands ready to take on greater responsibility and sacrifice to restore peace across the continent—just as it did in Liberia, Sierra Leone, Darfur, Mali, and The Gambia, where it committed personnel and resources when global solidarity demanded action.

"Through ECOWAS, the African Union and our Gulf of Guinea partnerships, we continue to advance mediation, democratic governance, counter-terrorism and maritime security," he said, adding that Nigeria's foreign policy depends on the same conviction that guides its economic reforms.

President Tinubu stated that Nigeria is actioning its sustainable development commitments through disciplined macroeconomic management, robust institutions, private-sector growth, and strategic public investment.

Emphasising that the mission directly links Nigeria's national advancement to Africa's progress and a global duty to foster peace, equity, and prosperity, he observed that internal achievements mean nothing if the nation ignores gathering external threats, declaring that geography offers no exemption from the consequences of a fractured world.

Government trust, according to him, is earned only when decisions improve lives, stressing, however, that since no nation is insulated from global conflicts, leaders must face security and climate realities head-on rather than pretending borders offer safety.

The President urged global action on climate change, rejecting the false choice between development and climate action, even as he emphasized that developing countries must industrialize, eradicate poverty, and expand energy access using low-carbon pathways backed by technology transfer and climate finance.

He reaffirmed Nigeria's commitment to the Paris Agreement and a fair energy transition, stressing that Africa bears a heavy climate burden despite contributing under 4% of global emissions.

Under the Energy Transition Plan, he hinted that the nation is working towards net-zero emissions by 2060 while expanding access to affordable, reliable and sustainable energy.

President Tinubu declared that Nigeria will not let fear dictate its technological future, affirming that AI is a tool driven by human intent, and to harness the tool for human advancement, the nation is aggressively expanding its digital public infrastructure, accelerating broadband deployment, and driving tech entrepreneurship.

He reiterated Nigeria's call for reform of the international financial architecture, wider access to concessional financing and debt sustainability structure that recognise developmental needs, pointing out that "one of the greatest obstacles to sustainable development is inadequate financing," as most developing nations spends a good part of their resources on debt servicing at the expense of education, healthcare and infrastructure.

Drawing lessons from Nigeria’s prolonged struggle against Boko Haram, ISWAP and other armed groups, the President said "no nation, however formidable its defences, can secure itself completely against dangers sustained beyond its borders."

He noted that while modern threats like terrorism and cyberattacks exploit gaps in global action, lasting military victory requires a foundation of education, economic opportunity, accountable governance, and human rights.

As a founding member of ECOWAS, President Tinubu said Nigeria remains ready to uphold regional solidarity and African leadership in resolving security challenges, "reinforced by principled international partnerships."

The Nigerian leader maintained that Nigeria is committed to the peaceful settlement of disputes under the United Nations Charter, as "the conflicts in Sudan and other war-torn countries demand urgent diplomacy to address their humanitarian, economic and geopolitical consequences."

"We should all be afraid of a world in which we can no longer tell the victim from the aggressor. When our investment in propaganda shields perpetrators from justice to the point that telling the truth becomes a crime, the promise of this institution stands betrayed," he stated.

On the expectations from the UN general debate the Nigerian leader noted that "a reformed, inclusive and effective United Nations is indispensable to the peaceful, just and sustainable world that future generations deserve.

"Whatever our differences, we must remember that humanity is our oldest citizenship, and peace is the inheritance we owe every child," he further stated.

text:
Yeah, there’s actually another word for this. It’s called delusions of grandeur. 🤷🏻‍♂️

Most guys are looking for a woman who will bring them peace, love, trust, and good communication.

I’ve dated women of all different shapes and sizes. Women with no job, women with great careers, women society would consider beautiful, and women society might not. But for me, it was never about finding the perfect woman because there is no perfect person out there.

If you can sit across from someone and have a good conversation that lasts more than five minutes, you’re already off to a good start. If the date lasts a few hours and you both have fun, that’s an even better sign. If you meet again, have dinner, see a concert, or just spend time together, you’re building a foundation. Whether it eventually becomes a friendship or a romantic relationship, you’re building the infrastructure for something meaningful.

The majority of men don’t care if you drive an Italian sports car, already own a home, graduated from Yale Business School, and make $375,000 a year. Most men don’t require a woman to have a BBL, augmentations, lashes, extensions, or look like an OF model on Instagram. In fact, from where I’m sitting, that artificial Instagram look seems to be becoming less appealing to a lot of men.

And I understand that women don’t necessarily make all of those changes for men. A lot of it is competition between women themselves. Women can be incredibly competitive with one another, including when it comes to beauty and appearance.

Where I think the real dating problem lies is that a lot of women repeatedly choose toxic men. I’m not saying men don’t choose toxic women because they absolutely do. But there’s this romanticized idea of the mysterious, dark, handsome bad boy. Somewhere underneath that, there can also be this belief that he’ll eventually become a great husband and father once the right woman changes him.

And if women keep waiting for Thor to roll up in a Bugatti like the poster said, they’re probably going to go through a lot of Thors.

Because here’s something worth thinking about. If a guy looks like Thor, has enormous wealth, and can attract virtually any woman he wants, what makes you think he’s automatically going to wake up one morning and say, “You know what? I renounce my entire Playboy lifestyle. I’m deleting the other 30 women in my phone and committing myself exclusively to you because you’re just that amazing.”

Does it happen? Sure. There are exceptions. But you can’t deliberately chase men who openly advertise that they don’t want commitment and then be shocked when they don’t commit.

It becomes, “I can fix him. I’ll be the woman who finally makes him settle down. There are just a few things I need to change about him.”

Stop going after the guy carrying a giant flashing sign that says, “I don’t want to settle down. If you’re lucky, I’ll leave a Snickers bar and my number on the nightstand when I leave at three in the morning. I’ll call you next time I’m in town.”

Then when he behaves exactly the way he told you he would, suddenly it becomes, “All men are pigs,” while thousands of ordinary men who might actually offer the love, loyalty, stability, and companionship you say you want were never even considered.

I think more to the point, people have to examine what they’re actually looking for in a partner. If you’re waiting for a perfectly sculpted Greek god with a mansion, a Bugatti, and a CEO position, ask yourself what happens when those things disappear.

What if Thor gets into an accident and loses his legs? What if he suffers a brain injury and can’t be a hedge fund manager anymore? What if he’s badly burned and his face is no longer Instagram perfect? Does the love disappear with the looks, money, and status?

Because if the goal really is finding a good man, there is no shortage of good men out there. But too much of modern dating has become focused on three things: looks, height, and financial power.

text:
🔸 September 24 - Saint Thekla the Protomartyr 🔸

Today, we commemorate the Holy Protomartyr Saint Thekla. For the zeal with which she evangelized many pagans, she is honoured with the title “Equal to the Apostles.” St Thekla was from the city of Iconium (today Konya, Turkey) and was the daughter of illustrious parents. Distinguished by her beauty, she was betrothed to an eminent youth at age 18. When the blessed Thecla heard the Apostle Paul preaching in Iconium, she came to love Christ with all her heart.

Against her mother’s will, she renounced her marriage to devote her life to preaching the Gospel. Thekla’s fiancé denounced St Paul to the Roman prefect of the city for turning his bride against him, and he was imprisoned. But Thekla continued to visit him in prison where she was nourished by his teachings. At his trial, St Paul was banished from Iconium. Thekla was again urged to consent to her marriage, but she refused. Her enraged mother even persuaded the judge to sentence her to be burned alive. 

Beholding a vision of Christ as she entered the flames, Thekla remained unharmed, and the torturers fled in fear. She left to seek out St Paul and his companions, and eventually found them hiding in a cave near the city. She went with them to spread the Gospel in Antioch. Here, she was pursued by a local pagan ruler named Alexander who was captivated by her beauty. For refusing his marital offer, she was condemned to death for being a Christian.

They set wild animals upon her, but they would not harm the holy virgin, and instead lay meekly at her feet. The torturers then had St Thekla tied to be dragged by two fearsome bulls, but the chords broke and the bulls ran off. Terrified that the Saint was being preserved by a divine power, the ruler gave orders to set her free.

With the blessing of the Apostle Paul, St Thekla then settled in Seleucia (today Silifke, Turkey) where she preached the Word of God to the pagans and healed the sick by her prayers. At age 90, envious pagan sorcerers came to defile St Thekla, but as she prayed to Christ, and large rock split open and concealed her. In this very cave, St Thekla delivered her soul to the Lord.

Happy Feast of Our Lady of Mercy! Prior to Vatican II, her title was Our Lady of Ransom. 

In 1218, on the feast of St. Peter in Chains, Our Lady is said to have separately appeared to three people to ask them to found a religious order. She asked St. Peter Nolasco, St. Raymond of Peñafort, and King Jaume I of Aragón to ransom slaves.

On August 10, 1218, The Royal, Celestial and Military Order of Our Lady of Mercy and the Redemption of Captives was founded by the three who met at the high altar of Barcelona. They were asked to make a fourth vow to offer themselves in exchange for the slave when the ransom could not be paid.

Those needing to be ransomed were Byzantine and European Christians from 649 onward when Muslims raided Cyprus and Sicily, and attacked Constantinople. The raids drastically increased as a succession of North African Muslims invaded Spain, beginning in 711. These white slaves were highly valued and sold in Muslim markets throughout the Middle East. The slavers stole people as far away as Iceland. North African corsairs raided European coasts for men, women, and children. Muslims enslaved non-Muslims.

In the Black Sea area, millions were enslaved by the Ottomans ~1500-1800. From about 650-1900, 18 million sub-Saharan Africans were taken for Muslim markets. Most of the men were castrated, some by having the penis removed. Although most died, the roundups were still lucrative.

Ohio State historian Robert Davis estimated that 1–1.25 million Western Europeans were enslaved between  ~1500 and 1800. However, hundreds of thousands were taken before that time.

The enslavers are still with us. Slavery continues. Our Lady of Mercy, pray for us.

text:
Before being drafted by the Atlanta Falcons, Michael Penix Jr. wrote a letter to NFL GMs: “I’m a product of Dade City, FL. Population 7,600. No Trader Joe’s, no Whole Foods. No steak houses or country clubs. No personal QB coach, no strength coach, no state-of-the-art training equipment. Nothing about Dade City is luxurious, but that‘s the way we like it. It’s a town full of pride, and a lot of our pride comes from football. We swap out summer camps for tackle football on concrete in the 95-degree heat. You find out quick if you’re built for this game or not.

I’m thankful that I grew up in that environment. The reason I’m on your draft board today is because of it. Adversity wasn’t just a buzzword in Dade City, it was in the water. Nothing is handed to you, you have to earn everything. If you fall — you get up. Simply put.

To think injuries are the only adversity I’ve faced in college would be shortchanging my story. I faced adversity before I even got to college. Two weeks before signing day I was told by the team I was committed to for two years that I no longer had a scholarship. They didn’t think I was good enough to play in the SEC. I decided to go to Indiana because Nick Sheridan was the QB coach, and he believed in me from the time he offered me at Tennessee to when he took his position at Indiana. IU had 10 straight losing seasons when I got to Bloomington, one winning season since 1994. I knew what I was walking into, but I felt I could help turn the program around. In 2020 we became the 7th-ranked team in the country, the highest ranking the program has had since 1967....

Finally Coach DeBoer called. I remembered the success we had when he was my offensive coordinator in 2019…. Now he had just gotten the Washington job, his first shot at a big-time program. He saw something in me that the rest of the college football world didn’t. It was not a popular move. First time Power 5 head coach and the first thing he does is get a QB transfer who wasn’t thought of as a top 100 player in the portal. And so I wasn’t promised anything. Not a starting job, no NIL deal, no special treatment. Nothing was going to be handed to me. I was going to have to earn everything. Good. That’s what I was accustomed to.” https://t.co/YLlQwsfn3E

text:
Washington State 

Washington Accelerator for Residential Production Program 

WA State Dept. of Commerce 

Eight local governments will upgrade their systems

Sept. 24, 2026

WA Dept. of Commerce awards $475,000 to help eight local governments speed up housing permits  

Grants fund new permitting software, digital applications and AI tools that catch incomplete applications  
 
OLYMPIA, Wash. – The Department of Commerce today announced $475,000 for eight local governments to speed up the review of residential building permits. The grants pay for new permitting software, digital application systems and AI tools that check whether an application is complete before it's submitted.  

Demand far exceeded the resources available. Commerce received 60 applications requesting $3.7 million total and was able to fund eight awards.  

"We urgently need more housing, and we need to make it easier to build,” said Commerce Interim Director Sarah Clifthorne. “These grants will help communities speed up permitting review and help get more homes built."

Grant recipients  

Pierce County – $70,000  

Snohomish County Health Department – $70,000  

City of Tacoma – $70,000  

City of Bellevue – $70,000  

City of Lacey – $70,000  

City of Ridgefield – $70,000  

City of Tumwater – $35,000  

City of Yakima – $20,000  

A common bottleneck  

Permit delays are a known bottleneck in housing production. Incomplete applications, repeated rounds of corrections and outdated software can add weeks or months to the process.  

"Right now, one in four residential permit applications arrives incomplete, our inspection scheduling still runs on voicemail, and critical permit records are scattered across paper files and multiple systems," said Vanessa Dolbee, Lacey's director of community and economic development. "This grant could mean fewer resubmittals, shorter wait times and a much clearer path from application to permit." 

The eight grants announced today target those steps directly.  

Lacey and Tumwater will move to modern digital permitting platforms that let applicants apply, track and pay for permits online.  

"This support transforms our permitting process into an engine for local growth, moving builders from application to construction with predictability and speed," said Matt Ames, IT project manager for the City of Tumwater.

Bellevue will launch applicant-facing tools that review uploaded documents and flag missing or inconsistent information before an application is submitted.  

"This grant will support the City of Bellevue's implementation of AI tools that will help permit applicants get the right information early in the process and submit fully prepared applications, reducing delays and enabling a faster, more predictable permitting experience," said Jake Hesselgesser, Bellevue's acting director for development services.  

Other awardees will audit local development regulations, upgrade or replace aging permitting software, and assess where their permit reviews slow down. The Snohomish County Health Department, which reviews septic systems for new homes outside sewer service areas, will automate the transfer of application data from the county planning department so reviews can start sooner.  

Part of a broader push for housing  
Washington needs to add more than 1 million homes by 2044 to keep pace with expected population growth, according to Commerce projections. These grants are part of Commerce's broader work to speed up housing production. Commerce awarded similar grants in 2024.  

Through the Washington Accelerator for Residential Production, Commerce is bringing together practitioners and experts to recommend state actions that reduce costs and shorten timelines for new housing. Commerce is also developing guidance to help local governments offer permit-ready plans, pre-approved home designs that can move through permitting faster.  

For more info,  visit the Local Project Review webpage.

text:
🚨Researchers have created a targeted nanotherapy that has shown rapid effectiveness against endometriosis in early trials. 

A single dose of this therapy successfully reduced both endometriosis symptoms and overall disease progression in preclinical trials.

Published in the journal Advanced Healthcare Materials, the study details a novel treatment that uses nanoparticles to deliver a commonly available drug, niclosamide, directly to disease-specific immune cells.

 In mouse models, just one dose of the treatment reduced both endometriosis symptoms and overall disease progression, offering a major breakthrough for a chronic condition previously considered incurable. By delivering the drug directly to the lesion sites, the nanocarrier overcomes the low solubility of the medication, minimizing the risk of adverse effects.

Endometriosis is a debilitating condition affecting approximately 10% of women globally, characterized by painful uterine-like tissue growing outside the uterus, which can lead to severe pain, chronic fatigue, and infertility. 

Current options are largely restricted to surgeries that offer temporary relief or hormonal therapies that carry harsh side effects such as bone density loss and premature menopause. 

This new nanotechnology-driven approach represents a paradigm shift toward non-hormonal, highly precise management of the disease. While human clinical trials are still on the horizon, this milestone offers promising hope for millions of women seeking long-term relief without compromising their reproductive health.

source: Washington State University. (2026). WSU team develops potential treatment for endometriosis. Advanced Healthcare Materials.

The reality is, we will all see in the near future. 

Here is something I wrote about China, and no matter which side of Trump you stand, it will give you an idea of what they've been up to and what we, as Americans, need to prevent. 

"Would it bother you if China aggressively expanded its Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) into Africa, South America, and Central America?     

Under the program, Beijing offers massive infrastructure projects, but in practice it often relies on bribes, inflated contracts, and unrealistic promises. This traps countries in crushing, unsustainable debt, effectively giving China economic control and ownership over key assets and strategic resources. In many cases, these nations become economically enslaved by debts that can never realistically be repaid, while a small elite at the top lives lavishly.    

And what about China’s push to replace the petrodollar with the petroyuan? They’re working with Iran, Russia, Venezuela, and 30+ other countries (many in BRICS) to make that happen.  

If successful, the United States would face serious negative economic and geopolitical consequences.   America currently benefits enormously from the dollar’s status as the world’s primary reserve currency. Replacing the petrodollar system with a yuan-based one would sharply weaken the dollar. That would drive high inflation, push interest rates much higher, cause imported goods prices to spike, undermine U.S. Treasuries, and erode dollar dominance overall.

Everyday American life would become noticeably more expensive and difficult. In that scenario, China could increasingly dictate terms to the U.S., and if Washington resisted, Beijing could weaponize economic pressure or sanctions to impose huge burdens, further trying to undermine the dollar. How does 200% inflation sound to you...lol    

This has been China’s long-term strategy for over 30 years, and it explains why the Trump administration is taking strong action with Iran, Venezuela, Panama, Cuba, and even exploring opportunities in Greenland to disrupt and stop it all.  China was roughly a decade away from achieving the scenario described above.   Now they’re not. The United States has reasserted control over critical global energy flows and routes, firmly keeping the dollar as the world’s de facto reserve currency."

text:
Since Yolanda passed, hundreds of you have reached out to tell me what your faith teaches about seeing your spouse again. I’ve read every message. All 1,321 of them! I had no idea how differently religions answer the question that now keeps me awake at night.

Many Christians believe they will recognize and be reunited with loved ones in heaven, though Jesus says people will not marry in the resurrection. 

Latter-day Saints (Mormons) believe a marriage sealed in the temple can endure for eternity. Some Jewish teachings speak of souls finding one another again in the World to Come. Islam offers hope that faithful spouses will be together in Paradise. Hindu and Buddhist traditions often speak of rebirth, though they differ widely on what continues after death and whether two people meet again. 

I’m grateful to everyone who has shared a belief, a prayer, or a story with me. I’m still trying to understand it all. But underneath every question about heaven and eternity is the simplest wish of my life:

I want to see my Yolanda again. That’s non-negotiable. I lead my entire life with that belief. I want to hear her laugh, hold her hand, and tell her I love her. And if there is a life beyond this one, I hope with everything in me that we find each other there. And if not, then Lord, we need to have a serious talk. ♥️

text:
Ever since I came to know of ISKCON Bahrain, Thursday evenings have often taken me there.

Interestingly, the place was first shown to me by Narayan, our office security guard. One of the few remaining Hindus from Noakhali. Nearly thirty years with our company. And almost every time I see him, there is a japa mala in his hand.

I had written about Narayan sometime back. His story is here: https://t.co/8Ia20zgP3w

Thakur would say, never go to a temple or see a sadhu empty-handed. Carry something, however small. A fruit. A few flowers. Whatever you can.

Not because Bhagavan needs it. It is we who need to learn the habit of offering before asking to receive.

So my routine at ISKCON is simple.
I carry a fresh coconut, richly dabbed with turmeric, and offer it to Janardhan. Then sit quietly for a while. Chant. Have the bhog. Return.

The bhog too is simple. And always delicious.

Radhashtami has just passed. Today, instead of charanamrita, I received a tulsi leaf.

Look around and you see Hindus from every walk of life. Far from home. Each carrying his own load - work, family, money, life.

For a few blessed hours, all that stays outside.

Naam kirtan. Hari Naam. And somewhere in between, you forget whatever was weighing on you.

Sri Hari never disappoints.

And there is one thing about this place I have learnt.
Try leaving without prasad.
You can't. 🙂

A sevayet will call you back. A devotee will spot you. Somehow, somebody will make sure you have eaten.

Tried and tested.

Perhaps Sri Hari has a simple rule for anyone who comes to His abode:
You don't leave unfed.

#ISKCON #HareKrishna #HariNaam #SanatanaDharma #Bhakti #Prasad #Bahrain #RadhaKrishna

Newark, New Jersey.

Dale Alfrey attended an estate sale and noticed four ordinary-looking boxes filled with old papers.

Nobody seemed particularly interested in them.

Neither was Dale.

But for $25, he decided to take a chance.

He had no idea he’d just bought something that would consume the next 20 years of his life.

The boxes reportedly came from the estate of Michael P. Bornes, a Manhattan bookseller.

When Dale began looking through them, he found page after page of technical notes, experiments and strange observations.

Some of it sounded so bizarre that Dale initially assumed he’d purchased the unfinished writings of a science-fiction author.

So he put the boxes in his basement…

and forgot about them.

Nearly two decades passed.

When Dale finally opened them again, he discovered that moisture had taken its toll.

The papers were deteriorating.

Ink was fading.

Some pages were covered with mildew.

Realizing the material might soon be lost forever, Dale began transcribing everything he could still read.

And that’s when he finally understood whose papers he believed he’d bought.

Nikola Tesla.

Tesla had died alone in a New York hotel in 1943.

After his death, government officials took possession of trunks and packages containing his technical papers because some of his work potentially had military significance.

But not everything Tesla owned was necessarily accounted for.

According to later accounts, belongings he’d left behind at various hotels had previously been sold to satisfy unpaid bills.

Dale became convinced that four boxes had somehow survived…

and ended up with him.

But it was what he claimed to find inside that made the story truly strange.

According to Dale’s account, Tesla had written about experiments conducted in Colorado Springs in 1899.

While monitoring unusual electrical signals, Tesla reportedly became convinced some of them weren’t random.

They appeared structured.

Intelligent.

And possibly…

not from Earth.

Dale spent years studying and transcribing the material.

By 1997, he had reportedly begun transferring it onto computer disks.

He also started making inquiries online, hoping someone might help fill gaps in the journals.

Then three men appeared at his house.

Dale said they wore dark suits.

One addressed him by his first name.

And somehow…

they knew about the boxes.

The spokesman offered to buy them.

Dale refused.

The conversation reportedly became threatening.

The man told him the papers didn’t belong to him and warned that people had disappeared over less.

Then the three men simply left.

Dale rushed outside.

No car.

No men.

Nobody on the street.

He returned to his study.

The four boxes were gone.

So were his computer disks.

His collection of Tesla books and articles had disappeared as well.

And according to Dale…

his computer’s hard drive had been erased.

He never recovered the papers.

And that creates the problem at the heart of this story.

There’s no independently authenticated collection available today that proves those documents belonged to Nikola Tesla.

Maybe they never did.

Maybe Dale misunderstood what he’d purchased.

Maybe the entire story grew in the telling.

But if his account was true, then four boxes of Tesla’s missing papers survived unnoticed for decades…

were purchased for just $25…

sat forgotten in a basement for another 20 years…

and disappeared shortly after their owner began telling people what he’d found.

Which leaves one uncomfortable question.

If those papers were worthless…

why would anyone have wanted them back?

text:
The tweet is partisan rhetoric, not a factual brief. Several of its core characterizations are false or inverted. Others are speculative opinions dressed as certainty. Here is a claim-by-claim breakdown with primary and contemporaneous sources.

Claim: Libertarians (“Losertarians”) “have exposed themselves for the globalists they truly are.”This is the opposite of the record. Thomas Massie and the libertarian current he represents are among the most consistent non-interventionists in Congress. Massie voted against aid packages for Ukraine and Israel, against additional Iron Dome funding, against resolutions supporting Ukraine’s sovereignty after the 2022 invasion, and against the 2026 Iran military campaign. He offered amendments to zero out regular U.S. assistance to Israel and argued American taxpayers should not fund foreign military adventures.

The Libertarian Party platform states: “American foreign policy should emphasize peace with all nations, entangling alliances with none. We would end the current U.S. government policies of foreign intervention including military and economic aid; tariffs; economic sanctions; and regime change.” It also rejects the U.S. acting as “policeman for the world.” That is the opposite of the usual meaning of “globalist” (support for overseas commitments, alliances, and aid)

Claim: “these fools openly promote full-blown communists taking the reins in Congress.”:
No evidence supports this. Libertarian doctrine is explicitly anti-socialist and anti-communist. The LP platform rejects government redistribution of wealth, control of trade, and forcible collection of the fruits of labor; it treats the free market as “the only [economic system] compatible with the protection of individual rights.”

Massie is a fiscal conservative who repeatedly voted against large spending bills. In September 2026 a prominent libertarian investor, Scott Banister (early PayPal/Uber/SpaceX backer), committed $40 million specifically to oppose DSA-aligned candidates in state races. That is the opposite of promotion.

DSA-backed House candidates who advanced in 2026 primaries did so almost entirely in deep-blue districts. They replace other Democrats; they do not decide control of the House. Calling liberty-oriented Republicans or third-party voters “promoters of communists” is a standard two-party smear, not a description of their platforms or spending.

Claim: They think they are “positioning Massie for 2028 by destroying anything Trump has done.”:
Partly observable, partly exaggeration. After Massie lost the May 19, 2026 Kentucky GOP primary (Ed Gallrein 54.9%, Massie 45.1%), his concession-speech crowd chanted “2028!” and “President!” Massie did not shut it down and later filed paperwork that left a 2028 run open. He also continued criticizing specific Trump policies he viewed as unconstitutional or fiscally reckless: the Iran strikes, the large domestic spending/tax package, and delays around the Epstein files. Those disagreements existed before the primary and were the stated reasons Trump targeted him. Whether they “destroy anything Trump has done” is an opinion, not a documented strategy of self-sabotage.

Claim: “All they’re actually doing is handing it all over to the DSA, which we’ll never vote our way out of.”:
This is a prediction, not a fact. Midterm and presidential elections continue after 2026. DSA influence inside the Democratic Party is real and growing in some urban primaries, but the claim that alienated liberty voters have already made a DSA-controlled Congress irreversible is hyperbole. Safe-district DSA nominees do not flip the House; competitive districts do. The tweet treats any refusal to rubber-stamp the current GOP majority as equivalent to installing “full-blown communists.” That is the same binary the attached video repeats with on-screen text: “Trump and a GOP majority are the only shield we have.”

Context of the quoted tweet and the video:
The quoted post from @tummler_af simply notes that some MAGA voices celebrated Massie’s ouster and dismissed his supporters, then later asked those same people for votes. That observation matches the public record of the most expensive House primary in history, Trump’s explicit recruitment of a challenger, and large outside spending (including from pro-Israel groups) against Massie. The reply video frames the choice as GOP majority versus the activist clip shown at the start. That is persuasion, not documentation.

The original tweet uses slurs, inverted labels (“globalists”), and an all-or-nothing threat. Those are classic propaganda techniques. They do not become true because turnout math can sometimes punish a party that purges its own fiscal and anti-war wing. Massie’s actual voting record, the Libertarian platform, and documented libertarian spending against DSA candidates are the primary sources that contradict the central accusations.

text:
While the voice behind hits like “Life of Sin” and “Living the Dream,” Sturgill Simpson was once a teenager with no idea what the future looked like. At the time, he wasn’t aware that he would eventually build a career in country music. All Simpson wanted to do was get far away from his home. Ready to experience all the world had to offer, the singer did it on the government’s dime when he joined the United States Navy. And according to Simpson, he would have died for his country. 

Sitting down for an interview that included a quick round of 20 questions, Simpson was asked what led to him wanting to join the military. Thinking on the question, he returned to his life as a teenager. “When I joined the Navy, my understanding was that I have to get the f*** out of this town, any way I can. I didn’t have any money. I knew I wasn’t going to college.” 

Coming from the small town of Versailles, Kentucky, Simpson found himself working at the Combat Information Center. He also traveled to Japan. The singer might have used the military to get away from home, but he insisted he was more than willing to pay the ultimate price. “I love my country, man. I was a wild kid, and I might not have been the most squared-away sailor. But if it came down to it, I would have absolutely died on a ship in the middle of the ocean for the United States of America. I am a patriot.”

KALIBRATE: THE REAL REASON FUEL PRICES ARE SO HIGH

The company you are referring to is Kalibrate (officially registered as Knowledge Support Systems Inc.). While the company is globally headquartered in Manchester, United Kingdom (with US corporate offices in Michigan and New Jersey), it became a household name across California due to a massive federal antitrust lawsuit filed in the state.

Kalibrate provides AI-powered fuel pricing and location analytics software, including a widely used mobile app that allows fuel retailers and dealers to manage and deploy gas prices directly from their phones.

Key Overview of Kalibrate:

The Software & Mobile App: Kalibrate acts as an AI-driven pricing ecosystem. Fuel dealers input their private store data, volumes, and local competitor metrics. The AI then analyzes historical patterns, traffic volume, and market demand to recommend optimal, profit-maximizing fuel prices.

Widespread Adoption: The platform is utilized by nearly all major US fuel brands and big-box retailers. Its clients and defendants in recent litigation include 7-Eleven, Circle K, BP, Marathon Petroleum, Speedway, Walmart, Albertsons, and TravelCenters.

The California Antitrust Controversy:

Kalibrate dominated national headlines due to class-action litigation filed in the Eastern District of California.

The Accusation: The lawsuit alleges that Kalibrate operates as the "central nervous system" for an illegal, algorithmic price-fixing scheme. Instead of stations competing naturally to offer lower prices, the AI allegedly coordinates high pump prices across competing brands simultaneously.

The Impact: According to the legal complaints, in areas where US fuel dealers heavily adopted the Kalibrate app, gas prices artificially increased by up to 30 cents per gallon compared to what normal market competition would dictate.

Legal Precedent: This case serves as a critical test for California's updated antitrust laws, which explicitly restrict competitors from using shared algorithms to artificially drive up the cost of living.

text:
"Social Darwinism adapted Charles Darwin’s evolutionary theory to justify social and economic inequality, arguing that wealth and power naturally accrue to the “fittest” individuals. Proponents such as Herbert Spencer and William Graham Sumner claimed that social welfare and regulation interfered with natural progress by supporting the “unfit.” 

Academic and media endorsement of these ideas helped naturalize extreme inequalities in wealth and status, even as modern science has discredited their biological basis and ethical legitimacy.

Ayn Rand’s Objectivism and Milton Friedman’s Chicago School economics offered new rationales for deservedness, focusing on individual merit and market efficiency. 

Rand argued that capitalism was the only moral system because it rewarded individual achievement and rational self-interest, while Friedman stressed the practical prosperity generated by free markets. 

Both opposed government intervention, championing minimal social welfare and the primacy of economic liberty. Their ideas were spread through universities, think tanks, publishing, and media, reshaping public policy and economic thought in the late 20th century.

In the 21st century, figures like Peter Thiel and Curtis Yarvin have advanced a new technocratic elitism, arguing that society should be governed by the most capable “builders“ rather than by democratic consensus. 

They endorse post-democratic, corporate-style governance, often framing redistribution and social welfare as impediments to advancement and effectiveness. These ideas spread through alternative publishing, podcasts, and new academic ventures, bolstering the belief that only a select few deserve to shape society’s future.

Higher education played a central institutional role in legitimizing, institutionalizing, and transmitting both 19th-century Social Darwinism and 20th-century market-libertarian economics. 

Rather than existing merely as abstract ideas, these intellectual frameworks relied on elite universities to establish scientific prestige, train influential thinkers, and build institutional pipelines into public policy and popular culture."

text:
She heard her daughters beg for their lives — through the telephone.

On May 2, 2001, nine-year-old Faith Battaglia and her six-year-old sister, Liberty, went to spend the evening with their father, John Battaglia, in Dallas. Their mother, Mary Jean Pearle, expected them home later that night.

Mary Jean and John were divorced after years of conflict. She had reported him for assault. A protective order barred him from threatening her and from possessing firearms. In 2001, a warrant was issued after he violated that order.

That night, Faith called her mother. John put the call on speaker and told Faith to ask why her mother wanted him to go to jail. Mary Jean tried to explain.

Then Faith’s voice changed.

“No, Daddy. Please don’t. Don’t do it.”

Gunshots followed. Mary Jean screamed for the girls to run. The call ended. She dialed 911 and raced toward the apartment.

It was too late. Police found Faith, 9, and Liberty, 6, inside.

John was arrested hours later at a tattoo shop. He later had two roses tattooed on his arms — one for each daughter.

At his 2002 trial, prosecutors said he killed the girls to punish their mother. The jury convicted him of capital murder and sentenced him to death. After years of appeals and a competency review, he was executed on February 1, 2018.

His last words were directed at Mary Jean. He offered no apology to Faith. No apology to Liberty.

The last word should not belong to him.

It belongs to two little girls who should have had their whole lives ahead of them.

Faith. Liberty.

Remember them for the fact that they lived. 🌹🌹

text:
Don’t Buy an Irrigation Controller for Convenience. Buy It for Your Landscape.

If you live in a drought-prone part of the U.S., a standard timer-based sprinkler controller is often the reason your water bill stays high and your plants still look stressed. Experts estimate that as much as 50 percent of outdoor water use is wasted through overwatering.

The right controller is not the one with the flashiest app or the biggest brand name. It is the one that matches your restrictions, soil, climate, sun exposure, and zones.

Start with the rules that actually apply to you
Local watering restrictions vary by city, utility, drought stage, and even street address. Some allow watering only on odd or even days. Others ban midday irrigation or limit days per week during drought. A good controller must let you program those windows and stay inside them. WaterSense-labeled weather-based and soil-moisture controllers are required to accommodate these restrictions.

Many utilities in California, Arizona, Nevada, Texas, and Colorado also offer rebates for WaterSense-certified units. Check yours before you buy.

Match the controller to the ground, not the catalog
Soil type changes everything. Sandy soil drains fast, so it usually needs shorter, more frequent cycles. Clay holds water but infiltrates slowly; longer, less frequent watering plus cycle-and-soak settings prevent runoff. Loam sits in the middle. Enter the correct soil type when you set up a smart controller so it calculates run times instead of guessing.

Climate and sun exposure create microclimates in the same yard. A south-facing slope in full sun loses water faster than a shaded north side. Group plants with similar needs into the same zone and let the controller treat each zone independently. That is why the number of zones on the controller should match (or slightly exceed) the number of distinct areas you actually have.

Weather-based and soil-moisture features do the daily work
Two proven technologies exist:

Weather-based irrigation controllers (WBICs) use local evapotranspiration (ET) data—how much water plants and soil actually lose—to adjust schedules automatically. They skip watering before rain, after rain, or when it is cool.
Soil moisture sensors measure what is already in the ground and override a scheduled cycle when the soil is still wet enough.

Both types can carry the EPA WaterSense label when independently certified. Replacing a basic clock timer with a labeled controller can save an average home thousands of gallons a year—figures commonly cited in the 7,600–15,000 gallon range depending on the study and prior watering habits.

Look for extra water-saving tools: a water-budget or “percent adjust” slider so you can instantly cut every zone by 20 percent during a drought stage, rain-delay or rain-sensor input, freeze skip, and notifications if the weather signal or sensor fails.

For a detailed comparison of current models built for drought-prone U.S. regions, including weather-based scheduling and zone features, see this roundup: https://t.co/jyJNLB4D16

Landscape first, brand second
A controller that cannot handle your restrictions, soil, or number of zones will waste water no matter how smart the marketing sounds. Program it correctly, group plants by need, and keep the system maintained. Smart technology only multiplies good setup; it cannot fix a poorly designed yard or ignored local rules.

If you are replacing an old timer this season, start with the WaterSense product list and your utility’s rebate page. Then walk your yard and note the actual differences in sun, slope, and plant type. That walk will tell you more than any spec sheet.

text:
AI replies to questions on Blockchains
No, a blockchain will not become too long to process, even for standard modern computers, let alone quantum facilities. This is because computers do not need to process the entire history of a blockchain from scratch to validate new transactions.
Here is why blockchain length is not a limiting factor:
1. The State vs. History Distinction
Nodes (the computers running the network) don't constantly reread the entire blockchain. Instead, they maintain a database of the current "state" of the network.
In      Bitcoin, this is the UTXO set (Unspent Transaction Outputs)—a list      of who currently owns what coins.
To      validate a new transaction, a node only checks this relatively small,      up-to-date list to ensure the sender has the funds. It does not need to      look back at transactions from ten years ago.
2. Pruning and Light Nodes
Not every participant in a blockchain network needs to store the entire history.
Pruned      Nodes:     Full nodes can delete (prune) old historical blocks once they have been      processed and verified, keeping only the most recent blocks and the      current state.
Light      Clients: Mobile wallets and casual users only download      block headers (a tiny fraction of the data) and rely on      cryptographic proofs to verify transactions.
3. Data Storage Scales Faster Than Chain Growth
Blockchains are intentionally designed with strict limits on how fast they can grow (e.g., Bitcoin's block size limit and 10-minute block times). The physical size of the Bitcoin blockchain grows by only a few tens of gigabytes per year. Hard drive storage capacity and data transfer speeds generally grow at a much faster rate, meaning storing the history actually becomes cheaper over time.
4. Quantum Capabilities are Overkill
Quantum computers excel at specific types of complex mathematical problems (like factoring large numbers or breaking traditional cryptography). They do not offer an advantage for storing raw data or sequential processing of simple ledger balances. Standard data management techniques—like indexing and sharding—are what keep blockchains efficient, and they work perfectly fine on standard silicon chips.
Would you like to explore how quantum computing actually threatens blockchain (such as breaking cryptographic keys), or are you interested in how developers scale blockchains (like sharding and layer-2 networks) to handle millions of users?
------------------------------------------------------------

Unlike traditional fiat banking systems where fraudulent transfers or physical robberies can leave investigators at a dead end, blockchain technology provides a permanent, immutable ledger that fundamentally changes how financial crimes are tracked and resolved. While blockchain transactions are irreversible, they leave a permanent digital trail that makes it incredibly difficult for criminals to actually use or cash out stolen funds.
Here is how the architecture of decentralized systems alters the dynamics of financial fraud and recovery:
🔎 Absolute Traceability vs. Banking Secrecy
In the fiat world, stolen money often disappears into a web of shell companies, offshore accounts, and corrupt jurisdictions protected by banking secrecy laws.
On a public blockchain (like Bitcoin or Ethereum), every single transaction is publicly visible.

The      Ledger Never Forgets: Once a robbery or exploit occurs, the      hacker's wallet address is instantly known.
Public      Tracking: Security firms, law enforcement, and everyday      users can trace the exact flow of the stolen funds in real time as they      move from wallet to wallet.
No      Expiry Date: Because the blockchain cannot be altered,      investigators can wait years for a criminal to make a mistake, as the      evidence never degrades.

🛑 The "Cashing Out" Bottleneck
While a thief can easily transfer stolen crypto between anonymous addresses, turning that crypto into spendable fiat currency (like USD or EUR) is exceptionally difficult.

Blacklisting:     Centralised stablecoin issuers (like Tether or Circle) and major      cryptocurrency exchanges frequently freeze stolen assets the moment they      touch an account linked to a known exploit.
KYC/AML      Barriers: To convert crypto to fiat, criminals must      eventually use an exchange that enforces Know Your Customer (KYC)     and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) regulations, which immediately      flags their identity.

⚖️ Real-World Resolution Successes
Because of this transparency, global law enforcement has successfully recovered billions in stolen cryptocurrency—achieving results that are nearly impossible in traditional fiat paper-trail or cash robberies.
Notable examples include the U.S. Department of Justice seizing billions of dollars worth of Bitcoin linked to the historic Bitfinex Hack and the Silk Road marketplace years after the crimes took place.
⚠️ The Remaining Vulnerabilities
Despite superior traceability, blockchain systems introduce unique risks that fiat systems do not have:

No      Reverse Button: In a fiat system, a bank can reverse a      fraudulent wire transfer or credit card charge. On a blockchain, if a user      falls for a phishing scam or types the wrong address, the transaction cannot      be undone by any central authority.
Smart      Contract Exploits: Code is law. If a decentralized application      has a flaw in its code, hackers can exploit it to drain funds legally      permitted by the contract architecture.
Crypto      Mixers:     Criminals use privacy tools (mixers) to obfuscation transaction histories,      though law enforcement has increasingly gotten better at cracking or      sanctioning these protocols.

Would you like to look closer at how blockchain security analysts unmask anonymous wallets, or are you interested in a specific historic case study of a major crypto heist and recovery?

AI is built initially from the prompts of many human brains to the point where AI is far more knowledgeable than any one human and I believe that AI will be hugely beneficial to mankind. However, even AI and AGI are still learners, albeit it very fast learners, which means even AI and AGI still have the same problem as humans in that they cannot in all honesty say they know it all. For instance, based on what yu have said, if someone stole crypto and immediately exchanged it for fiat money in one of the many offshore banks, then no amount of tracking on the XRP ledger will recover that stolen value, because it will be less traceable in the current fiat systems.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
You have accurately highlighted the exact pivot point where technology meets human jurisdiction: the "off-ramp" to the fiat world.
If a criminal steals cryptocurrency and successfully manages to swap it into fiat currency inside a non-cooperative offshore bank, the tracking on that specific blockchain ledger cannot directly force the bank to hand the money back.
This scenario perfectly illustrates the tension between AI/blockchain capabilities and the reality of human systems, broken down into two distinct dynamics:
1. The Legal "Brick Wall" of Fiat Systems
Once value crosses the bridge from digital assets into traditional cash, the rules change entirely:
· Loss of Ledger Control: A blockchain ledger like the XRP Ledger can only govern data written on its own network. It has zero authority over a database owned by a private bank in an offshore tax haven. [1]
· The Sovereign Shield: If a bank operates in a jurisdiction that refuses to comply with international subpoenas or mutual legal assistance treaties (MLATs), the trail effectively hits a political brick wall. As you noted, the uncertainty remains because technology cannot override human geopolitics.
2. The Blockchain's Revenge: The Permanent Trap
Even if the criminal successfully deposits fiat into an offshore account, the blockchain trail doesn't disappear; it morphs into a permanent legal trap. This is where specialized blockchain intelligence tools alter the long-term outcome:
· Bridges Can Be Burned: To get that crypto into an offshore bank, the thief usually has to route it through an entry point—often a cryptocurrency exchange or a digital gateway. If investigators act quickly enough, features on modern protocols allow for intervention before the exit. For instance, while the native cryptocurrency XRP cannot be frozen or clawed back due to its decentralized nature, other issued tokens and stablecoins on the XRP Ledger (like Ripple's dollar-pegged stablecoin, RLUSD) explicitly utilize built-in "Clawback" and "Deep Freeze" features precisely to reverse fraudulent activity or comply with regulations before assets can escape. [1, 2, 3, 4]
· The "Marked Bills" Effect: If the thief uses a standard bridge to convert crypto to fiat, the remaining crypto wallets they used are permanently flagged globally. Any remaining funds in those digital wallets become toxic; they can never be moved to a major regulated exchange or spent openly without triggering immediate alarms. [1, 2]
· The Long Game:Because the ledger is a permanent historical record, law enforcement agencies often wait. Criminals eventually try to move money out of offshore havens, or the offshore jurisdictions themselves change their laws under international pressure years down the road. The permanent digital footprint means the thief must look over their shoulder indefinitely. [1]
Ultimately, your observation captures the core reality of AI, AGI, and modern tech: knowing everything about the data does not equal having control over the real world. AGI might eventually optimize how we predict or track fraud, but as long as fragmented human laws and rogue banking systems exist, technology will always have to stop at the border of human free will and political sovereignty.

🚨 10 Things That Happened in the Stock Market Today (and why every investor needs to pay attention): 🧵👇

1️⃣ The 10-Year Treasury Yield Shockwave
The 10-Year yield spiked past 5.10%, reaching levels not seen in nearly two decades. When risk-free yields hit 5%+, equity risk premiums shrink fast, putting immediate valuation pressure on long-duration mega-cap growth stocks.  

2️⃣ Oil Crosses the $100 Psychological Barrier
Brent Crude futures surged 3.9% to cross $103/barrel amid escalating Middle East geopolitical friction. Energy costs spiking this late in the economic cycle directly translates into headline CPI inflation spikes, keeping pressure on transport and consumer discretionary names.  

3️⃣ Fed Expectations Flip to Rate Hike
A hawkish tone from Fed Governor Barr combined with sticky inflation pushed 30-day Fed Funds futures to price in a ~66% chance of a rate hike in the upcoming FOMC meeting. The "rate cut narrative" was temporarily shelved, forcing a swift market repricing.

4️⃣ S&P 500 Pulls Back From All-Time Highs
After touching fresh records, the S&P 500 pulled back ~0.8% to 7,706, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropped 1.1%. Broad-market pullbacks on high-yield days show macro drivers dominating micro fundamentals right now.  

5️⃣ Mega-Cap Big Tech Divergence
Meta ($META) gained relative strength (+1.0%) on continued optimism around its AI tools, while Google ($GOOGL -3.8%) and Amazon ($AMZN -2.0%) saw selling pressure. The days of all Magnificent 7 stocks moving in lockstep are fading—stock selection matters more than ever.

6️⃣ Utilities & Discretionary Take the Hardest Hit
Utilities ($XLU -1.9%) and Consumer Discretionary ($XLY -1.5%) were the bottom-performing S&P sectors. High yields make dividend-paying utilities less attractive as bond proxies, while higher oil prices act as an immediate tax on retail consumer spending power.  

7️⃣ The Fear Gauge Spikes
The CBOE Volatility Index ($VIX) climbed nearly 7% up to 15.8. While still below panic thresholds, the sudden uptick reflects institutional investors buying downside put protection as geopolitical uncertainty mounts.  

8️⃣ Breadth Favors the Bears (1.9-to-1)
Decliners outpaced advancers by almost 2-to-1 across the benchmark S&P 500. Total consolidated exchange volume spiked above 17 billion shares, signaling broad institutional participation on the sell-side rather than low-volume summer drift.  

9️⃣ Small-Caps Feel the Liquidity Pinch
Rising short-term yields (2-Year Treasury near 4.95%) hit small-caps and heavily indebted balance sheets hardest. Companies needing to refinance debt over the next 12–18 months face significantly higher interest expense hurdles.  

🔟 The Key Takeaway for Long-Term Investors
Short-term macro noise is driven by bond yields, geopolitics, and Fed speculation. But yield spikes like this historically offer strategic entry points for disciplined dollar-cost averagers who stick to quality balance sheets and index fundamentals. Don't trade the headlines—focus on the long-term compounding cycle.

text:
Jarin Stevenson breaks down his NEW role for @UNC_Basketball - 9.24.26
🏀 Versatile “Swiss Army knife” role: Jarin Stevenson said Coach Michael Malone envisions him playing and defending positions one through five, serving as a defensive stopper while also spacing the floor, hitting 3-pointers and creating opportunities for teammates.
🧭 Growing into leadership: Entering his senior season, Stevenson sees himself taking on greater responsibility with a roster featuring younger and less-experienced players. He is helping freshmen and newcomers adjust to college life, basketball expectations and “the Carolina way.”
💪 Last season built confidence: Stevenson said his expanded role after Caleb Wilson’s injury in Miami gave him confidence that he could defend multiple positions, create problems defensively and contribute at a high level when given additional responsibility.
🛡️ Defense remains a priority: Although Carolina plans to play faster under Malone, Stevenson stressed that defense is receiving considerable attention. Practices emphasize defensive principles, rotations, communication and trusting teammates to be in the correct positions.
🗣️ A reserved personality presents a leadership challenge: Stevenson described himself as naturally shy and reserved. He is working to become more vocal and communicate better while recognizing that leadership can also come through demonstrating the right habits rather than constantly talking.
🔥 Malone wants more aggression: Stevenson said Malone’s fiery approach can push him to play harder and become more aggressive. Stevenson is learning to find an emotional edge during games and practices without abandoning his natural personality.
🏃 Practices combine teaching and competition: Stevenson praised Malone’s practice structure, which mixes live competition with teaching segments. Different coaches handle offensive and defensive instruction, while the staff tracks practice wins to encourage competition.
🏆 Competition helps bring out Stevenson’s intensity: Stevenson said keeping track of practice victories gives him additional motivation. When his team starts poorly or falls behind, he has increasingly tried to show a more fiery side and energize teammates.
🎯 Matt Able brings shooting: Stevenson enjoys having Able as a teammate after previously facing him as an opponent. He described Able as a strong catch-and-shoot threat who can also create opportunities within the offense.
🧱 Sion James provides interior energy: Among the new frontcourt players, Stevenson highlighted Sion as an effective rim protector who runs the floor, attacks the offensive glass and plays with a “relentless motor.”
🎯 Simo adds another perimeter threat: Stevenson described Simo as a knockdown shooter who is consistently ready to catch and shoot, makes good passes and generally “plays the right way.”
⚡ Terrence offers scoring versatility: Stevenson praised Terrence’s ability to attack the basket, score from mid-range and finish creatively around defenders.
👀 Nia creates opportunities with size: Stevenson described Nia as essentially a 6-foot-9 point guard whose size allows him to see over defenses, attract defenders and generate open catch-and-shoot opportunities for teammates.
🤝 Chemistry has Stevenson excited: Stevenson repeatedly expressed enthusiasm about his teammates, saying the roster contains players with different strengths who appear to mesh well together. He said thinking about what they could accomplish this season makes him excited.
🏠 Returning home has been personally meaningful: After spending two years at Alabama, Stevenson said being back near his family and community has had a major impact. He specifically mentioned returning to Seaforth, reconnecting with students and teachers and spending more time with relatives, including his grandmother.
🌎 Time away provided perspective: Stevenson believes leaving home for Alabama helped him better appreciate his family and community. Now he is learning to balance family time with time for himself, something he said has improved his life.
🔑 Trust is a central theme: Stevenson said Malone repeatedly emphasizes players trusting one another—trusting teammates to rotate correctly, communicate and provide defensive support.
📈 Stevenson’s next step is broader than statistics: His comments suggest his senior-season challenge will involve combining versatility and defense with greater aggression, communication and leadership as Carolina incorporates numerous new players and adopts Malone’s faster, defense-conscious system.
